author: sg
body:
## Problem

The radio's contact table (~350 slots) doesn't age out old contacts. Once full, the firmware just emits `CONTACTS_FULL` and drops the new node's advert — so new contacts never replace stale ones, and the bot logs `CONTACTS_FULL` indefinitely. The bot's sqlite `contacts` table holds 500 and acts as the long-term archive; the radio is the working set.

## Solution

When enabled, the bot evicts the **stalest contacts from the radio** to keep `radio_evict_headroom` free slots:
- **at startup**, after device-info/contacts sync;
- **automatically on `CONTACTS_FULL`** (debounced);
- **on-demand** from the web UI **Manage → Radio** page.

Eviction operates on a fresh `get_contacts(lastmod=0)` dump (the DB archive may hold contacts no longer on the radio, so it can't choose victims) and **never deletes DB rows** — the archive is preserved. Victims are stalest-first by a fused key: bot-DB `last_synced_at` → radio `lastmod` → a plausible `last_advert` (garbage sender-clock timestamps are treated as oldest). **Protected:** configured owners, all bot users, anyone the bot DM'd in the last 24h, and any contact types in `radio_evict_protect_types`. Removal is capped per run and aborts after 3 consecutive radio errors; the meshcore lib's in-memory contact cache is kept in step so `send_dm` won't reference an evicted entry.

## Config (`[bot]`)

| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `radio_evict_enabled` | `true` | auto triggers (startup + CONTACTS_FULL) |
| `radio_evict_headroom` | `8` | keep ≥ N free slots |
| `radio_evict_protect_types` | _(none)_ | contact types never evicted (names/ints) |
| `radio_evict_max_per_run` | `50` | safety cap per run |
| `radio_evict_min_interval` | `120` | seconds debounce for auto runs |

Manual eviction works even when disabled; the switch only governs the automatic triggers. Web policy changes are **runtime-only** — `mcbot.conf` is the startup source of truth.

## Web UI / API

- `GET /api/radio/contacts-status`, `POST /api/radio/evict-contacts`, `POST /api/radio/contacts-policy` (auth required).
- Radio tab "Contact table" card: used/max/free + protected/evictable counts, a read-only firmware autoadd-byte diagnostic, an auto-evict toggle + headroom input, and an "Evict now" button that previews victims (dry-run) before confirming. Rebuilt static assets included.

## Notes

- The firmware-native `set_autoadd_config` is **not** exposed — its flag byte is undocumented (firmware source/web research were unavailable). Only a read-only `autoadd_raw` diagnostic is surfaced; the setter can be added later once the semantics are verified.
- "No headroom reached" is reported as a `shortfall` (e.g. when protections exceed capacity), never an error.

## Testing

`tests/test_radio_eviction.py` (run with a deps-equipped Python) — victim selection ordering/protection/garbage-timestamp handling, dry-run, headroom math, per-run cap, 3-error abort, shortfall, **DB-archive preservation**, and the disabled-policy handler gate. All pass; existing `tests/test_repeat_tracking.py` still passes; `web-ui` builds clean.

author: einlanzerous
body:
Closes CTFG-39.

## Problem

While ingesting the Economics Explained issue *"How Would Healthcare Change If Everyone Had To Pay A \$1 Copayment?"*, the full 729-word article was captured (`body_text` = 5,865 chars) and summarized correctly — but the story's **`snippet`** came back as the email's **preheader/teaser** (the inbox preview line), which newsletters embed hidden at the top, duplicated and padded with zero-width spacer chars. The prompt defined `snippet` as *"a short excerpt or the lead sentence"* and had no substance test for what counts as a `story`, so a headline-with-teaser could surface as a tweet-length "story".

## Change (`internal/ai/prompt.go`)

- Tighten **`story` vs `blurb`**: a story must develop across multiple sentences/paragraphs; a single sentence / headline / headline-with-teaser is a `blurb` (or `ad`/`promo`).
- Tell the model to **never treat the preheader/teaser as content or snippet**; `snippet` is the lead sentence of the item's *actual body*.
- Bump `PromptVersion` → `2026-06-10.1`.
- Add `internal/ai/testdata/fixtures/economics_explained_jun_09_2026.html` (the real issue) as an eval fixture.

## Validation — `make score-fixtures` (gemma4:31b)

- **Target case fixed:** the healthcare story's snippet is now `"Economists have a word for what happens when you don't pay for something yourself: moral hazard."` (the article's real opening) instead of the teaser. Short video/IPO teasers now classify as `blurb`, not `story`.
- **No regression** on `example_digest` (stories + blurbs split correctly), `example_essay` (1 story), or `letters_from_an_american` (2 stories).
- `morning_brew_jun_07` (the largest fixture, 14 KB) hit `ai: response is neither array nor object: unexpected EOF` — this is the **pre-existing, size-correlated model-output truncation tracked in CTFG-33** (also seen in prod on IT Brew), **not** caused by this change: `letters_from_an_american` failed once then passed on retry, and the prompt edit only adds ~10 lines of instruction. Out of scope here.

## Follow-ups (noted in CTFG-39)

- **CTFG-36** — per-segment story *content* (the actual "read the full story in the Reader" gap; this PR only fixes classification + snippet selection).
- Sanitizer strip of the hidden preheader/preview-text span + zero-width padding in `internal/ingest` (relates CTFG-19/CTFG-37), so the duplicated teaser never reaches the model.

author: nosliwsirhc
body:
## What

Public pages are server-rendered on demand in the Worker and read their copy from D1. Cloudflare does **not** cache Worker-generated responses by default, so before this every visit re-ran the render + a D1 query, and the hashed `/_astro/*` bundles were served `max-age=0, must-revalidate`.

- **`src/middleware.ts`** — caches `200 text/html` GET responses in the data-centre Cache API (`caches.default`), the documented pattern for no-origin Workers. Repeat hits serve from the edge with no D1 read (`s-maxage=60`).
- **`public/_headers`** — `/_astro/*` (content-hashed → immutable) cached a year instead of revalidating each load.
- **`src/lib/cache.ts`** + publish handlers — flush the edge cache on publish/delete.

## Admin is never cached

- `/admin` and `/api` → `private, no-store`.
- **Any request carrying the `sh_admin` cookie bypasses the cache** → editors always see live/draft content.
- **`?preview=1` requests bypass the cache** → fixes a draft-leak: the preview URL renders the unpublished draft, which must never be stored or served to the public.
- Only `200 text/html` with no `Set-Cookie` is stored; redirects/404s/`/media` are not.

## Flush on publish

`flushPublicPages()` runs when a page/article is published (and when an article is deleted):
- **Per-data-centre** `caches.default.delete()` always (no credentials needed; instant in the editor's region).
- **Global purge-by-URL** via the Cloudflare API when `CF_PURGE_TOKEN` + `CF_ZONE_ID` Worker secrets are set. Without them, global staleness is bounded by the 60s TTL (and editors already see changes immediately via the cookie bypass).

## Note

SSR was already in place — all content pages are `prerender = false` with content read from D1 server-side (no client-side data fetching). This PR only adds the caching layer + its safety/flush.

dev-021(`976e416`)이 flushSave에 추가한 `setActiveWorkspace`가 **매 자동저장마다 새 객체 참조**를 만들고, fetchGraph effect가 **객체 자체를 의존성**으로 갖고 있어 자기 파괴 루프가 형성:

author: enzo-adami
body:
### What

Two opt-out guards for the per-turn tool guardrail controller
(`agent/tool_guardrails.py`), both born from real incidents running a
long-lived local agent on a small model:

**1. Repeated-mutation halt.** The existing `idempotent_no_progress` guard
only watches read-only tools, and the failure counters only advance when a
call *fails*. A mutating tool that keeps **succeeding** on the exact same
call is invisible to all current guards — we observed a model issue the
identical `write_file` 38 times in a single turn. The new check counts
identical successful mutating calls per signature (tool + full args, content
included — so legitimate iterative edits never match, since different
content means a different signature). It reuses the existing
`no_progress_warn_after` / `no_progress_block_after` thresholds: warn, then
halt (`repeated_mutation_halt`). Gated behind `hard_stop_enabled` like the
other halts, and reset per turn.

**2. Destructive-overwrite guard.** Blocks a `write_file` that would replace
a non-empty file (≥ `safe_write_min_bytes`, default 200) with content
smaller than `safe_write_shrink_ratio` (default 0.5) of its current size.
Motivation: the model accidentally blanked a status file and a full research
report by overwriting them with empty scaffold content. Design points:

- **Data-loss prevention, not loop detection** — independent of
  `hard_stop_enabled`, controlled by its own `safe_write_enabled` flag
  (default on).
- **Blocks the call, never halts the turn** — the model recovers in place by
  writing the full intended content.
- **Intent override** — re-issuing the *identical* call once confirms a
  genuine shrink/replace, which then proceeds.

### Config

New keys under `tool_loop_guardrails`, all with safe defaults:
`safe_write_enabled` (true), `safe_write_min_bytes` (200),
`safe_write_shrink_ratio` (0.5, validated to (0, 1]).

### Tests

`tests/run_agent/test_mutation_and_safe_write_guards.py` (9 tests): warn →
halt progression, no false positive on iterative edits with changing
content, per-turn reset, `hard_stop_enabled` gating, shrink block + identical
re-issue override, small/new/growing files allowed, independence from
`hard_stop_enabled`, flag off. Existing guardrail suite passes unchanged
(9/9).

### Field experience

Both guards have been running patched into a production-like local install
since 2026-06-08/09: the mutation halt has caught real config-edit loops,
and the overwrite guard stopped further accidental file blanking with no
false positives on normal edit traffic at the 0.5 ratio (real accidental
blankings kept ~22% of the original size; a 0.2 ratio would have missed
them).

author: ppxd
body:
## Summary

When ≥2 `agent.code` (or `flow.subworkflow`) nodes suspend in one parallel wave, each parks on its own durable wait keyed by its run id. Two bugs made parallel fan-out **silently wrong** (the headline finding of the cognitive-architecture audit):

- **Dispatch:** `DispatchPendingAgentRunAsync` / `DispatchPendingSubworkflowChildAsync` took only `FirstOrDefault` of the pending waits → K-1 of K staged runs were never enqueued (stranded until the reconciler's stale-window sweep).
- **Resume (silent corruption):** the completion notifiers called the run-level `ResumeAsync`, which resolves **every** pending wait for the run and stamps the **same** payload on all of them → the first completer's result was fed to every parallel node; the other runs' real results were discarded.

The fix is one generic mechanism: **`IWorkflowResumeService.ResumeOnWaitCompletionAsync`** — resolve **only** the completing wait, **unconditionally** (a finished run's result must be consumed even if a sibling completion is mid-flight; a plain `onlyWaitId` scope alone still loses it on the run-flip CAS race), then re-dispatch only once **no pending waits remain** (so K parallel waits each resolve with their own payload and the run advances exactly once, after the last completes). Both notifiers resolve their own wait via this method; both dispatch methods enqueue **every** pending wait. **Single-wait runs behave exactly as before (non-breaking).**

## Test plan

- [x] `ParallelAgentResumeFlowTests` (real engine + AgentRunService + notifier): dispatch-all (both enqueued), dispatch-on-last (run stays Suspended after one completes; sibling wait untouched), **no cross-contamination** (each node maps its own result), idempotent double-notify.
- [x] `SubworkflowFlowTests.Two_parallel_subworkflow_children_…`: the same guarantees for the subworkflow path; existing single-child cases still pass (non-breaking).
- [x] Full suites — unit **1190**, integration **640** (+3), zero regressions.

## Summary

**Database service layer (`db.py`)**
- Async SQLAlchemy Core engine with WAL mode (`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`) for concurrent bot + web access
- Full CRUD: `create_item`, `list_items`, `update_item`, `delete_item` — all scoped by `user_id`
- `read_at` timestamp set on mark-read, cleared on mark-unread; duplicate URLs allowed (by design)

**FastAPI application factory (`main.py`)**
- `create_app(database_url)` factory enables per-test database injection
- Async lifespan context: DB init on startup, `engine.dispose()` on shutdown (in `try/finally` — runs even if startup fails)
- Bot startup stubbed via `try/except ImportError` — app boots cleanly until `bot.py` lands in Issue #5

**HTTP Basic Auth middleware**
- `BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD` / `BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` env vars; no-op when unset (local dev)
- `hmac.compare_digest` for timing-safe credential comparison
- `/telegram/webhook` exempt via exact path equality — Telegram secret token validation in Issue #4

**Router stubs**
- `routers/items.py` and `routers/webhook.py` mount cleanly; full routes in Issue #4

**Test suite — 24 tests, all passing**
- `test_db.py` (16): create, list with status filter, update read state, delete, WAL mode, user isolation, sort order, duplicates
- `test_main.py` (8): startup smoke, idempotent init, auth middleware (all branches), webhook bypass, directory creation

Closes #1, #2, #3

## Test Coverage

~90% of shipped logic covered. 3 minor gaps noted for future issues:
- `list_items` with unrecognised status string (handled at API layer in Issue #4)
- Malformed Base64 auth header path in middleware
- Trivial `get_current_user()` stub

Tests: 0 → 24 (+24 new)

## Pre-Landing Review

Ran `/review` — status CLEAN. 5 issues auto-fixed:
- `import base64` moved to module level
- `hmac.compare_digest` for timing-safe password comparison (was `!=`)
- Lifespan wrapped in `try/finally` for `engine.dispose()` on startup failure
- Unused `Depends`/`StaticFiles`/`Jinja2Templates` imports removed
- Unused `client` fixture param removed from test signature

## Adversarial Review

Claude adversarial subagent ran as part of `/review`. All critical findings addressed (timing oracle, resource leak). Webhook exemption without secret token validation is intentional — Issue #4 adds `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` validation.

## Plan Completion

| Issue | Status |
|-------|--------|
| #1 — db.py shared service layer | ✅ DONE |
| #2 — FastAPI factory + async startup | ✅ DONE |
| #3 — Basic Auth middleware | ✅ DONE |
| #4–#9 | Intentionally deferred |

## Documentation

README.md created — setup instructions, env vars, API table, DB schema, test summary.

## Next

Issue #4: REST API endpoints (`POST /items`, `GET /items`, `PATCH /items/{id}`, `DELETE /items/{id}`, `POST /telegram/webhook`)

author: gatekipa
body:
## Summary

The approved EN/FR `villageclaq_welcome` Meta template had dispatcher/registry support but no real producer — existing welcome sends are email/SMS fire-and-forget. This PR adds the smallest safe server-side, queue-backed WhatsApp welcome producer so the template can be included in manual QA.

**Recipient is the joining/accepted/claimed member only** — never other group members or admins.

## What's included

- **`src/lib/welcome-producer.ts`** — mirrors the payment-receipt producer. Queues at most one `notifications_queue` row (`channel: whatsapp`, `template: welcome`, `whatsappType: welcome`) per membership with variables ordered `{{1}} memberName`, `{{2}} groupName`. The existing queue drain cron dispatches it and records the provider message ID; the WhatsApp webhook correlates delivery status — no behavior change needed there.
- **`POST /api/members/welcome-notifications`** — Bearer-authenticated; only the joining member (or platform staff) may trigger production for a membership.
- **Triggers (client fire-and-forget via `src/lib/notify-welcome.ts`)**:
  - invitation acceptance (`accept_invitation`) — skipped on `already_member`
  - proxy claim via invitation (`claim_proxy_membership`)
  - proxy claim via token link (`claim_membership_with_token`)
  - join-code success (`join_group_via_code`) in both the public join page and the join dialog — `pending_approval` never triggers
- **Not covered (by design)**: admin add-member always creates unclaimed proxies (`user_id NULL`) — they never joined themselves, so no unsolicited MARKETING-category message is sent. Join-code approval-activation is a documented follow-up.

## Preferences / eligibility

- `getEnabledChannels(supabase, userId, "new_member", groupId)` gates the send; WhatsApp disabled → skip, no queue row.
- ⚠️ The default `new_member` matrix has WhatsApp **OFF** (`notification-prefs.ts`), preserved as-is per product decision. QA must enable the `new_member` WhatsApp preference on the test account.
- Missing phone → skip; phone failing `formatPhoneForWhatsApp` → skip. EN/FR selection unchanged (`fr` only when locale is exactly `fr`; producer prefers caller locale, falls back to `preferred_locale`).
- Logs only masked phones (`maskPhoneNumber`) and shortened UUIDs.

## Idempotency

Strict exactly-once per membership: check-before-insert on `notifications_queue` (any existing welcome row for the membership blocks re-enqueue, including failed rows), `23505` treated as duplicate, backed by **migration `00088`** (partial unique index on `data->>'membershipId'` where `channel='whatsapp' AND template='welcome'`). **The migration file is added but NOT applied** — run it manually in the Supabase SQL Editor before live QA, per repo convention.

## Tests / verification

- `npm run test:welcome-producer` — 12/12 pass (exactly one queue row, variable order, `new_member` gating, whatsapp-disabled skip, missing/invalid phone skip, proxy skip, pending_approval skip, duplicate block, FR locale, masked-phone logging, trigger/route source checks)
- `npm run test:payment-receipt-producer` — 9/9 pass
- `npm run test:whatsapp-webhook` — 6/6 pass
- `npm run audit:whatsapp` — pass, including 6 new welcome-producer readiness checks
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean; `npx eslint <touched files>` — no new findings (1 pre-existing error + warnings on base unchanged)
- `npm run build` — succeeds; `git diff --check` — clean; changed-file secret/phone scan — clean

**No WhatsApp/email/SMS messages were sent at any point. No production data was mutated. No Meta templates/config changed. No deploy.**

The tier selector let buyers pick general ($8) while preventa ($6) was
still available, which makes no sense — nobody should opt into paying
more. The tier is now derived, never chosen:

author: atshelchin
body:
## What changed?
Remove the Bluetooth (BLE) transport from the protocol and every implementation — WalletPair is now relay-only (WebSocket relay is the single transport).
- **SDK** (major 2.0.0, changeset included): delete `src/ble/` + the `./ble` export; `relay` is now required in `PairingParams`/`buildPairingUri`/`parsePairingUri`; `DAppSession.createPairing` requires a relay transport exposing `url` (now declared on the `Transport` interface); remove the BLE-only `onBeforeTransportConnect` wagmi option.
- **Protocol docs**: delete §18 Bluetooth Binding (renumber §19 Security→§18), drop transport-independent framing, rename the "Transport Adapter" role to "Relay" (wire id `"_adapter"` kept), relay param required; same treatment in the rationale, security-audit-brief, and root readme; fix cross-refs broken by renumbering.
- **Website (walletpair.org)**: remove the ws/ble transport toggle, dynamic `walletpair-sdk/ble` imports, BLE wallet hints, BLE e2e tests, and BLE docs/landing copy.
- **Examples**: webapp pages drop `WebBleCentralTransport`/`onBeforeTransportConnect`; RN wallet deletes the `ble-peripheral` native module + BLE libs and strips the BLE branch from `index.tsx` (the existing WebSocket relay path is preserved → still a working relay-only wallet), removes Bluetooth permissions/dep and the stale Podfile pod ref.
- **Consumers**: bump `walletpair-sdk` to `^2.0.0` in the extension and walletpair.org.

## Why?
BLE carried a large maintenance burden (native iOS/Android peripheral modules, framing, Web Bluetooth) and gave users a redundant second choice. Standardizing on one best default — the WebSocket relay — simplifies the protocol, SDK, and apps.

## Human owner
@atshelchin

## AI assistance
- [x] AI-assisted (Tool/model: Claude Code / Opus 4.8 — all code/doc edits + multi-agent self-review)

## Risk level
- [x] High

SDK pairing-flow-adjacent changes (relay-required pairing URI + `transport.url` precondition) are High per the WalletPair-specific rule. **No cryptography touched** — ECDH, key derivation, sealing, sequence numbers, and the handshake state machine are unchanged; the edits are confined to the pairing-URI string layer and one transport precondition. Everything else (deletions, docs, examples, dep ranges) is Low.

## Tests / verification
- SDK: `tsc` exit 0 · biome (changed source files clean) · vitest **711/711** · build ✓
- RN wallet: `tsc` clean on changed files
- walletpair.org: svelte-check clean for changed files (one pre-existing lucide icon-type quirk, unrelated)
- Pre-existing eslint/prettier debt in walletpair.org/webapp confirmed against `main` baseline — not introduced here
- Not run: browser/native E2E, native builds, `expo lint` (environment-limited)

## Reviewer focus
- `walletpair-sdk/src/crypto.ts` `parsePairingUri`/`buildPairingUri` (relay required) and `dapp-session.ts:179` `transport.url` precondition
- `walletpair-protocol-v1.md` §18 deletion + §19→§18 renumber
- RN wallet `index.tsx` relay-only flow

## Rollback plan
- Whole change: `git checkout main` (main untouched)
- Per-commit: `git revert afebc11` (review fixes) / `git revert db797fd` (main removal)

## Summary
- add a reusable deterministic helper that downsamples grouped fingerprints to the smallest non-empty family
- balance family data by default for `train` and `build-templates`
- expose `--balance/--no-balance` and `--balance-seed` CLI options
- report original and selected sample counts during training/template builds

## Why
Uneven family counts can bias classifier training and family-template calibration. Using the same deterministic seed lets both workflows select the same balanced family-level dataset without deleting raw fingerprints.

## Tests
- `python -m pytest tests/training_data/test_training_data.py`
- `python -m pytest`

Result: 43 passed, 3 existing `datetime.utcnow()` deprecation warnings.

## Notes
- generated `model/*.joblib` artifacts are intentionally excluded
- model-version templates are intentionally unchanged because family-level balancing does not apply to that workflow

## Summary

- Adds GET /api/settings/company and PUT /api/settings/company route handlers using the requireAuthScope + getWorkspaceIdForUser pattern established in UNI-2107 (PR #199)
- Adds src/lib/settings/company-store.ts -- per-workspace in-memory settings store (name, slug, trading_name, abn, acn); the workspaceId key is always resolved from the authenticated user DB record, never from the request body
- Extends CompanySettings and UpdateCompanyRequest API types to include trading_name, abn, and acn
- Wires the company settings frontend to send all four fields on save and reload state from the API response (previously only name was sent, and the backend endpoint was missing)

## Auth shape (canonical - mirrors UNI-2107 POS routes)

GET  /api/settings/company
PUT  /api/settings/company   { name, trading_name?, abn?, acn? }

401  Not authenticated        (no valid JWT)
403  No workspace found       (user has no workspace row)
400  name is required         (empty/missing name on PUT)
200  CompanySettings object

## Test evidence

- src/lib/settings/__tests__/company-settings-route.test.ts (12 tests) 17ms PASSED
- src/lib/pos/__tests__/pos-route-auth.test.ts (19 tests) 19ms PASSED
- Total: 31 tests passed

Tests cover:
- GET returns default seeded name
- PUT saves name and fields, GET returns saved values (save persists and reload)
- Unauthenticated GET and PUT return 401
- Authenticated user with no workspace GET and PUT return 403
- Cross-workspace isolation: workspace B cannot read workspace A settings
- PUT by workspace B does not overwrite workspace A settings
- Spoofed workspaceId in request body is ignored (route uses DB-resolved value)
- Empty/missing name returns 400

author: ryankiley
body:
In Safari, clicking copy or reset shifted the icon by ~1px. Root cause: WebKit promotes an element to its own compositing layer when a transform/filter animation **starts** and demotes it when it **ends** — and at a fractional button position (a dragged floating panel, flex subpixels) the demotion re-rasterises snapped to different device pixels. The copy swap transitions `scale` + `filter: blur(2px) ↔ none` and the reset spin is a transform animation, so every click ran a promote→demote cycle. Chrome keeps such layers warm, which is why it never showed there.

Fix — keep the layers standing so there's nothing to re-snap:
- `will-change: transform` on `.tw-toolbar-btn` (the `:active` press scale) and the reset svg (hover wind-up + spin); `will-change: transform, filter` on the stacked swap icons. Three tiny 14–24px elements per panel — negligible memory.
- The swap icons rest at `filter: blur(0)` instead of `none`, so the filter context is never created/destroyed mid-cross-fade (the other promote/demote edge in WebKit).

No visual change at rest or in the animations (verified resting geometry and the cross-fade round-trip in the preview). For eyeball proof in Safari itself there's a local side-by-side harness (`dist/safari-test.html`, untracked): legacy vs fixed at a fractional offset, zoomed 4×, auto-cycling both animations.

`dist/` not regenerated, per convention — rebuild on merge.

author: felipewilliam2
body:
## Contexto

Revisão LGPD das páginas legais (Termos de Uso, Política de Privacidade, Exclusão de Dados) identificou um bug de layout, inconsistências entre a Política e as ferramentas realmente usadas pelo site, um prazo regulatório incorreto e cláusulas incompatíveis com o CDC. Esta PR aplica as correções em dois commits: ajustes técnicos/objetivos e ajustes de redação jurídica (aprovados pelo responsável).

## Mudanças

### 🐛 Header/Footer duplicados
`/termos-de-uso` e `/politica-privacidade` renderizavam `<Header />` e `<Footer />` próprios **dentro** do `MainSiteShell`, que já os renderiza — resultando em dois headers e dois footers. As páginas agora retornam só o conteúdo, como `/exclusao-de-dados` já fazia.

### 📋 Política de Privacidade alinhada à realidade técnica
- **Seção 6.1:** remove Substack (descontinuado), adiciona **Mautic** e o processamento do assistente de IA (**Google Gemini**) na entrada do Google LLC. CRM: Salesforce (HubSpot descontinuado).
- **Seções 3–5:** documenta o chatbot — nova categoria "Dados de Planejamento de Viagem" (destino, datas, orçamento, mensagens), coleta via assistente virtual e finalidade 5.6 com base legal do Art. 7º, V (procedimentos preliminares a contrato).
- **Seção 9 reescrita:** bases legais por categoria de cookie (analíticos = legítimo interesse; marketing = consentimento), gestão pelo link "Gerenciar cookies" do rodapé e nova Seção 9.4 com o **direito de oposição ao analytics** (Art. 18, § 2º) — o banner prometia essa informação na Política e ela não existia.

### ⚖️ Correções legais na Política
- **11.2:** prazo de comunicação de incidente à ANPD: `72 horas` (regra do GDPR) → **3 dias úteis** (Resolução CD/ANPD nº 15/2024).
- **1.2/6.2:** GDPR passa de declaração de "conformidade" para referência de boas práticas (evita obrigação voluntária auditável não aplicável).
- **3.5 (nova):** dados de crianças e adolescentes no grupo de viajantes (Art. 14, LGPD).
- **8.2:** remove prorrogação de prazo inexistente na LGPD; cita corretamente o Art. 19, II.

### ⚖️ Termos de Uso adequados ao CDC
- **4.3:** exoneração total de responsabilidade (nula — CDC arts. 25 e 51, I) substituída por cláusula com ressalva expressa dos direitos do consumidor.
- **5.3:** documenta os dois modos reais de atuação — venda direta (emissão e recebimento do cliente) e intermediação (pagamento direto ao fornecedor via link) — remetendo a responsabilidade ao CDC e à Lei Geral do Turismo (Lei nº 11.771/2008).
- **6.2:** adiciona a base legal de procedimentos preliminares a contrato (Art. 7º, V).
- **12.3:** foro de São Paulo com ressalva do foro do domicílio do consumidor (CDC art. 101, I).

### 🍪 Banner de cookies e HubSpot
- Texto do banner agora é genérico ("cookies de marketing para comunicações personalizadas") — a LGPD não exige nomear ferramentas no banner, e o texto citava HubSpot, que não é mais usado.
- `index.html`: removido o loader do HubSpot (`js.hs-scripts.com`) e todo o bloco de detecção de intenção de contato que existia só para acioná-lo (~60 linhas). O script continuava dropando cookies de uma ferramenta descontinuada.

### 🗑️ Exclusão de Dados
Tabela de escopo: HubSpot CRM → **Salesforce CRM**; adicionada linha do Mautic (contatos e histórico de marketing).

## Testes

- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm test:regression` — 617 testes ✅ (teste do `loadHubspot` substituído por guarda que impede o retorno do script)
- Playwright: `cookie-consent.spec.ts` + `seo_metadata.spec.ts` — 34 testes ✅ (banner, gating do Mautic, revogação, canonicals)

## Notas de revisão

- As novas redações jurídicas foram aprovadas pelo responsável, mas **recomenda-se validação por assessoria jurídica antes do merge** (em especial a cláusula 5.3 dos Termos, que reflete o modelo de atuação híbrido).

## Fora do escopo (follow-ups)

- Backend ainda tem HubSpot (`api/hubspot-webhook.ts`, `services/hubspot`, vars `HUBSPOT_*`) e o CLAUDE.md descreve o fluxo antigo de leads — limpeza separada após confirmar a migração completa para Salesforce.

author: ayobamiu
body:
## Problem
`jobs.processing_config` was corrupted by a double-encoding bug, in **two shapes** from the same root cause (a JSON *string* value treated as if it were an object):

1. **String scalar** (36 rows) — stored as a JSON string scalar inside the jsonb column (`JSON.stringify` applied twice). On read-back it decodes to a JS string, so `processing_config.extraction?.method` / `.processing?.method` are `undefined` and callers silently fall back to defaults (`paddleocr` / `gpt-4o`) instead of the job's intended config (e.g. `extendai` / `gpt-4.1`).
2. **Char-indexed object** (3 rows) — an object polluted with numeric char-index keys (`{"0":"{","1":"\"",…}`) plus the real `extraction`/`processing` keys overlaid.

## Root cause (write path)
- **Shape 1:** the multipart upload endpoint (`src/server.js`) reads `processingConfig` from `req.body` as a **form-field string** and passes it straight to `createJob`, which `JSON.stringify`s it again (`src/database.js`). The PATCH `/jobs/:id/config` path already JSON-parses a string body, which is why the other rows were stored correctly.
- **Shape 2:** the PUT `/jobs/:id/config` merge spread the existing config (`{ ...existingConfig, ... }`) while it was still a string scalar; spreading a string yields numeric char-index keys. **That merge is already guarded** (it parses-if-string first), so this only affected rows written before the guard existed.

## Fix (at the source)
- **`createJob` (`src/database.js`)** — parse `processingConfig` if it's a string before storing, so *all* callers persist a proper object.
- **Upload endpoint (`src/server.js`)** — parse the multipart string up front, so the default-model fill *and* `createJob` both operate on an object. (Also fixes a latent bug where the default-model fill was skipped for string configs.)

A read-side parse-if-string normalization was previously added only to the save-and-reextract / reextract-sections handlers; this fixes the data at the source so the worker and all other readers are covered.

## Backfill
`migrations/backfill_double_encoded_processing_config.js` — dry-run by default, `--apply` to write. Two passes:
- **Pass 1 (string scalars):** `jsonb_typeof='string'` → parse → store object.
- **Pass 2 (char-indexed objects):** `jsonb_typeof='object'` with numeric-string keys → drop numeric keys (keep overlaid real config), falling back to reconstructing the JSON string from the char keys if no real keys survive.

Both passes only write when a valid object containing `extraction`/`processing` results; anything ambiguous is reported and skipped. **Already applied** (36 + 3 rows, 0 ambiguous).

## Verification (live DB)
| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `string` scalars | 36 | **0** |
| objects with numeric char-index keys | 3 | **0** |
| clean objects with `extraction`/`processing` | 6 | **45 / 45** |

Spot-checks: a previously string-scalar job now reads `extendai / openai / gpt-4.1`; the 3 char-indexed rows now read their intended configs (`qwen3-max`/`qwen`, `gpt-4o`/`openai`). `node --check` passes on both source files; the backfill is idempotent (re-running finds nothing to do).

Backend-only and back-compatible — no merge-order constraint.

author: marcellhenrique
body:
# PR Summary: Flows Client Abstraction (`weni.flows`)

## What we did

- Created a new `weni/flows/` subpackage with a reusable, endpoint-agnostic HTTP client for the Flows platform:
  - `weni/flows/client.py` — `FlowsClient`, exposing `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, and `delete` convenience methods on top of a single private request executor. It handles URL normalization (no duplicate or missing slashes), header construction (`Content-Type: application/json` + `Authorization: Bearer <token>`), and response parsing (parsed JSON, or `None` for empty-body successes such as `204 No Content`).
  - `weni/flows/exceptions.py` — a typed error hierarchy under a single base: `FlowsClientError` with `FlowsClientConfigError` (missing configuration), `FlowsHTTPError` (non-2xx, exposing `status_code` and `response_body`), `FlowsNetworkError` (transport failures), and `FlowsResponseError` (unreadable success bodies). All errors chain the original exception for diagnostics.
- Implemented eager configuration resolution at construction time, with precedence `context.project` → `context.credentials` → `context.globals` → environment variable, falling back to the default Flows staging URL. A missing `auth_token` fails fast with `FlowsClientConfigError` — the client never sends unauthenticated requests.
- Added a fully mocked pytest suite (`weni/flows/tests/`) with 39 tests covering verb delegation, URL building, headers, payload forwarding, configuration precedence, fail-fast validation, and every error translation path — **100% coverage** of the new module, no real network calls.
- Release hygiene: bumped the version to `2.7.0` (MINOR), added a `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and added a "Flows Client" user-guide page to the docs site (`docs/user-guide/flows-client.md`, registered in `mkdocs.yml`).
- Scope guarantees honored: `weni/broadcasts/` was not modified in any way, and the client contains no knowledge of any specific Flows endpoint.

## Why we did it

- Today, every toolkit feature that talks to Flows has to hand-roll the same HTTP plumbing — resolving the base URL, validating and attaching the auth token, building well-formed URLs, and translating `requests` failures — as `weni/broadcasts/sender.py` does manually. This duplicates ~120 lines of boilerplate per integration and spreads subtle inconsistencies across the codebase.
- By centralizing that plumbing in `FlowsClient`, a new Flows integration only needs to write the endpoint path and the payload:

  ```python
  from weni.flows import FlowsClient

  client = FlowsClient(context)
  result = client.post('/api/v2/anything.json', json={'text': 'Hello'})
  ```

- The single `FlowsClientError` base type gives integrations one consistent way to handle every failure mode (configuration, HTTP, network, parsing) instead of each feature defining its own ad-hoc exceptions.
- Fail-fast configuration validation surfaces deployment misconfiguration at client construction with a clear, named error — before any request reaches Flows — instead of an opaque 401/403 at request time.
- This is deliberately an abstraction-only delivery: no existing feature was migrated and no endpoint integration was added, keeping the diff small and reviewable. Refactoring `weni/broadcasts/` to use the client is an intentional follow-up task.

author: therealevanhenry
body:
## Small faithfulness batch (0.7.3, batch 1 of the campaign)

Four small parity fixes, bundled per the PR #166 precedent. Every behavioral claim was audited against the iperf3 source (`iperf_api.c` @ 8701e52) before implementation.

### #169 — END-block SUM jitter is the mean, not the max
iperf3: `avg_jitter += sp->jitter` per stream of the direction, then `avg_jitter /= test->num_streams` (iperf_api.c:4249, 4490). `sum_summaries` used worst-case; identical at `-P 1`, divergent at `-P ≥ 2` UDP (text `[SUM]` + `-J end.sum.jitter_ms`). Same fix the interval layer got in #166 (#142).

### #167 — `-S/--tos` accepts strtol-base-0 forms
`-S 0x20` / `-S 020` now parse (shared numeric arm with `--dscp`), with iperf3's IEBADTOS 0-255 range check (iperf_api.c:1504-1511) at string parse and at `build()` for the lib setter path. CLI carries the raw string through `ClientBuilder::tos_str` (lib stays clap-free).

### #160 — pacing follow-ups from the #157 review
- **`-b rate/burst` honored**: the limiter green-lights `burst` blocks per throttle check (iperf3's multisend loop, iperf_api.c:2193-2213); the count rides the param exchange (`"burst"`, sent only when nonzero, iperf_api.c:2461) so reverse/bidir servers batch too; present-burst range is 1..=1000 per IEBURST — `/0` is an error, distinct from no slash.
- **`--pacing-timer 1K` works**: iperf3 parses it with `unit_atoi` (1024-based, iperf_api.c:1780); the old plain-u32 clap parser rejected suffixes. The i32::MAX wire cap moved into `pacing_timer_str`.
- **`done` re-checked after the throttle sleep**: at very low `-b` the green-light sleep can outlast the test; the sender wrote one extra block past `done` (red test observed 2 blocks where 1 was correct).

### #188 — block size bounds at config, like iperf3
iperf3's semantics (iperf_api.c:1926-1942) are subtler than the issue stated: `blksize == 0` maps to the **default** (UDP: dynamic-from-MSS), then TCP validates `1..=MAX_BLOCKSIZE` (IEBLOCKSIZE) and UDP `MIN_UDP_BLOCKSIZE..=MAX_UDP_BLOCKSIZE` (IEUDPBLOCKSIZE). Implemented exactly that at `ClientBuilder::build()`, and the same bounds on a **negotiated** `len` in the server's `from_params` — closing the `-l 0` UDP header-write panic, a negative-len `as usize` wrap (multi-EiB alloc), and the oversized-alloc DoS from hostile peers. No SERVER_ERROR state on rejection: iperf3 clients follow that with an errno exchange we don't speak, and real clients never send these values — the server drops the test instead. The #184 `.max(1)` guards stay as defense.

### Wire note
`TestParams` gains an optional `"burst"` field, serialized only when nonzero — exactly iperf3's `if (test->settings->burst) cJSON_AddNumber(...)`, so the param JSON stays byte-compatible for every flag combination that exists today.

### Verification
- TDD: red observed for the limiter burst window, the done re-check, `parse_bitrate` burst range, `from_params` bounds, and the jitter mean; all green after.
- Full workspace suite green; clippy/fmt clean; xcheck green on all 7 targets.
- Smoke compat-matrix drift gate to run post-merge per campaign process.

Fixes #167. Fixes #169. Fixes #188. Closes #160.

author: nitinshendgeai
body:
## Root cause

The `envsubst` template approach (`listen ${PORT}`) was unreliable — Railway injects `$PORT` at container runtime, but if template substitution ran before that env var was available, nginx silently bound to nothing or the wrong port. Health check probed Railway's `$PORT`, got "connection refused", and marked the deploy failed.

## Fix

Three changes, all minimal:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `nginx.conf` | `listen 80` (hardcoded, same as EXPOSE) |
| `Dockerfile` | Direct `COPY nginx.conf` (no template); keeps `RUN touch .env`; `EXPOSE 80` |
| `railway.json` | `"internalPort": 80` — tells Railway to probe port 80 for health checks; timeout raised to 60s |

With `internalPort: 80`, Railway knows exactly which port to route traffic to and probe. No dynamic substitution needed.

## Test plan
- [ ] Docker build completes (`flutter build web` + nginx layer)
- [ ] Container starts, health check at `/` passes on port 80
- [ ] Flutter web app accessible at Railway URL

author: gonzafg2
body:
## Summary

Upgrades the `claude-code-review.yml` reviewer from the generic `/code-review` plugin to a **project-specific, change-aware** review.

## What changes

1. **Project-context prompt.** The reviewer reads `CLAUDE.md` and classifies each PR, then applies the right lens:
   - **ADR/RFC** (`docs/adr/`, `docs/rfcs/`) → design-coherence review (does it weaken a MANIFIESTO commitment? sound decision? template followed? TBD references?). *Does not hunt for bugs that don't exist.*
   - **Rust code** (`crates/`) → the hard security rules (no `unsafe`, no unbounded pre-auth allocation, no legacy crypto, type-state intact, mandated log fields, key zeroization).
   - **Other** → light consistency review.
2. **Fused output.** A single GitHub PR review: summary **body** + **inline comments** anchored to file:line — both at once, natively.
3. **Model pinned** to `claude-sonnet-4-6` for deterministic reviews.
4. **Permission** `pull-requests: read → write` — the minimum needed to post a review.
5. Drops the generic plugin + marketplace and the installer's placeholder comments.

## Why

The generic reviewer evaluated every PR as if hunting for code bugs, which is noise on the ADR PRs that are the entire current backlog (#46–#51). This makes the review evaluate against the MANIFIESTO and threat model — and it's already in place for when `crates/` lands.

## Type of change

- [x] Refactor / chore / CI / build

## Security considerations

- `pull-requests: write` is an increase in surface, but the **minimum** needed to post a review; no `contents: write`. On fork PRs, GitHub issues a read-only token under the `pull_request` trigger, so an external fork's review cannot post — safe by default. Suits the single-maintainer flow (branches in-repo).
- The prompt interpolates only `github.repository` and `pull_request.number` (an integer) — no free-text user input reaches a shell, so no injection surface. No `run:` blocks.

## Checklist

- [x] Commits signed off under the DCO.
- [x] Conventional Commits.
- [x] Signed commit.
- [x] YAML validated.

## Notes for reviewers

This PR will be reviewed by the **old** generic reviewer (the new one only takes effect once merged). The first PR to get the new project-aware review will be the next one opened after merge.

author: fujacob
body:
## Summary

Mechanical change: the swift-log level floor now defaults to `.info` instead of being hardcoded to `.trace`, so `.debug`/`.trace` log calls short-circuit (their message string and metadata dictionary are never built) unless verbose logging is explicitly turned on.

**This is not a privacy or security fix, and nothing dangerous was being logged.** No prompt text, OCR, screenshots, or JSONL were ever written in release builds: those sinks are gated on `-cotabby-debug` and stay gated. The only thing that ran in release was the CPU and allocation cost of *formatting* debug log lines that nothing consumes.

Why that happened: swift-log only skips evaluating a log call's `@autoclosure` when the handler's level is strictly above the call's level. Every handler hardcoded `.trace` (the lowest level), so no `.debug`/`.trace` call was ever skipped, in any build. The always-on `OSLogHandler` is installed in release too, so on the hot path (focus snapshots, engine routing, generation boundaries) release builds still built each debug line's string + metadata and handed it to `os_log` per keystroke. Under `-cotabby-debug` the same un-gated floor additionally meant ISO8601 + `JSONSerialization` + a locked disk write per keystroke, which inflates the energy numbers used to investigate #661.

Behavior after this change:
- Default floor `.info`: `.debug`/`.trace` calls are skipped before they allocate.
- `-cotabby-debug` raises the floor to `.trace` (full Console + JSONL capture, unchanged).
- `COTABBY_LOG_LEVEL=<trace|debug|info|...>` overrides it explicitly, e.g. Console `.debug` without the heavier file/screenshot artifacts.
- New one-time `Logging initialized` line records `debug_mode`, `min_log_level`, and the JSONL sink paths.

## Validation

```
xcodebuild -project Cotabby.xcodeproj -scheme Cotabby -destination 'platform=macOS' build \
  -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile
# ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **

swiftlint lint --quiet Cotabby/Support/CotabbyDebugOptions.swift Cotabby/Support/FileLogHandler.swift
# exit 0
```

Not yet exercised end-to-end at runtime. To confirm on next launch:
- No flags: one `Logging initialized` line with `min_log_level=info`, and no per-keystroke `.debug` lines in `log stream`.
- `-cotabby-debug`: `min_log_level=trace`, `cotabby.jsonl` / `llm-io.jsonl` populate, and `event_log` / `llm_io_log` paths appear in the startup line.

## Linked issues

Refs #661. This is measurement-hygiene groundwork: it removes per-keystroke logging overhead so energy profiling is accurate. It is not by itself a steady-state energy fix; the larger levers (inference frequency, OCR defaults, idle timers) are separate follow-ups.

## Risk / rollout notes

- Not a privacy or security change. Release builds never wrote prompt, OCR, screenshot, or JSONL data, before or after this PR; those file sinks remain gated on `-cotabby-debug`. The only change is that debug-level log lines are no longer formatted in the default configuration.
- Behavior change: `.debug`/`.trace` are no longer emitted to OSLog by default, so `log show/stream ... --level debug` will not show them without `-cotabby-debug` or `COTABBY_LOG_LEVEL=debug`. `.info` and above (model-load config, permission transitions, routing fallbacks, warnings, errors) still stream. CLAUDE.md debugging docs updated to match.
- The dedicated llm-io sink is unchanged (still `.trace`, debug-only install), so counting generations per minute from `llm-io.jsonl` is unaffected.
- No schema, settings, or pbxproj migration. No new files, so no `xcodegen generate` needed.
- `COTABBY_LOG_LEVEL` accepts swift-log level names; an unrecognized value is ignored and falls back to the flag/default.

author: pillowedshirt
body:
### Motivation

- Make the viewer auto-update without manual "Update now" presses and avoid full browser reloads by preferring Streamlit-native fragment reruns when available.  
- Keep a robust fallback to `streamlit-autorefresh` so older Streamlit versions still auto-update.  
- Provide clear UI feedback about whether updates are running and which refresh engine is active.  

### Description

- Added `Callable` to the typing imports and detection for `streamlit_autorefresh` so the code can use either refresh engine.  
- Introduced a persistent refresh counter in `st.session_state` (`viewer_refresh_count`) and explicit state variables `refresh_status` and `refresh_mode` to track and display refresh behavior.  
- Wrapped the entire live-dashboard loading and rendering logic inside `def render_live_dashboard() -> None:` so it can be rerun as a fragment without reloading the page.  
- Replaced the previous top-level `st_autorefresh` usage with a fragment-first runner that uses `@st.fragment(run_every=f"{int(refresh_sec)}s")` when `hasattr(st, 'fragment')` is true and falls back to a single `st_autorefresh(interval=..., key="live_data_update_fallback")` call otherwise, while keeping the manual `Update now` button and showing an error if no engine is available.  
- Updated the viewer status line to report `update`, `mode`, `interval`, and `cycle` (`refresh_status`, `refresh_mode`, `refresh_sec`, `refresh_count`).  

### Testing

- `python -m py_compile viewer.py` succeeded and verified the file compiles.  
- Automated AST/source checks confirmed there is exactly one fallback `st_autorefresh` call, a single `render_live_dashboard` function, and the native fragment runner decorator present.  
- `git diff --check` and other repository checks passed with no whitespace or syntax issues reported.  
- Attempts to install/runtime-verify runtime dependencies (`pip install streamlit ...` and `streamlit run viewer.py`) failed due to the environment lacking Streamlit and the package-index proxy returning 403, so full interactive UI validation could not be executed in this environment.

author: scala-steward-bot
linuxdynasty
body:
Closes #2161. Advances scoped incident-context reads (#2144); the scoped authz **predicate** itself stays `needs-security-review` and is out of scope here.

## Durable-signal finding (the prior investigation missed a non-fuzzy path)

The earlier #2144/#2161 trace concluded the incident→repo join is fuzzy (PagerDuty `lower(service_name)` match) and shipped nothing. That trace stopped at the **read-path** name join. There **is** a durable, structural, non-fuzzy join it missed — the Terraform backend-locator resolver already wired in production for the drift domains:

- `incident.Service.ID` (real provider service id) equals an applied PagerDuty service fact's `provider_object_id` — `go/internal/collector/terraformstate/pagerduty_applied.go:71-73`.
- That applied fact carries the Terraform `backend_kind` + `locator_hash` — `pagerduty_applied.go:191-192`.
- `tfstatebackend.Resolver.ResolveConfigCommitForBackend` maps `(backend_kind, locator_hash)` → a **single owning `RepoID`** with explicit `ErrAmbiguousBackendOwner` (>1 repo) / `ErrNoConfigRepoOwnsBackend` (none) — `go/internal/relationships/tfstatebackend/resolver.go:103-152`, production-implemented by `PostgresTerraformBackendQuery` — `go/internal/storage/postgres/tfstate_backend_canonical.go:104-150`, and already wired in `cmd/reducer/main.go`.

Durable chain: `incident.Service.ID → applied service fact (provider_object_id) → (backend_kind, locator_hash) → owning repo_id`. No service name anywhere in the edge.

## What this implements

A reducer-owned `DomainIncidentRepositoryCorrelation` that emits a `reducer_incident_repository_correlation` fact per provider service id, with the exact/derived/ambiguous/rejected discipline of `service_catalog_correlation`:

- **exact / derived** (single owning repo, unambiguous backend) → durable repository edge.
- **rejected** (blank provider id / name-fingerprint only), **ambiguous** (multi-repo or same provider id under two backend locators — fork/mirror never false-merges), **unresolved** (no Eshu repo owns the backend) → `provenance_only`, **no edge**.

This keeps the downstream #2144 scoped predicate fail-closed: an incident with no durable repository edge is invisible to a scoped token. The domain is additive (registers only when loader+writer are wired) and idempotent (deterministic fact id over scope/generation/provider/provider_service_id; `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`).

## Proof matrix (correlation-truth)

- Positive: exact + derived edges.
- Negative: name-only rejected (resolver never consulted), unresolved no-edge.
- Ambiguous: resolver-ambiguous + same provider id under two distinct backend locators.
- Fork/mirror: distinct canonical repos → ambiguous, no false merge.
- Idempotency: stable fact id across exact→ambiguous flip; distinct ids per provider service id.
- Loader null-handling + resolver-adapter no-owner/ambiguous/single-owner translation.

## Gates

- `go test ./internal/reducer ./cmd/reducer ./internal/storage/postgres ./internal/telemetry -count=1` — pass.
- `go test ./internal/reducer -race -run 'IncidentRepositoryCorrelation|BuildIncidentRepositoryCorrelations' -count=1` — pass.
- `go test ./cmd/bootstrap-index ./cmd/ingester ./cmd/reducer ./internal/runtime ./internal/status ./internal/storage/postgres -count=1` — pass.
- `golangci-lint run` (touched packages) — 0 issues.
- `verify-performance-evidence.sh` — pass (benchmark + observability markers found for hot-path changes; bench ~168µs/op for 512 rows over 4 distinct backends, resolver memoized once per backend; evidence in `go/internal/reducer/README.md`).
- `verify-package-docs.sh` — pass.
- `git diff --check` clean; `go build ./...` clean.

## Security review

The resolution-confidence rules (what counts as a confident provider→backend→repo resolution, fork/mirror handling) are a tenant-isolation boundary and carry the `needs-security-review` label inherited from #2161. The edge itself is additive and fail-closed-safe to land independently; the #2144 scoped predicate is sequenced after this.

### Motivation
- Provide an abstract, themeable design system so UI colors/spacing/shadows/radii can be switched without changing component CSS. 
- Preserve the existing `warm-paper` design while migrating hard-coded visual colors to tokens so multiple themes (default, warm-paper, dark) can be supported.
- Expose a lightweight UI control for users to choose a theme and persist it across sessions.

### Motivation
- Make manual evidence review faster by opening workbooks at the pending ID on the send-data sheet so the operator can check the exact record immediately.
- Allow marking a single ID at a time and keep the workbook open so the cursor can jump to the next pending ID without resetting cursors, saving, or closing between IDs.

- Add helper functions `Test-RowBitDone`, `Get-RowReviewId`, `Get-PendingReviewRows`, `Get-WorksheetByName`, and `Move-ToSendDataId` and wire a new `sendDataSheetName` label to locate the `送信データ` sheet and position the cursor on column A matching the current ID in `ReviewEvidence.ps1`.

author: shabih-paystack
body:
Adds `case 1862:` to the per-user-error skip-list in `MySrvC::connect_error()`. Without it, a backend connection failure due to `password_expired = Y` on the user counts toward `mysql-shun_on_failures` and can mark the backend `SHUNNED` — degrading or failing connections for unrelated clients on the same backend.

`1862` is the errno MySQL 8.0 / Aurora returns at `mysql_real_connect()` time when the user has an expired password. It's per-user state, not backend health — by definition the backend is responsive enough to evaluate credentials and report the expiry. This matches the intent of the existing entries (`1044`, `1045`, `1203`, `1226`, `3118`, etc.).

Verified on `v3.0.9` and `v4.0` head — `1862` is not in the current skip-list. Reproduction and damage measurement in #5846.

Happy to add a regression test under `test/tap/` if the maintainers indicate the preferred location. The existing entries in this switch don't appear to have dedicated tests, so I followed that precedent for the initial submission.

Closes #317. Verification-only (no code change) — confirms by **observation** what the #308 audit only read.

## Why
The #308 worker-shim audit read `createGraphics(WEBGL)` / `createFramebuffer` as worker-safe but never ran them. The same audit's `text()` claim was a false positive that observation refuted (P130), so an unverified "it's fine" wasn't trustworthy. This closes the loop.

## What
`viz-worker-webgl.spec.ts` — two sketches, worker-vs-main:
- `createGraphics(width, height, WEBGL)` — a **2nd** OffscreenCanvas + WebGL2 context off-main, blitted to the main WEBGL canvas
- `createFramebuffer()` — an FBO on the main canvas's context, drawn as a texture

Verdict: `viz.worker` mounted, **`viz.glctx` live** (a real GL context came up — the strongest WEBGL signal), zero engine-log errors, non-blank compositor pixels.

| createGraphics(WEBGL) | 0.0344, `glctx:1`, errs `[]` | 0.0509 |
| createFramebuffer | 0.0570, `glctx:1`, errs `[]` | 0.0833 |

Both render off-main == main → **confirmed working, no fix needed.** (litFraction is corner-referenced, so full-bleed 3D reads low; the 0.02 floor separates render from blank ~0.005 and `glctx` is the real proof — noted in the spec.)

body:
## Slice 665 — board-pack "Generate draft" empty-date validation feedback

On `/board-packs`, clicking **"Generate draft"** with an empty (or malformed) quarter-end date silently no-opped — the submit handler's `if (periodEnd)` guard swallowed the empty case with no toast/inline message, and the button's `disabled={!periodEnd}` left the operator unsure whether the action failed or was processing (audit **ATLAS-015**, 2026-06-10 empty-tenant UI audit).

Adopts the canonical `risks/new` client-side-validation pattern: a pure `validateGenerateForm` fn (extracted so vitest pins it without the React tree) returns a field-error map; the page renders an inline `role="alert"` message wired to the date input via `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby`, validates on submit-attempt, and re-validates live afterward so the error clears as the operator fills in a valid date. The submit no longer relies on a silent `disabled` to mask the failure; the form blocks submission and the server is never contacted with an empty date.

### Acceptance criteria

| AC | Description | Status |
| -- | ----------- | ------ |
| AC-1 | Empty/invalid quarter-end date shows clear inline validation / toast; no silent no-op | PASS — inline `role="alert"` error ("Enter a quarter-end date.") on submit-attempt; e2e asserts visible + correct text |
| AC-2 | Submit blocks (or control disabled) until a valid date is present, consistent with the app's form-validation pattern | PASS — `validateGenerateForm` gates submit (`hasErrors` short-circuits before `generate.mutate`); server never contacted with empty date; mirrors `risks/new/validate.ts` |
| AC-3 | A valid date still generates the draft (no regression); Playwright asserts empty-date feedback + happy path | PASS — valid date fires the POST and the new pack surfaces in the list; both paths asserted in `board-pack-generate-validation.spec.ts` |

### Anti-criterion

- **Does NOT change board-pack generation semantics — client-side validation/feedback only.** HONORED: zero changes to `internal/api/`, `migrations`, `proto`, or any wire shape. The `generateBoardPack` POST body is unchanged.

### Files touched

| File | Change |
| ---- | ------ |
| `web/app/(authed)/board-packs/validate.ts` | NEW — pure `validateGenerateForm` + `hasErrors` (mirrors `risks/new/validate.ts`) |
| `web/app/(authed)/board-packs/validate.test.ts` | NEW — vitest pin (6 cases: empty / whitespace / malformed / impossible-calendar / valid / trimmed) |
| `web/app/(authed)/board-packs/page.tsx` | inline error render (`aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby`/`role=alert`), submit-attempt validation gate, live re-validate, drop silent `!periodEnd` disable |
| `web/e2e/board-pack-generate-validation.spec.ts` | NEW — Playwright spec (hermetic BFF route-mock per slice-594 lesson): empty-date feedback + happy path |
| `web/coverage-thresholds.json` | per-file floor for the new `board-packs/validate.ts` (98, same PR as the tests) |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Unreleased / Added bullet |

author: ivank
body:
## Summary

Phase 5: enable a **second approval class** at its own entitlement scope. The classify→gate→grant→conclusion pipeline is already `(class, target)`-generic and `gcppam.Config.Entitlements` already maps class→entitlement id, so the only single-class assumption left was `entitlementName` hardcoding the resource parent as `projects/<target>`.

- **`gcppam`**: new `EntitlementScopes map[string]string` (class → `projects`/`folders`/`organizations`); `entitlementName` uses it, defaulting to `projects`.
- **config**: the `class "<name>" {}` block gains an optional `entitlement_scope`.
- **serve**: `gcppamConfig` threads each class's scope into the backend.

A second class (e.g. `database`) can now gate independently and live at a folder- or org-level entitlement, not just a project.

## Key decisions

- **Removed the hardcoded `projects/` parent** — it violated the gcppam package's own stated principle ("no hardcoded names, everything is Config"). Scope is now per-class config.
- **Backward compatible**: absent `entitlement_scope` ⇒ `projects/<target>`, byte-identical to before (existing gcppam tests stay green).
- **No new machinery** — multiple gating classes already flow through gate targets, grants, the verdict, and the UI; this just lets them differ in entitlement scope.

## Risks / limitations

- Scope strings are passed through to the PAM resource path (`projects`/`folders`/`organizations`); an invalid scope would produce an invalid entitlement name (surfaced as a PAM API error at request time) — not validated up front.
- The requester-pool slot is still `PR mod pool` (true leasing remains future work, unchanged).

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` green (19 packages); existing gcppam tests unchanged (default-projects path)
- [x] `TestEntitlementNameScope` — projects (default), folders, organizations, unconfigured→""
- [x] `TestLoadServerAndClassBlocks` extended — `entitlement_scope` parses
- [x] `TestGcppamConfigPerClassScope` — serve wires scope per class; default class has no explicit scope

This PR introduces a gRPC service on top of markitdown This opens up to streaming services in multiple languages in HTTP2. Also with a strong document definition it is great for semantic embedding for getting more meaning into your chunks. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Client["gRPC Client"] Server["MarkItDown gRPC Server"] Core["Standard MarkItDown Converters"] Stream["Experimental Streaming Layer"] PDF["PDF page-by-page"] PPT["PPTX slide-by-slide"] Client -->|"Convert"| Server Client -->|"ConvertStream"| Server Client -->|"ConvertDocumentStream"| Server Server --> Core Server --> Stream Stream --> PDF Stream --> PPT PDF -->|"reuse extraction logic"| Core PPT -->|"reuse per-slide logic"| Core ``` ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant gRPC as gRPC Server participant Stream as Streaming Controller participant Conv as PDF or PPTX Converter Client->>gRPC: ConvertStream / ConvertDocumentStream
experimental_incremental=true gRPC-->>Client: started loop For each page or slide gRPC->>Stream: request next fragment Stream->>Conv: convert one page or slide Conv-->>Stream: markdown fragment Stream-->>gRPC: normalized fragment alt ConvertStream gRPC-->>Client: markdown_chunk else ConvertDocumentStream gRPC-->>Client: element (heading, table, paragraph, ...) end end gRPC-->>Client: completed ```

author: tejasghatte
body:
## Summary

Adds full OpenAI-compatible batch API support for Vertex AI (create, retrieve, list, cancel) via the HTTP transport, and fixes ID stability issues in both the Vertex and Gemini batch implementations.

## Changes

- **Vertex batch IDs are now base64 (RawURLEncoding) encoded/decoded** in the OpenAI HTTP integration, matching the existing Bedrock pattern. Vertex batch IDs are full resource names (`projects/.../batchPredictionJobs/{id}`) and `input_file_id` values are `gs://` URIs — both contain slashes that would break URL path routing without encoding.
- **Gemini batch list** now returns the full resource name (`batches/<id>`) as the ID instead of stripping the prefix, making IDs stable and consistent with create/retrieve responses.
- **Vertex cancel and delete** now echo back the caller's batch ID directly instead of re-extracting a bare job ID from the resource name, keeping IDs stable across the full lifecycle.
- **`extractBatchIDFromName` (Gemini) and `vertexBatchJobIDFromName` (Vertex)** helper functions removed since IDs are no longer stripped.
- **Vertex `BatchCreate` supports raw-passthrough mode**: validation and typed-field extraction are skipped when a raw request body is present, allowing callers to pass arbitrary Vertex `BatchPredictionJob` payloads directly.
- **Vertex `BatchCreate` no longer strips `output_uri`/`gcs_bucket`/`gcs_prefix` control params** from `extra_params` before forwarding to Vertex, since those keys are no longer injected by the typed path.
- **Vertex region validation** relaxed: the `"global"` region is no longer explicitly rejected; only an empty region is an error.
- **Integration test config** updated to enable Vertex batch scenarios (`batch_file_upload`, `batch_list`, `batch_retrieve`, `batch_cancel`) and disable virtual key testing temporarily.
- **Integration tests** added for Vertex batch create-with-file, retrieve, cancel, and full e2e (upload → create → poll → list → cleanup).

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [x] Transports (HTTP)
- [x] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
go test ./core/providers/vertex/...
go test ./core/providers/gemini/...
go test ./transports/bifrost-http/...
```

For integration tests, set the following environment variables and run the Python test suite:

```sh
export VERTEX_PROJECT_ID=<your-project>
export VERTEX_REGION=<e.g. us-central1>
export VERTEX_GCS_BUCKET=<your-bucket>
# Then run:
pytest tests/integrations/python/tests/test_openai.py -k "batch"
```

Expected: Vertex batch create, retrieve, cancel, list, and e2e file API tests pass. Batch IDs returned by create round-trip correctly through retrieve and cancel without modification.

## Breaking changes

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

Vertex batch IDs returned by the OpenAI HTTP transport are now base64 (RawURLEncoding) encoded. Any client storing a Vertex batch ID from a previous version will need to re-create the batch, as old bare IDs will not decode correctly. Gemini batch list IDs now include the `batches/` prefix where previously only the suffix was returned.

## Related issues

## Security considerations

Batch IDs and `input_file_id` values are base64-encoded for URL safety only; no secrets or PII are introduced. GCS URIs passed as `input_file_id` are opaque to the transport layer and are only decoded immediately before being forwarded to the Vertex API.

- [ ] I read `docs/contributing/README.md` and followed the guidelines
- [x] I added/updated tests where appropriate
- [ ] I updated documentation where needed
- [x] I verified builds succeed (Go and UI)

author: quadseven
body:
## Why

The manifest-merge step at `.github/workflows/build.container-multiarch.yml:188` built the `docker buildx imagetools create` argument list with `$IMAGE_REF` used **as the `printf` format string**:

```
$(printf "${IMAGE_REF}@sha256:%s " *)
```

Putting a runtime variable in `printf`'s format position is the classic SC2059 footgun: any `%` (or `\`) in `IMAGE_REF` is interpreted as a format directive rather than a literal, which would silently corrupt the generated `name@sha256:<digest>` refs and produce a broken/empty manifest list. `IMAGE_REF` derives from `inputs.image` + the `registry` secret, so it isn't fully constrained here.

## Change

Single-line diff — keep the format string literal, pass the ref as a `%s` argument:

```
-          docker buildx imagetools create -t "${IMAGE_REF}:${TAG}" $(printf "${IMAGE_REF}@sha256:%s " *)
+          docker buildx imagetools create -t "${IMAGE_REF}:${TAG}" $(printf '%s@sha256:%s ' "$IMAGE_REF" *)
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The `printf` uses a literal format string and passes `$IMAGE_REF` as an argument.
- [x] Single file changed; no inputs, secrets, or consumer call-sites changed.
- [x] Workflow still parses (validated with a YAML load); intentional SC2046 word-split on the `$(...)` result is preserved.
- [x] No behavior change on the happy path (a normal image ref with no `%` produces identical refs).

Size: XS

## Out of scope

- The intentional unquoted word-split of the `$(...)` result (SC2046, already annotated).
- The `checkout` `persist-credentials` hardening on this file (tracked in #10).

Closes #13

author: bizkon
body:
## Зачем

CI на main давно красный по нескольким независимым причинам (инфра/долг). Этот PR закрывает **все, кроме Lint**: после него на PR зелёные/neutral **8 из 9** чеков, красным остаётся только намеренно отложенный biome.

## Что починено

### 1. Typecheck — `TS2688: Cannot find type definition file for 'node'`
CI-команда: `turbo run typecheck && tsc --noEmit -p scripts/tsconfig.json`. `"types": ["node"]` в tsconfig есть у **4 пакетов** (`voice`, `ui`, `db`, `agents`) **и** у корневого `scripts/tsconfig.json` — все реально используют `node:fs`/`node:path`/`node:url`, но `@types/node` **не был объявлен** в их package.json (в отличие от 6 пакетов, где он есть). В strict-pnpm CI не резолвилось. turbo фейлит **fail-fast по одному пакету**, маскируя остальные (`voice→ui→db→agents→scripts`) — поэтому чинилось итеративно. Локально проблема скрыта хоистингом.

**Фикс:** `"@types/node": "^25.9.1"` в `voice`, `ui`, `db`, `agents` и в **корневой** `package.json` (для `scripts/tsconfig.json`).

### 2. pnpm audit (moderate+) — postcss XSS
`postcss <8.5.10` ([GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93)) транзитивно через `apps/admin > next > postcss`. **Фикс:** `pnpm.overrides` → `"postcss@<8.5.10": ">=8.5.10"`.

### 3. Deploy previews + Dependency Review → неблокирующие
- **preview.yml** — `vercel pull` падал без `secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN`. Добавлен job-level `env: VERCEL_TOKEN` + step-guard `if: ${{ env.VERCEL_TOKEN != '' }}` → без секрета деплой-шаги **скипаются** (job зелёный); появятся секреты — авто-активируются.
- **security.yml** — `dependency-review-action` требует Dependency graph (недоступен под trade-controls флагом). Job гейтится repo-переменной `DEPENDENCY_REVIEW_ENABLED` → по умолчанию **skip** (neutral).

| Typecheck · Test · Build · Audit (high+) · pnpm audit (moderate+) · Deploy admin · Deploy miniapp · Dependency Review (skipping) | **Lint (biome)** — отложен |

4-й класс долга — **Lint (biome, ~303 ошибки)** — намеренно **НЕ** здесь. Правильный фикс = config (vcs/ignore/test-relax) + механический реформат **122 файлов** + 62 ручных lint-правки. author: akostrzewski-ant
body:
This PR fixes `"AstNode is not of expected type, but instead has type 'SEL'"` that occurred during FSM detection phase for a continuous assignment with RHS `AstEq` under enabled `--coverage`. Additionally, fixes C++ compilation errors unveiled after that.

* Added support for selection operators by using `AstArraySel::baseFromp` for scope extraction. A warning `COVERIGN` will be issued for the unsupported ones.

* Fixed variable redeclaration in emitted C++ code caused by temporary variable not taking into account scope name.

The temporary variable created inside `FsmLowerVisitor::buildOne` did not take into account scope name, so duplicates were created when variables with the same name came from different scopes. Fixed this by utilizing `V3UniqueNames` for name generation. 

The `t_fsm_duplicate.v` test has unused pins named `input unused<n>` to avoid code being optimized out.

# Topic summary DB 저장 및 조회 API MVP

## 작업 내용

- raw text 기반 topic summary report MVP를 DB 저장 및 read API 단계로 확장했습니다.
- `topics`, `topic_articles` 저장 구조와 기본 dry-run save CLI를 추가했습니다.
- 저장된 topic summary를 조회하는 `/topics`, `/topics/{topic_id}` API를 추가했습니다.
- API와 저장 report에는 raw text 전문을 노출하지 않습니다.

## 주요 변경 사항

- `db/migrations/005_create_topics_tables.sql`
  - topic summary와 근거 article 연결을 위한 테이블, FK, unique constraint, 조회 index를 정의합니다.
  - 동일 input의 provider/model별 결과를 저장할 수 있도록 `unique(summary_input_hash, provider, model)`을 사용합니다.
  - `confidence`는 `0~1` 범위만 허용하도록 DB-level check constraint를 추가했습니다.

- `scripts/save_topic_summaries.py`
  - 기존 summary 생성 helper를 재사용해 save plan과 markdown report를 생성합니다.
  - 기본 실행은 read-only dry-run입니다.
  - `--execute`가 명시된 경우에만 transaction 안에서 topic과 article link를 저장합니다.
  - approved fix로 upsert conflict target을 migration의 composite unique constraint와 일치시켰습니다.

- `app/utils/topic_summary.py`
  - 실제 bounded summary input을 기반으로 `summary_input_hash`를 생성합니다.

- `app/routers/topics.py`, `app/main.py`
  - topic 목록 및 상세 read-only router를 추가하고 FastAPI app에 등록했습니다.

- 테스트
  - migration 구조, dry-run/save plan, mocked persistence, composite conflict target, pagination/detail/404/raw text 미노출을 검증합니다.

## 추가/변경된 API

- `GET /topics`
  - `page`, `page_size`, `status`, `date_from`, `date_to`, `keyword` 필터를 지원하는 pagination 목록 API입니다.
  - `items`, `page`, `page_size`, `total`, `has_next`를 반환합니다.

- `GET /topics/{topic_id}`
  - topic summary와 관련 article metadata를 반환합니다.
  - 존재하지 않는 topic은 `404`를 반환합니다.

- API 응답에는 `raw_text`가 포함되지 않습니다.
- 기존 API response 구조는 변경하지 않았습니다.

## DB 변경 사항

- migration SQL에 `topics`, `topic_articles` 테이블을 추가했습니다.
- 주요 constraint:
  - `unique(summary_input_hash, provider, model)`
  - `unique(topic_id, article_id)`
  - `topic_articles.topic_id -> topics.id`
  - `topic_articles.article_id -> articles.id`
  - `topics.confidence` 범위 check: `0 <= confidence <= 1`
- Human operator가 Supabase SQL Editor에서 migration을 수동 적용했고, verification 문서에 table/constraint/index 확인 결과를 기록했습니다.
- Human-approved limited execute에서 deterministic topic 1개와 관련 article link 1개를 저장했습니다.

## README 영향

- README는 변경하지 않았습니다.
- `/topics` API 구현은 추가되었지만 production deployment와 production HTTP verification은 아직 수행하지 않았습니다.
- 운영 surface가 확정된 뒤 README/RUNBOOK 업데이트를 별도 작업에서 반영할 예정입니다.

## 테스트

- 초기 구현 검증:
  - Python compile: passed
  - focused summary/save/API tests: 30 tests passed
  - full unittest: 105 tests passed

- Approved fix 검증:
  - Python compile: passed
  - focused migration/save/topics API tests: 11 tests passed
  - full unittest: 106 tests passed
  - save CLI help: passed
  - 전체 및 targeted `git diff --check`: passed

- Human-approved verification:
  - Supabase migration 수동 적용 확인
  - save CLI dry-run 성공
  - limited `--execute` 저장 성공
  - local `/health`, `/topics`, `/topics/1` API 응답 확인
  - `/topics`, `/topics/1` 응답에서 raw text 미포함 확인

- Scope/security:
  - K8s, GitHub Actions, frontend, Dockerfile 변경 없음
  - credential 값 노출 없음

## 확인 결과

- Approved fix 적용 후 `UPSERT_TOPIC_QUERY`와 migration 모두 `(summary_input_hash, provider, model)` composite key를 사용합니다.
- Human-approved Supabase verification:
  - migration 적용 및 expected table/constraint/index 확인
  - dry-run 성공: DB write 및 raw extraction 없음
  - limited execute 성공: topic 1개, related article link 1개 저장
- Human-approved local API verification:
  - `/health`, `/topics`, `/topics/1` 정상 응답

- Approved fixes 적용:

  - save CLI upsert target 검증 테스트 추가
- Antigravity re-review: `PASS`

## 비고

- Supabase migration 및 limited execute는 human-approved verification으로 수행되었으며 Codex가 실행하지 않았습니다.

author: teakayah
body:
💡 What: Optimized DuckDB-Wasm result extraction in `getRows` by checking the Arrow schema for BigInt-like types instead of running `typeof === 'bigint'` on every single cell.
🎯 Why: The previous implementation performed a dynamic `typeof` check on every cell across all rows, creating CPU overhead when processing large datasets with standard numerical or string types.
📉 Impact: Significantly reduces CPU overhead and speeds up rendering of large tables when no BigInt columns are present by using a fast-path mapping loop without type checks.
🔬 Measurement: The application will render large query results faster in the Grid.js UI. This can be verified by executing a heavy query in the Analytical Drop-Zone and comparing rendering time.

## Summary

Refs #763
Refs #775

Fixes Skills Generator plain-mode output when `include_example_code=false`.

PR #786 confirmed frontend wiring. Preview QA on the first #787 revision showed prompt-only compliance was **insufficient**: with Example Code OFF (PLAIN header), the LLM still returned `**Examples:**`, fenced ` ```json ` blocks, and JSON input/output samples.

This revision keeps the prompt cleanup **and** adds a deterministic post-LLM sanitization guard in `WorkerClient.generate_skill()`.

## Root cause

1. **Prompt layer:** `skills_generator.md` template mandates a `## Examples` section with arrow-form JSON samples.
2. **Runtime layer:** LLM can still ignore/disable-path instructions → examples/code leak into `skill_definition`.

Agent Generator unchanged (no evidence of same bug).

- `app/llm_engine/client.py`
  - `_sanitize_skill_definition_plain()` — output guard (disabled path only)
  - existing `_skill_prompt()` / `example_code_note` prompt tightening retained
- `tests/test_skills_generator.py`
  - output-level sanitization tests (false cleans, true preserves)
  - existing prompt assembly tests retained

## Sanitization behavior (`include_example_code=false` only)

Applied to returned `skill_definition` after LLM response:

| Removed | Details |
|---------|---------|
| Fenced code blocks | Any ` ```lang ... ``` ` block |
| `## Examples` | Section through next `##` heading |
| `**Examples:**` | Bold variant through next section |
| `## Implementation Example` | Section through next `##` heading |
| Arrow-form lines | `Input: ... → Output: ...` bullets |
| JSON example bullets | `Input: `{...}` / `Output: `{...}` lines |

When `include_example_code=true`, output is returned unchanged.

💡 What: Combined multiple `.filter()` passes in `filterVehicles` into a single iteration using logical AND (`&&`).
🎯 Why: In JavaScript, chaining `.filter()` executes multiple full loops over an array and creates intermediate arrays at every step. This wastes CPU cycles and memory. Consolidating the conditions optimizes both time and space complexity.
📊 Impact: Eliminates 5 redundant array iterations and the allocation of 5 intermediate arrays during vehicle filtering operations.
🔬 Measurement: Run `pnpm test:run` to ensure all 135 tests still pass, validating that functionality remains perfectly identical while executing more efficiently.
