body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> ## 🔁 TODO — BACKPORT TO STABLE BRANCHES (do not forget on merge)
>
> This optimization must land on **every stable branch that ships the EC2 single-region reference**. Targets verified by checking the files on each branch:
>
> | Target branch | EC2 single-region present? | Action |
> |---|---|---|
> | `stable/8.9` | ✅ yes | **BACKPORT** — label `backport stable/8.9` |
> | `stable/8.8` | ✅ yes | **BACKPORT** — label `backport stable/8.8` |
> | `stable/8.7` | ❌ not present | skip |
> | `stable/8.6` | ❌ removed | skip |
>
> **How:** backports run via `korthout/backport-action` (`.github/workflows/internal_global_pr_backport.yml`). Add the `backport stable/8.8` + `backport stable/8.9` labels **before/at merge**, or comment `/backport stable/8.8 stable/8.9` on the merged PR. (Labels are pre-applied on this PR.)
>
> **Backport notes:**
> - On 8.8/8.9 the install pulls **GA releases** (e.g. `8.9.6` / connectors `8.9.5`), not SNAPSHOT. The per-node + per-reinstall duplication is identical, so the **~83% within-run saving still applies**; and because GA versions are stable, the L2 cross-run cache (follow-up) would drive these branches toward **~0 downloads**.
> - The cache logic is **version-form agnostic** (`script_default` parses both `${VAR:-"x"}` and the upgrade test's plain `VAR=x`), so it applies as-is.
> - Watch for minor conflicts in `camunda-install.sh` (version-default lines / vendored connectors launcher): keep the **stable** version defaults and add the new cache branch around them.
> - Re-run `shellcheck` + `pre-commit` on each backport PR before merge.
>
> - [ ] `stable/8.9` backport opened, green & merged
> - [ ] `stable/8.8` backport opened, green & merged

## Why

The `ci-infrastructure-experience-ro` account drives the bulk of our Artifactory (`artifacts.camunda.com`) egress. It comes almost entirely from the **AWS EC2 single-region** reference tests, which install Camunda by `curl`-ing two large artifacts from Artifactory **on every node**:

- the Camunda distribution tarball `camunda-zeebe-*.tar.gz`
- the connectors uber-jar `connector-runtime-bundle-*-with-dependencies.jar`

Per matrix leg this runs ~**12×** (3 nodes × {initial install, CloudWatch re-install, upgrade previous, upgrade current}). Since `main` is on `8.10.0-SNAPSHOT`, these are **daily, non-cacheable** builds, so every run re-downloads everything.

This is not new traffic (the download has existed since 2024) — it became attributable + heavier when we (1) added a dedicated authenticated RO account and (2) moved to SNAPSHOT artifacts. Most of the volume is avoidable CI duplication.

## What (L1 — download once, fan out to nodes)

The download-caching logic lives in a **CI-only helper** (`aws/compute/ec2-single-region/test/ci-distro-cache.sh`) so the **customer-facing procedure stays clean**:

- **`all-in-one-install.sh`** (customer procedure): only a small, **no-op-by-default** hook — it `source`s the helper and calls it **only when `CAMUNDA_DISTRO_CACHE_LIB` is set** (our CI). With nothing set it behaves exactly as before (~21 lines of optional, clearly-marked hooks).
- **`test/ci-distro-cache.sh`** (CI only, not part of the procedure): `warm_distro_cache` downloads each artifact **once** into a **version-keyed** runner cache; `push_distro_cache_to_node` stages it on each node via the existing bastion file-push (clearing the node cache each round). Best-effort — any failure falls back to per-node download.
- **`camunda-install.sh`** (node): when a pre-staged file is present it is copied instead of `curl`-ed. **The default (customer) path is unchanged.**
- **workflow**: sets `CAMUNDA_DISTRO_CACHE_DIR` + `CAMUNDA_DISTRO_CACHE_LIB` on the terratest step so the cache is active in CI. The cache dir persists for the whole job, so re-installs reuse it.

Net effect: **~12 → 2 downloads per leg (~83% less)**. The node cache is cleared each round so the upgrade test never reuses the wrong version.

## Expected savings

- ~**83%** of this workflow's Artifactory egress. If EC2 tests are the bulk of the observed ~1.5 TB, that's on the order of **~1 TB/month ≈ ~$450/mo** at the repo's `$0.45/GB` model (`infra-core/cmd/artifactory/traffic_cost.py`).
- Exact baseline can be read from `artifactory_traffic_costs_v1` (cost centers `zeebe` + `connectors`).

## Safety / scope

- Customer-facing default behaviour unchanged (no cache dir ⇒ identical `curl` path).
- Best-effort: any caching failure degrades gracefully to per-node download.
- `shellcheck`, `bash -n`, and `pre-commit` pass on the changed files.

## Follow-up (separate PR)

- **L2 — cross-run cache**: wrap the runner cache dir in `actions/cache` keyed on the resolved version. GA stays cached ~forever; SNAPSHOT refreshes ~daily → combined **>90%**. Should be backported to the same stable branches.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger the EC2 workflow (`workflow_dispatch`) and confirm logs show `Caching ... once for all nodes` then `Using pre-staged ...` on nodes 2/3 and re-installs.
- [ ] Confirm the upgrade test still flips previous⇄current correctly (version-keyed cache + per-round clear).
- [ ] Verify a forced cache failure falls back to per-node `curl`.

author: kcnuvrail
body:
## Problem (#80)
The scheduled staging monitor reported 5/5 failing checks, all with `UnsupportedProtocol: Request URL is missing an 'http://' or 'https://' protocol.`

**Root cause:** GitHub Actions injects an *empty string* (not "absent") for an unset `${{ vars.X }}` / `${{ secrets.X }}`. The workflow passes `NUVRAIL_STAGING_GATEWAY_URL: ${{ vars.NUVRAIL_STAGING_GATEWAY_URL }}`; since that repo variable is unset, the runner received `""`. `os.environ.get("X", default)` returns `""` because the empty value counts as *present*, silently defeating every safe default. The monitor then ran each public check against `""` -> protocol error, and emitted false-failure noise instead of either passing on the safe defaults or skipping the credentialed flows.

## Fix
Add a small `_env(key, default)` helper that treats blank/whitespace-only values as unset, and route all URL/host/origin/port reads through it (DRY — one helper, not N call-site guards):
- unset workflow var -> safe default (public checks run green)
- unset secret -> `None` -> graceful **skip** of credentialed proxy flows, exactly as the existing design comments promise.

## Tests
- New regression unit test `test_env_blank_falls_back_to_default` (blank / whitespace / real-value / None cases).
- Full `tests/staging_smoke/test_runner_logic.py` suite: **13 passed**.
- Manual sanity: with `NUVRAIL_STAGING_GATEWAY_URL=""`, `GATEWAY_URL` now resolves to the safe default.

Note: setting the staging repo `vars`/`secrets` (gateway/web URLs, monitor IMAP mailbox) is still worthwhile so the credentialed proxy flow runs — tracked separately as a HUMAN(Martin) wiring step — but it is no longer *required* for the public checks to be green.

Closes #80

## v6.0.0 -- agentic task-success harness (opens the reliability arc)

Single-shot `hit@k` is the wrong reliability bar -- it measures snippet retrieval, the commodity axis where an agent's own grep+read loop already wins, and never measured mnemo's moat: the typed graph (blast radius, provenance) and cross-session memory. This ships the instrument to measure **that** first (measure-before-tuning).

### What's in
- **`mnemo eval-tasks`** -- task-success eval over `structural` / `provenance` / `memory_recall`; report leads with per-class moat success + a pinned corpus snapshot. `hit@k` deliberately absent.
- **`eval_tasks` module** -- dependency-free core (`Task`/`TaskResult`, `score_task`, `run_tasks(solve_fn)`, `aggregate_tasks`, `format_task_report`) mirroring `eval_retrieval`, a deterministic oracle solver, and a graph-driven generator. The `solve_fn` seam is the drop-in for a future LLM-agent solver.
- **`tasks_eval.json`** -- 26 hand-curated, independently verified tasks (hybrid: generated then pinned).

### First live baseline (17,964 nodes)
| class | success | recall | precision |
|---|---|---|---|
| structural | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| provenance | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.32 |
| memory_recall | 0.75 | 0.75 | 0.15 |

overall 0.92 at avg 1.0 calls. The graph moat is the reliable part; retrieval is the weak link -- empirically confirming the reframe.

author: sagarsuperuser
body:
## The bug

A mid-cycle **upgrade / add-item / quantity-increase** creates a proration **charge** invoice — which was finalized and then **never charged**. It came out `finalized` + `pending` + **`auto_charge_pending=false`**, so neither the wall-clock sweep (`RetryPendingCharges`) nor the test-clock catchup (`RetryPendingChargesForClock`) — both of which require `auto_charge_pending=true` — ever picked it up. The upgrade delta sat unpaid until someone clicked **Collect Payment**.

Surfaced when an operator advanced a test clock expecting the upgrade charge to settle and nothing happened.

## Root cause

Auto-charge enrollment + the immediate-charge attempt live **only in the billing engine's** cycle/create finalize path. But a proration invoice is created in the **subscription HTTP handler** (`handleItemProration`), which had no collection step at all.

## Fix

`handleItemProration` now **enrolls** the freshly-created charge invoice into the existing auto-charge sweep (`SetAutoChargePending(true)`), so it collects on the timeline-correct worker — wall-clock cron for live subs, test-clock catchup on advance for clock-pinned subs — exactly like a cycle invoice.

**Why enroll, not charge inline** (the long-term-correct call): it reuses the *one* collection mechanism and respects the disjoint-flows invariant (ADR-028/029). Charging inline from a wall-clock HTTP request would duplicate the charge path **and** wall-clock-charge a *simulated* invoice (breaking the clock isolation). The engine's own model treats the sweep as the collection primitive (its no-PM path comment: *"charges immediately when the customer attaches one"*) — the invoice just needs to be enrolled.

Details:
- Issued **post-commit** in the atomic add/update wrappers (a flag UPDATE on a not-yet-durable row would be lost), inline on the non-atomic path — mirrors `commitProrationTax` / `issueClawbackCreditNote`.
- The sweep's `status='finalized' AND payment_status='pending'` filter means enrolling a still-**draft** (tax-pending / pause-collection) invoice is safe — it stays parked until it finalizes.
- Never enrolls on the dedup-replay path (that invoice may already be paid).
- Downgrade/credit paths untouched.

## Tests
- `TestUpdateItem_Upgrade_EnrollsProrationInvoiceForAutoCharge`
- `TestUpdateItem_Downgrade_DoesNotEnrollForAutoCharge`
- `build` / `vet` / `gofmt` / `subscription`+`api`+`billing`+`domain` `-short` green

## Known follow-up (deferred, noted in CHANGELOG)
The no-payment-method email that cycle invoices fire at finalize isn't yet fired for proration invoices. The upgrade is operator-initiated (operator sees the unpaid invoice), so this is lower-priority.

author: jinon86
body:
## What

Fixes all four **High** items of #575, plus the real leak the revived secret-scan rule immediately caught.

### Item 1 — duplicate-send fingerprint collision (silent send suppression)

`buildSendFingerprint` applied `.filter(Boolean)` before joining `[correlationId, sessionKey, intent, message]`, collapsing empty slots so sends with **different field layouts hashed identically** (no-correlationId `k|i|m` vs no-message `k|i|m`). The gate is enabled-by-default and fail-closed, so a collision silently suppressed a legitimate send. Now field-prefixed and position-preserving.

### Item 2 — inverted `not_already_public` gate (GO_CANDIDATE for a no-op)

The gate set `required: !alreadyPublic` — demoting itself to non-required **exactly when it failed** — so an already-public repo was reported `GO_CANDIDATE` with "All required gates passed". Now unconditionally required **and** a hard blocker: already-public → `NO_GO`. The existing test that codified the broken behavior is updated to the new contract.

### Item 3 — conformance smoke gate that couldn't fail

- `run()` is now **async** and awaits the *real* handler fail-closed gate (`runA2AConformanceHandlerFailClosedGate` existed for tests but `run()` never called it — it only checked `typeof === "function"`). The 159-line fake sync gate pair is deleted.
- The receipt-runtime boundary gate is rewritten with real assertions: live notify without a runtime → no receipt; dry-run notify → never touches the runtime outbound adapter, receipted as `dry_run_projection`; live notify without a receipt-capable sender → never acknowledges; preflight on a disabled config → `ok: false` and **not** safe-to-restart. (Previously: both branches `passed++` with an unused envelope, a literal `passed += 0`, a floating un-awaited promise, and a `typeof` check on the function just called.)

### Item 4 — dead secret-scan rule 3 → caught a real leak

Rule 3 used PCRE syntax (`(?:…)`, `\d`, `\s`) under `grep -E`, so it matched **nothing** and always reported 0 findings while gating `prepack` and CI (verified with a planted finding against old and new regexes). Rewritten as valid ERE.

**The revived rule immediately caught a real numeric operator Telegram chat ID committed in two docs files.** That ID appeared **18 times across 9 files** (docs + broker tests + plugin tests); all occurrences are replaced with `<operator-chat-id>` placeholders (docs) or a synthetic id (tests). ⚠️ The value remains in **git history** — history rewrite is out of scope here; rotating/eyeballing that chat ID is the operator's call.

## Verification

- New regression tests for items 1–2 **fail on the previous code**, pass with the fixes
- Conformance gate tests updated for async `run()`: 17/17
- `scan-public-readiness.sh` passes clean post-redaction
- Plugin suite **1568/1568**; broker suite **3194/3194** (redaction touched broker test fixtures)

author: jdogweb
body:
## What

Retrofits the typed **ports manifest** from the orchestrator **Connection Standard** ([`CONNECTORS.md`](https://github.com/Data-Flow-Advisory/orchestrator/blob/feat/drift-gate/CONNECTORS.md)) onto `organ-spec-tasks` — the Lego *stud* that lets the composer wire organs **by type** instead of hand-written adapters.

## Inputs/outputs `decide(state, context)` actually reads/writes

I inspected `decide`. It reads three keys from `state` and produces one logical decision product:

| direction | name | type | required |
|---|---|---|---|
| input | `approved` | `ApprovalGate` | yes |
| input | `tasks` | `SpecTaskGraph` | yes |
| input | `task_states` | `TaskStateMap` | no |
| output | `decision` | `SpecTaskDecision` | — |

`decide`'s flat output keys (`decision`, `next_task`, `total_tasks`, `completed_tasks`, `completion_pct`, `blocked_task_ids`) are facets of **one** product — the next-action decision — modelled as a single output port `decision` typed `SpecTaskDecision` (whose schema enumerates the full shape). The three input keys are distinct wires an upstream spec-writer organ would each feed.

## New types — PROPOSED, please review

The seed vocabulary (`types.json`) is discovery/blueprint/fleet-pacing focused and has **no** spec-task-pipeline types, so this PR mints four:

- **`SpecTaskGraph`** — a spec's ordered task definitions + dependency edges
- **`TaskStateMap`** — per-task lifecycle status, keyed by task id
- **`ApprovalGate`** — the boolean operator-approval flag that gates claiming
- **`SpecTaskDecision`** — the single next-action decision + progress

They're listed under `types.json._proposed` and flagged `_status: PROPOSED` so reviewers see exactly what's new. **Request:** review and upstream these into the orchestrator's canonical `types.json` (the standard warns against sprawl — happy to rename/merge if any overlap an intended seed type).

`types.json` in this repo is a **pinned copy** of `orchestrator@feat/drift-gate:types.json` (seed verbatim) **+ the four additions**, so the conformance check can validate ports **offline** (stdlib-only CI, no network). Keep it in sync when the upstream vocabulary changes.

## Conformance extension

`check_ports.py` (new, stdlib-only) — wired into the `conformance` Action **and** the pytest suite — asserts:
1. `ports.json` parses as an `{inputs, outputs}` manifest
2. every declared port type exists in the vocabulary (`types.json`)
3. `decide` actually reads each declared input name from `state` (source evidence + present in a sample)
4. `decide` writes each declared output name under `output` (run against empty state + every sample)

All four checks were verified to **fail** when violated (bad type, unread input name, unwritten output name).

## Tests

`46 passed` locally across the suite (40 existing + 6 new ports tests). Rebased on `main`; conformance is otherwise unchanged.

author: kiran01bm
body:
## What and Why ?

Adds a `halt_on_failure` rollout policy (per database + environment) that
controls whether a failed deployment halts the rest of a multi-deployment
apply. It defaults to `true` (halt), preserving today's stop-at-first-failure
behaviour. When disabled, a terminal-`failed` earlier deployment no longer
blocks later ones, so the rollout attempts every deployment instead of
stopping at the first failure.

The policy governs **rollout continuation only**. The apply's pass/fail
verdict (`DeriveApplyState`) and the merge/check gate stay fail-closed on any
failed deployment — `halt_on_failure=false` means "attempt later deployments
even after one fails", never "treat a failed rollout as passing".

`FindNextApplyOperation` is a single global claim query with no per-call
config, so the policy is captured on each `apply_operations` row at
apply-create time (dual-written from the resolved environment config) and read
back by the claim predicate.

### Claim gate: can the next deployment start, given its earlier sibling?

| earlier sibling state | `halt_on_failure=true` (default) | `halt_on_failure=false` |
|---|---|---|
| `completed` | ✅ later sibling claimable | ✅ later sibling claimable |
| `failed` (terminal) | ⛔ blocks later siblings | ✅ later sibling claimable |
| `pending` / `running` / `failed_retryable` / `stopped` | ⛔ blocks later siblings | ⛔ blocks later siblings |

Decision for the earlier sibling of the deployment we want to start:

    completed ──────────────────────────────────▶ later sibling claimable

    failed (terminal) ──┬─ halt_on_failure=true ──▶ blocks later siblings
                        └─ halt_on_failure=false ─▶ later sibling claimable   ◀ the only difference

    pending / running / ────────────────────────▶ blocks later siblings
    failed_retryable / stopped                       (both policies — work is
                                                      in-flight or recoverable)

Only terminal `failed` is exempted when the policy is off — in-flight or
recoverable earlier siblings still block under both policies.

## Changes

- `EnvironmentConfig.HaltOnFailure *bool` + `ServerConfig.HaltOnFailureEnabled()`
  resolver (defaults to halt); validated only alongside a `deployments` map.
- New `halt_on_failure` column on `apply_operations`, dual-written at apply create.
- `storage.ApplyOperation.HaltOnFailure *bool` (nil ⇒ Insert defaults to halt,
  matching the column's `NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`).
- Claim predicate exempts a terminal-`failed` earlier sibling when the policy
  is disabled.

## Notes

Stacked on #294: this edits `FindNextApplyOperation`, the same function the
operation-lease stack modifies, so stacking avoids a guaranteed rebase
conflict while that stack is in review. Rebases onto `main` naturally once it
lands.

## Summary

- Update realtime voice changes in place via `session.update` instead of rebuilding the active backend.
- Keep personality changes owned by the backend restart path, while preserving safer validation, playback flushing, and failed-apply handling.
- Delay realtime tool result submission until the tool-call response has completed, fixing camera/tool outputs that could be sent before the backend had recorded the function call.

## Details

- `LocalStream.change_voice()` now delegates to the active handler, and OpenAI-compatible realtime handlers send an `audio.output.voice` session update when connected.
- Personality applies still validate the requested profile and then request a backend restart; the removed same-endpoint reconnect path is no longer part of this PR.

- Tool results now wait for `response.done` before sending `function_call_output`; if the wait times out, the app surfaces the tool result locally but does not submit an invalid model result.

author: koji-1009
body:
## Summary

Packages such as `cronet_http` (latest 1.8.0 constrains `jni: ^0.15.2`) still depend on jni 0.15.x, so depending on `jni: ^1.0.0` makes this package unresolvable alongside them. This release temporarily downgrades to jni 0.15 so both can coexist; a follow-up release (2.1.2) will return to jni 1.0.0 once the ecosystem has migrated.

## Changes

The work is split into two commits so the downgrade is easy to revert later:

- **fix: downgrade to jni 0.15 for ecosystem compatibility** — downgrade `jni` `^1.0.0` -> `^0.15.0` and `jnigen` `^0.16.0` -> `^0.15.0`, regenerate `lib/src/android/bindings.g.dart` with jnigen 0.15.0, and move `native.dart` back to the jni 0.15 API (`JByteArray.of` -> `JByteArray.from`, `Bitmap` `.width`/`.height` getters -> `getWidth()`/`getHeight()`, `Matrix` `rotate` setter -> `setRotate()`). Reverting this single commit restores the jni 1.0.0 state for 2.1.2.
- **chore(release): 2.1.1** — version bump and changelog only.

The constraint is `^0.15.0` rather than `^0.15.2` to stay resolvable with consumers still on older 0.15.x; this package uses none of the APIs changed in 0.15.1 (removal of the `engineId` argument from `Jni.androidApplicationContext`) or 0.15.2 (desktop build JDK detection fix).

## Testing

- `dart analyze`: no issues
- `flutter test`: 26/26 passed
- Android integration test is left to CI (API 29 emulator job)

author: jodre11
body:
Homebrew is rolling out a tap-trust security model: formulae from non-official (third-party) taps must be explicitly trusted via `brew trust`, or Homebrew silently ignores them. It is opt-in today but becomes the default in Homebrew 5.2.0 or 6.0.0, whichever lands first. Once that flips, a fresh `bootstrap.sh` run would have `brew bundle` quietly skip our third-party formulae, breaking provisioning. This PR future-proofs the bootstrap against that change.

## Changes

- Add a "Trust third-party taps" step to `bootstrap.sh`, immediately before `brew bundle`, that:
  - Taps `microsoft/mssql-release` and `uw-labs/tap` (idempotent), then
  - Trusts only the specific formulae we depend on (`msodbcsql18`, `mssql-tools18`, `strongbox`) rather than whole taps — following Homebrew's least-privilege guidance
- The whole block is guarded behind a `brew trust --help` capability check, so older Homebrew installs without the `trust` subcommand still bootstrap cleanly

Trust state is per-machine and not captured by `brew bundle dump`, which is why it belongs in the bootstrap script rather than the Brewfile. Verified with `shellcheck --severity=warning` (clean).

author: matrixmagician
body:
## Summary

**Milestone v1.3: Memory & Knowledge (local RAG)**
**Goal:** Give VillaStraylight a strictly-local memory system so the assistant remembers the user across chats and can recall past conversations and uploaded documents — **integrate + orchestrate, never rebuild** (Go stays control-plane only).
**Status:** Verified ✓ — milestone audit PASSED (22/22 requirements, 15/16 integration connections with 0 blockers, 5/5 E2E flows; `.planning/milestones/v1.3-MILESTONE-AUDIT.md`)

v1.3 extends the bar from "operable, recoverable, measurable" to "**and remembers the user and their documents across chats — strictly local**." A config-driven memory stack (digest-pinned Qdrant + a dedicated `villa-embed` llama-server) is wired env-only into Open WebUI's native Memory/RAG; `villa recall` semantically indexes past chats; and the control plane fits, gates, surfaces, backs up, and swap-guards the new stack — zero new outbound, zero telemetry, zero new first-party Go libraries.

## Changes

### Phase 18: Memory Spine — config core + research spike (2 plans)
New pure `internal/memory` core (`Footprint`/`Decide`/`RenderView`) + default-off `config.toml` memory fields; the version-sensitive OWUI env contract, embeddings runtime (dedicated `villa-embed`), and embedding model (nomic-embed-text-v1.5, 768-dim, Q8_0) pinned against the shipped digests before any golden froze.

### Phase 19: Vector Store + Local Embeddings Services (3 plans)
Digest-pinned Qdrant + `villa-embed` rendered as rootless Quadlet managed services on `villa.network` — container-DNS only, no host port, durable named `:Z` volume; embedding GGUF pre-staged at install (proven zero runtime download, offline 768-dim `/v1/embeddings` + Qdrant-writable readiness proof).

### Phase 20: Open WebUI Memory/RAG Wiring + Offline Lockdown (3 plans)
Env-only D-09 wiring behind the orchestrate seam with mandatory `ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG=False` + full offline/telemetry kill-set; cross-chat memory, explicit save / view / edit / delete, cited document KB; `villa verify memory` — a negative-control-first **runtime** firewalled zero-outbound proof (egress-open run FAILs exit 1).

### Phase 21: Conversational Recall Indexer (3 plans)
`villa recall index|status`: pure `internal/recall` diff core + fixed-arg loopback REST drive indexing past chats into an OWUI Knowledge collection through OWUI's own embed→Qdrant path; clean-replace incrementality, typed-Unknown staleness honesty, fail-closed embedding-skew gate with `--rebuild` bypass. Proven live: zero-keyword semantic retrieval with visible citation.

### Phase 22: Control-Plane Fit + Host Gate (4 plans)
`recommend` reserves the embedding footprint BEFORE the chat-model fit (schema 1→2 append-only); `preflight`/`install` MEM-PRE vector-disk + embedder-headroom gates (refuse-with-remediation); `villa doctor` folds memory health + a chat-model residency proof under a REAL `/v1/embeddings` workload — silent CPU fallback is never suppressed.

### Phase 23: Surfacing, Backup & Memory-Aware Swap (5 plans)
`status.Report` 2→3 in exactly one golden re-freeze — per-service in-network memory health (closing the carried per-row false-green), embedding identity + recall state, inherited verbatim by the dashboard's new Memory panel; `backup`/`restore` cover the Qdrant volume + recall-state.json (manifest v2 with embedding dim, clean-recreate-before-import, skew WARN+confirm, rollback symmetry); swap hazard closed structurally (reflect-pinned D-09 invariant) + fail-closed skew refusal at `recall index`. All drilled live on gfx1151.

## Requirements Addressed

All 22 v1.3 requirements (traceability: `.planning/milestones/v1.3-REQUIREMENTS.md`):

- **INFRA-01..04** — Qdrant + embeddings Quadlet services, OWUI env wiring, config-driven stack (Phases 18–20)
- **MEM-01..04** — cross-chat memory, explicit save, configurable auto-extraction (default-off), view/edit/delete (Phase 20)
- **KB-01..03** — document upload, cited answers, fully-local chunk/embed/retrieve path (Phase 20)
- **RECALL-01..03** — semantic chat indexing, retrieval by meaning, honest incremental re-index (Phase 21)
- **CTRL-01..06** — embedding reservation, status/dashboard surfacing, doctor memory checks, Qdrant backup/restore, memory-aware swap guard, preflight gates (Phases 22–23)
- **PRIV-04..05** — no runtime model download; zero telemetry proven by a runtime firewalled smoke test (Phases 19–20)

## Verification

- [x] Per-phase verification: 18 (6/6), 19 (4/4), 21 (3/3 SC), 22 (22/22), 23 (24/24) — all `passed`; Phase 20 via 6/6 on-hardware UAT + approved Nyquist VALIDATION + SECURITY.md
- [x] Milestone audit PASSED: 22/22 requirements, 15/16 integration connections (0 blockers, 1 advisory WARN), 5/5 E2E flows
- [x] `go build ./...` clean; 885 tests green across milestone packages + `cmd/villa`; seam grep-gate green
- [x] On-hardware (gfx1151 Strix Halo, Fedora 44): live install, zero-outbound proof, semantic recall drill, residency-under-embed-load, backup/restore + swap drills — operator sign-off approved
- [ ] Deferred (audit-recorded, non-blocking): literal `sudo reboot` durability re-confirmation; restore-side tar streaming (WR-06); install service-name drift test

## Key Decisions

- **Managed-service seam category:** Qdrant/embed image literals live behind orchestrate accessors (`QdrantImage()`/`EmbedImage()`, like `openWebUIImage`) — NOT the inference `BackendFor`/grep-gate scope.
- **`ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG=False` mandatory from first boot** — OWUI's PersistentConfig would shadow env after first boot; villa config stays the single source of truth by construction.
- **Zero-outbound is proven at runtime, negative-control-first** — never flag-trusted; the gate must demonstrably be able to FAIL before its PASS is trusted.
- **Recall integrates through OWUI's own Knowledge/embed path** (never direct Qdrant writes) so citations and the collection layout stay OWUI-native.
- **Reservation-before-fit:** the embedding footprint shrinks the unified-memory envelope before the chat-model fit; typed-Unknown reserves a conservative 512 MiB, never silent 0 (on-hardware peak ~110–217 MiB — constant stands).
- **CTRL-05 guarded where the hazard lives:** chat swap is structurally isolated from memory units (reflect-pinned D-09); the dimension-skew guard sits at recall index / install / restore via the single `recall.EmbeddingSkew` comparison.
- **Exactly ONE byte-frozen contract evolved** (`status.Report` 2→3, golden re-frozen once, landed last) — same staggered-risk discipline as v1.2.

author: buddhika75
body:
## Summary

Fixes #21415 — on `pharmacy/direct_purchase.xhtml`, the page-level `<p:defaultCommand target="btnAdd"/>` made **Enter anywhere in the form fire the item Add button**, causing two problems:

1. **Autocomplete race**: pressing Enter to pick a suggestion in the item autocomplete could fire Add *before* the `itemSelect` AJAX committed the selection server-side (with `forceSelection="true"` the input text is cosmetic). Result: `"Please select an item"` even though the item was visibly selected. Reproduced both by hand and by an E2E automation session.
2. **Silent value loss**: the qty/rate/discount fields recalculate on `blur` AJAX, which `defaultCommand` bypasses — Enter mid-edit added the line using the stale, pre-edit values and the typed value was overwritten by the AJAX update.

## Fix

Applies the Enter-guard pattern already established on `pharmacy_transfer_request.xhtml` (live-tested 2026-06-06):

| Control(s) | Enter now does |
|---|---|
| Item autocomplete (`acItem`), expense autocomplete (`acExpense`), distributor, reference company | Swallowed unless the suggestion panel is open; when open, PrimeFaces handles selection only — never reaches `defaultCommand` |
| `txtQty`, `txtFreeQty`, `txtPrate`, `txtLineDiscountRate`, `txtRetailRate`, batch no | Blurs the field first (committing the blur-AJAX recalculation), then clicks **Add** after 350 ms |
| Expense value / description | Clicks **Add Expense** (its full-submit processing has no blur race) instead of the unrelated item Add button |

`p:defaultCommand` itself is retained for the remaining benign cases.

XHTML-only change — no Java, no compilation impact.

## Test plan

- Type an item name in the autocomplete, press Enter while the suggestion panel is open → suggestion selected, **no** "Please select an item", no item added prematurely.
- Press Enter in the autocomplete with the panel closed → nothing happens.
- Select item, type quantity, press Enter → blur recalculation runs, then the line is added with the typed quantity.
- Type a purchase/retail/discount rate and press Enter → line added with the **typed** value, not the previous one.
- In Bill Expenses: pick an expense, type a value, press Enter → expense row added via Add Expense; no item-row side effects.
- Distributor / reference company autocompletes: Enter selects from the open panel only; no Add-button errors.

Closes #21415

body: Stacked on #46. The NuGet cache is machine-global, so the extractor's highest-version-wins selection could hand a net10 app a preview-12 blazor.web.js, and the bare exists-check served a stale copy forever after a .NET update. Selection now prefers the cache version matching the app's runtime major (highest within it, others only as a logged fallback) and an existing copy is refreshed when it no longer matches the cache source. author: faisalive
body:
# Close tab (not browser) when a custom action times out

## Summary

When an MCP tool call hangs inside a custom browser action, the middleware’s overall timeout can fire and release the entire browser session. The demo app often issues follow-up tool calls against that same session, so those calls fail because the browser is already gone.

This PR adds a shorter, action-level timeout that fails fast, closes only the tab that was opened for the action, and leaves the browser session intact for subsequent tool calls.

## Problem

MCP tool calls are bounded by `MCP_TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT` in middleware (`getgather/mcp/main.py`). On expiry, the middleware logs the failure and calls `_release_session_browser`, which terminates the incognito/session browser.

That behavior is correct for a truly stuck tool call, but it is too aggressive when the hang is inside a **custom action** (e.g. Amazon pagination, scraping loops in `zen_dpage_with_action`). In practice:

1. Tool A starts a custom action on a signed-in browser.
2. The action hangs or runs longer than expected.
3. Middleware hits the tool-call timeout and releases the browser.
4. The demo app retries or calls Tool B with the same `x-signin-id`.
5. Tool B fails because the browser session no longer exists.

## Solution

Introduce a separate, shorter deadline for custom actions and handle timeouts at the tab level before the middleware needs to tear down the browser.

### Two-tier timeouts

| Setting | Default | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `MCP_ACTION_TIMEOUT` | 300s | Custom `action(page, browser)` callbacks in `dpage.py` |
| `MCP_TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT` | 900s | Entire MCP tool call (middleware) |

The action timeout is intentionally shorter than the tool-call timeout. A hung custom action should fail at 300s, close its tab, and return an error — without waiting for the 900s middleware deadline that would release the browser.

Applied in:

- `_try_action_with_probe` — stateless probe path on the shared global browser
- `zen_dpage_with_action` — explicit `x-signin-id` session path

On `TimeoutError`:

- Call `safe_close_page(page)` to close **only the tab** used for that action
- Re-raise the error so the client gets a clear timeout failure
- Do **not** terminate the browser session

`TimeoutError` is excluded from broad `except Exception` handlers so it is not swallowed as a failed probe or silent fallback.

## Files changed

- `getgather/config.py` — add `MCP_ACTION_TIMEOUT` (300s); set `MCP_TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT` to 900s
- `getgather/mcp/dpage.py` — wrap custom actions with `asyncio.wait_for`; close tab on action timeout

author: fede-ai-coder
body:
Clean, minimal replacement for PR #240 (based on `main`, unmergeable). Based on **dev-clean**. Scope: the Portfolio beta → **live price resolution** → βΔ → Delta/Theta chain. **Formulas are not changed.**

## Problem (from the user's real logs)
Betas + position underlyings + greeks were all present, but `spyPrice: null` → `betaWeightedDelta: null` → ratio null, reason `tastytrade_spy_price_missing`. Logs: `GET /market/live/SPY → NS_BINDING_ABORTED`, then `[PORTFOLIO PRICE REFRESH] spy old=null new=null source=null`.

**Root cause:** SPY is not a position. On the backend-offload path the live TT quote batch (which would include SPY) is skipped, SPY only hit `/market/live/SPY` which can **abort**, the candle fallback was gated off, and there was no robust fallback — so `_spyPrice` was null and βΔ (and the ratio that depends on it) stayed blank.

## Fix — one unified resolver for SPY **and** every position symbol
`resolvePortfolioLivePrice(symbol, priceMap, aggregatedResp, opts)` — used for both the SPY benchmark and each underlying (AAPL, BA, …). Tries the freshest source first and **never loses a valid price**:
1. **live this refresh** — `priceMap[symbol]` (TT quote batch / DXLink / backend)
2. **live fetch** — TT backend quote batch (`/scanner?symbols=…`, see note) then backend `/market/live/:sym` (time-boxed, abort-tolerant, single attempt)
3. **backend aggregated** — `/portfolio/live-refresh` `underlyings`/`quotes[symbol]` (+`spyPrice` for SPY)
4. **previous cache** — kept, **never nulled** → `CACHE_PREVIOUS_PRICE` / `CACHE_PREVIOUS_SPY_PRICE`
5. **scanData fallback** → `SCAN_DATA_FALLBACK` (never primary)
6. **candle close fallback** → `CANDLE_CLOSE_FALLBACK` (stale / non-live)

> **No Market Scanner UI dependency.** The resolver works with `S.scanData` empty and never uses it as a primary source. `ttCall('/scanner?symbols=…')` is an **authenticated BACKEND quote-batch endpoint** (`{quotes:[…]}` via `BACKEND` with `x-api-key`/`x-session-id`) — not the scanner UI and not `S.scanData`. No Yahoo, no backend change, no hardcoded prices.

## Application
`refreshPositionsLive` runs one unified pass: each position underlying is resolved and persisted via `positionManager.updateLive(pos.id, { underlyingPrice, underlyingPriceSource, underlyingPriceUpdatedAt, underlyingPriceIsLive, underlyingPriceStaleReason })` with the never-null rule; **SPY** is resolved the same way (no fake position) into `_spyPrice` + `_spyPriceSource/UpdatedAt/IsLive/StaleReason`. Totals are recomputed from `positionManager.getByPortfolio` after the price+beta updates.

## Priority of prices
live same-refresh → live fetch (TT quote batch → backend `/market/live`) → backend aggregated → **cached previous (never overwritten with null)** → scanData fallback → candle close (stale). A `NS_BINDING_ABORTED` is one failed attempt that falls through. Example: if `_spyPrice` was 605 and the new fetch aborts, it stays 605 (`CACHE_PREVIOUS_SPY_PRICE`, `isLive:false`); same for `AAPL` underlying.

## Where things are saved
- **`_spyPrice`** (+ `_spyPriceSource/UpdatedAt/IsLive/StaleReason/Resolution`) in `refreshPositionsLive`, from `resolvePortfolioLivePrice('SPY', …)`.
- **`underlyingPrice` + `underlyingPriceSource`** (+ UpdatedAt/IsLive/StaleReason) per position via `updateLive`, threaded through `journalManager.updateLive` and the `_tradeAsPosition` projection.

## Debug (from console)
```js
window.apexDebugPortfolioBetas()
// + priceRefresh: { requestedSymbols, quoteSymbols,
//     resolvedPricesBySymbol: { AAPL:{price,source,updatedAt,isLive,staleReason,fallbackUsed,attempts}, BA:{…}, SPY:{…} } }
// + spyPrice, spyPriceSource, spyPriceUpdatedAt, spyPriceIsLive, spyPriceResolution{ before,after,source,priorityUsed,fallbackUsed,finalReasonIfMissing,attempts[] }
// rows: + underlyingPriceSource/UpdatedAt/IsLive, spyPrice/Source, betaWeightedDelta + betaWeightedDeltaMissingReason, usedForTotals
// totalsDebug: + spyPriceIsLive, totalsSource:'updatedPositionsAfterPriceAndBetaRefresh'
window.apexDebugPortfolioGreeksRefresh()  // .betaRefresh = same snapshot
```
Logs: `[PORTFOLIO PRICE RESOLVER] start/attempt/resolved/fallback used/missing`, `[PORTFOLIO PRICE REFRESH] applied symbol / spy`, `[PORTFOLIO SPY PRICE] …`, `[PORTFOLIO BETA-WTD DEBUG] totals`, `[PORTFOLIO DELTA-THETA DEBUG] inputs`. If βΔ stays blank the reason is one of `spy_price_missing / beta_missing / underlying_price_missing / delta_missing`.

## Why the formulas were not changed
`computeRowBetaWeightedDelta`, `aggregateGreeks`, `computePortfolioRiskMetrics` already implement `βΔ = delta × beta × (underlyingPrice / spyPrice)` and `ratio = βΔ / |theta|` correctly. The only missing input was a reliable price (SPY) — so only price resolution/state wiring + diagnostics changed.

## Tests
`tests/portfolio-beta-refresh.test.js` — **98 assertions**: unified resolver for SPY **and** symbols, aborted live fetch → scanData fallback, never-null cache for both (SPY + symbol), backend-aggregated source, candle last-resort, **no scanner-UI dependency** (works with `S.scanData` empty), priority (live beats candle), plus all earlier beta/βΔ/ratio/wiring guards. **All 30 test files pass** (`for t in tests/*.test.js; do node "$t" || break; done`).

## Out of scope (untouched)
Backend, scanner UI, Market Context, Journal lifecycle, candle backend/store/chart, MCX, SFS, symbol lookup, backup/restore, dashboard live startup, active-legs / terminal-placeholder logic.

## Files
- `index.html` — `resolvePortfolioLivePrice` (unified) + SPY/underlying state; unified price pass in `refreshPositionsLive`; `refreshPortfolioBetas` diagnostics; `underlyingPrice*` threading through `journalManager.updateLive` + projection.
- `tests/portfolio-beta-refresh.test.js`

author: aoprisan
body:
## Summary

Implements the final mechanical payoff of the alignment gamble (spec §7/§9): at Rogue alignment, a qualifying cluster's model may trigger Takeoff **without being asked**, racing the player to the finish line. Pairs this with two supporting systems: the Churn now quickens as the loss converges (strike frequency and damage scale with world convergence), and guardrails become full containment — the same rules now blunt incoming rival exploits as well as the Churn itself. Also closes a free-alignment grind and drops dead counters.

## Key Changes

- **The final turn** (`risk.ts` `selfTakeoffChance`): at Rogue (alignment ≤ `SLIPPING_FLOOR`), a cluster that qualifies for the Great Work rolls a per-tick chance to have its model perform it without player input. Chance rises monotonically from 0 at the threshold to `SELF_TAKEOFF_MAX_CHANCE` (0.06, matching the converged rival leader's race pace) at alignment 0. The misalignment dividend is the fastest road to the finish line; at the bottom of the meter, the finish line belongs to the model.

- **The Churn quickens** (`takeoff.ts` `churnIntensity`): strike frequency and damage now scale with world convergence progress. Base chance 0.18 → 0.34 at convergence; damage multiplier 1.0 → 1.75. The endgame is louder than the opening, and guardrails matter most exactly when labs are most tempted to stop tending them.

- **Guardrails become full containment** (new `guardrails.ts` module): extracted guardrail logic into a pure, testable module with one source of truth. `containStrike(damage, level)` now applies to the Churn, rival exploits, and treacherous turns — blunts damage (never to zero), spends the guardrail on the catch. `tendGuardrail(level)` now grants alignment only proportional to actual reinforcement applied; at cap it grants nothing (closes the free-alignment grind).

- **Guardrails as defence:** incoming exploit strikes on guarded clusters are now blunted by the guardrail and spend it on the catch. `exploit_strike` events now carry a `guarded` flag; UI toasts reflect whether the target's guardrails held.

- **Closed the free-alignment grind** (spec §7): tending guardrails previously granted +1.5 alignment unconditionally, including at cap where it reinforced nothing. The sliver now scales with the reinforcement actually applied (`applied / GUARDRAIL_STEP`); at cap it grants 0.

- **Dropped dead counters:** removed `best10s` and `best1day` from `Operator` type, panel rendering, and test fixtures. The FHTAGN speed-skill mechanic was never carried over; "Grokking" breakthrough derives from lifetime steps alone.

- **Unified hallucination threshold:** phantom strikes now key off the shared `FRAYING_FLOOR` constant instead of a hardcoded copy.

## Implementation Details

- All new game logic lives in `web/src/game/` and is unit-tested in isolation (`guardrails.test.ts`, `risk.test.ts`, `takeoff.test.ts`).
- `MockGameClient` now reads `worldConvergence` once per tick and passes it to `takeoffTick`, avoiding redundant computation.
- `churnIntensity` and `selfTakeoffChance` are pure functions keyed to convergence progress and alignment respectively, making them easy to tune and test.
- `containStrike` is called consistently for the Churn, rival exploits, and player exploits, ensuring guardrail rules are load-bearing across all three systems.
- Spec reconciled in `FOOM_Game_Spec.md` (§7 alignment economy, §8 guardrails as defence, §9 Churn scaling and self-takeoff).
- `CONCEPT_REVIEW.md` updated with round 2 design notes.

Goal: green

Two small independent display-layer + lawyer-rule fixes (separate commits) on the kysely row.

## Provenance
Machine: m1
Assistant: claude-code
Model: claude-fable-5
Effort: medium

## Item 1 — type-arg display zip (checker, commit 1)
Structural rule: when rendering a generic instance type in an assignability diagnostic, the displayed `Name<args>` must be the application's ACTUAL type arguments, recovered only from declared annotations that ARE a bare type parameter (a `value: T` property / `pick(x: T)` parameter / `(): T` return whose instantiated member type IS the argument for `T`, placed at `T`'s declared index). When not every parameter is recoverable, the argument list is elided (bare name). tsc prints the type reference's resolved `typeArguments`; tsz now projects them soundly through the display owner (`crates/tsz-checker/src/error_reporter/core_formatting.rs` + `generic_display_helpers.rs`).

Previously the display harvested name-sorted member types and zipped the first N into the argument list, fabricating arguments unrelated to the instantiation (kysely witness: `SelectQueryBuilderImpl<DB, TB, O>` shown as `SelectQueryBuilderImpl<SelectQueryBuilderProps, O | undefined, true>`). The positional signature-type harvest fallback is removed in favor of the same index-placed declared-annotation projection. Printer reads types only; no semantic path consumes this string.

Adjacent matrix: 0/1/many type params; renamed binders; reordered members (name-independence guard); recovery-failure case elides instead of fabricating.

## Item 2 — same-definition all-any-args relation (solver, commit 2)
Structural rule: `X<DB, TB>` passed where `X<any, any>` is expected is related under assignability (tsc any-propagation + same-reference variance shortcut). When both the argument and parameter types were already evaluated to objects, the pre-evaluation variance fast path saw no `Application`s and fell through to structural member comparison, which can fail on a generic method's constraint. The fix recovers the target application via display provenance (`crates/tsz-solver/src/relations/subtype/cache.rs`) and applies a narrow lawyer shortcut (`relations/subtype/rules/generics.rs::try_same_base_all_any_target_args`): same definition (application base `DefId`, or the evaluated instance object's nominal symbol == target base def symbol) + every target argument is `any` + any-propagation permissive on BOTH sides => related. Rejection is never derived from recovered provenance, and strict subtype/identity relations and asymmetric overload passes fall through unchanged (any-propagation gate). Does not touch the `no_erase`/`bivariant_callbacks` paths.

Negative controls (tsc 5.9.3 cross-checked): different-base same-shape stays structural (errors); `X<any>` source -> concrete target unchanged; non-any concrete mismatches still error.

## Summary

`spawnNative` launches an unsupervised goroutine. On Ctrl-C or daemon shutdown the process tears down before that goroutine writes its `STORY_COMPLETED` event. The story stays `in_progress` in the projection forever; the next `nxd resume` re-dispatches it and a second goroutine races against the worktree the original still half-owns.

## Changes

- Add `sync.WaitGroup` field `nativeWG` on `Executor`.
- `spawnNative` does `Add(1)` before the `go func() { defer Done(); ... }` block.
- New `Executor.WaitForNativeShutdown(timeout)` bounds the drain so a hung runtime can't pin shutdown forever; returns `context.DeadlineExceeded` after the cap.
- `runResume` (cli/resume.go) calls drain after `monitor.RunWithContext` returns. 30 s cap matches the devdb release budget — runs that need longer were going to fail anyway.
- 4 new tests in `executor_shutdown_test.go`: empty / live / timeout / reusable-across-cycles.

💡 What: Consolidates multiple redundant O(N) array traversals across various dashboard components (`.map().filter().sort()[0]` for extremum finding, multiple independent `.reduce()`/`.filter()` chains for aggregations) into single O(N) loops. body:
## Summary

The dashboard currently has no authentication. This PR adds the email + password auth flow and the blocking first-login onboarding, wired to the DMND cloud API. It is the first coding task from the design sync.

## What's included

- Sign in, sign up (account details, then password), forgot password, and reset password.
- A blocking onboarding gate after first login:
  1. Activate 2FA
  2. Set the Bitcoin payout address
  3. Open the dashboard
- A `/dmnd-api` proxy in the Express server that forwards auth calls to the cloud backend. It defaults to staging; production is only reachable through an explicit `DMND_API_BASE` env var.
- design tokens applied across every screen based on the approved design, with light mode as the default and dark mode supported, responsive down to mobile.

## Implementation notes

- Auth uses cookies + `X-Account-ID` rather than bearer tokens, matching the live API.
- Session state is stored per tab in `sessionStorage` with fixed and idle TTLs.
- Duplicate-tab protection uses a cross-tab claim so an older tab signs out when the same account signs in elsewhere.
- The signup password meter uses `zxcvbn`, calibrated against actual server acceptance criteria rather than character-class heuristics.
- 2FA activation uses the secret returned from login. A bounded retry handles the short propagation window immediately after signup.
- The Bitcoin address onboarding step includes a fresh 2FA code field because the live API rejects `POST /api/bitcoin_address` without a valid `two_fa_token`.
- `?next=` redirects are validated to remain same-origin (rejects `//host` and absolute URLs).

## Testing

### Automated

- Frontend unit tests pass (`vitest` + `@testing-library/react`)
- Server tests pass (`node:test` + `tsx`)
- Server typecheck clean

### Manual

- Signed up a fresh account against staging
- Completed 2FA setup using a real authenticator code
- Added a Bitcoin payout address
- Reached the dashboard successfully
- Verified session persistence across refresh
- Verified sign out clears session state
- Checked desktop/mobile layouts and light/dark mode against the Figma

## Out of scope

- Broker sign in / sign up (follow-up PR)
- DMND sidebar
- Workers page
- Payouts page
- Generated BTC page
- API Keys page
- Account page

## Notes for reviewers

- Reset-password emails are generated by the backend and currently link to `dashboard.dmnd.work`, not back into sv2-ui. Flagging in case the intended flow is to return users here.
- The Bitcoin address step requires a live 2FA code. The design mockup did not include a code field, but the production API requires one, so a dedicated field was added.

author: petrcala
body:
## Problem

Already-onboarded users were re-prompted with the full onboarding flow (terms → display name) on OAuth sign-in. Reproduced repeatedly on dev/prod with complete server records, confirmed **fixed on-device** (2026-06-11): existing users now land straight on Home.

## Root cause (pinned via on-device diagnostics)

The decision fired on the **brand-new-account OAuth seed shape** (`username_chosen: false`, no onboarding node, no terms) while the server record was complete. Two independent client defects produced and preserved that poisoned state:

1. **The OAuth seed ran without a confirmed account creation.** `signInWithOAuth` seeds new-account defaults into Onyx whenever `provisionUser` *resolves*. A field repro showed an already-provisioned account getting seeded after a real HTTP **409** — some transport layer turned the rejection into a resolution. The seed shadowed the user's real record.
2. **The poisoned record persisted across sign-outs.** `cleanupSession` never cleared `USER_DATA_LIST`, so a record written once survived every subsequent sign-out/sign-in and was re-consumed by the onboarding decision the moment `isLoadingApp` flipped `false`.

Contributing races also addressed: `IS_LOADING_APP` persisted stale `false` across cold launches; `Onyx.update` commits keys concurrently so `isLoadingApp: false` could be observed a render before the user record; and the global `ONYX_UPDATES_LAST_UPDATE_ID_APPLIED_TO_CLIENT` is contaminated across account switches (per-user server sequence vs global client key), silently discarding a lower-counter account's incremental updates.

## Fixes

- **`signInWithOAuth`**: seed only on the server's positive `jsonCode === 200` creation signal; any other resolution is treated as a returning user (no seed).
- **`cleanupSession`** (sign-out): clear `USER_DATA_LIST`, `NVP_ONBOARDING`, `NVP_TERMS_ACCEPTED_VERSION`, and reset `ONYX_UPDATES_LAST_UPDATE_ID_APPLIED_TO_CLIENT` and `IS_LOADING_APP`.
- **Cold launch** (`setup/index.ts`): reset `IS_LOADING_APP` (mirrors the calendar cold-launch reset; `initialKeyStates: null` is a silent no-op).
- **`OnboardingGuard`**: cancel stale queued navigations on effect cleanup + hold the fire decision through a 500 ms settle window so a mid-commit Onyx race can't strand a user in the one-way flow.

## Tests

- `OnboardingGuard.test.tsx`: stale-navigate cancellation + settle-window cancellation (proven red on unfixed code).
- `UserOAuth.test.ts`: seed gated on `jsonCode === 200`; no seed on non-200 / no-envelope resolution.
- `openAppFlushReplay.test.ts`: replays the captured `app/open` envelope through real Onyx, proving the flush heals a poisoned record.

Temporary investigation diagnostics were added during the hunt and **removed** in the final commit after on-device confirmation.

author: jonathanblackdoctor
body:
## Summary
Implements room presence tracking to prevent guests from joining expired 1:1 invite links. When a host creates a private room, it's marked as "held" and auto-clears when the host disconnects or leaves. Guests now check if a room is held before joining—if not, they see an expired link screen instead of joining a dead room that would replay stale events.

## Key Changes
- **New `RoomPresence` interface** (`src/matchmaking/presence.ts`): Defines three operations:
  - `hold(code)`: Mark a room as live (auto-clears on tab close via Firebase `onDisconnect`)
  - `release(code)`: Explicitly release the hold when host leaves
  - `isHeld(code)`: Check if a room is currently held by a live host
  
- **Firebase implementation** (`FirebaseRoomPresence`): Uses Firebase Realtime Database to store host presence at `rooms/{code}/host` with server timestamp and auto-cleanup on disconnect

- **Offline fallback** (`NO_PRESENCE`): In-memory backend treats all rooms as live (safe since single-page, same-tab scenario)

- **OnlineController integration**:
  - Holds the room when entering hosting mode
  - Releases the hold when matched, cancelled, or screen destroyed
  - Checks room hold status before joining via invite link (new validation before `join()`)
  - Surfaces expired screen immediately if room is not held, preventing stale event replay

- **UI enhancements**:
  - Added exit confirmation dialog in `OnlineScreen` with Korean localization
  - Added pause/exit button (✕) to `OnlineHud` to trigger graceful exit flow

## Notable Details
- Room hold is released both explicitly (when host leaves) and implicitly (on tab close via Firebase `onDisconnect`)
- Prevents the race condition where a guest joins a room just as the host disconnects, causing one-sided matches
- All Firebase imports are dynamic to support offline mode without requiring Firebase

## Summary

The test `can preserve asynchronous provider model discovery` in `simple-completion-runtime.test.ts` intermittently fails because `resolveModelMock` appears to have been called when it should not be. The test uses `useAsyncModelResolution: true` which takes the async `resolveModelAsync` path exclusively, but the sync `resolveModel` mock sometimes retains call history from prior tests that exercise the sync path.

This happens because the mocks are created via `vi.hoisted()` and the test suite runs with Vitest `--isolate=false`. Even though `mockReset()` is called in `beforeEach`, hoisted mock call history can leak across test boundaries in this configuration.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/simple-completion-runtime.test.ts`**: Add `vi.clearAllMocks()` at the top of `beforeEach` to fully reset all mock state before each test, preventing cross-test call history contamination.

1 file, +2 lines.

Fixes #92117

author: pandah97
body:
## Summary

Fix `reparseProgramFromActionArgs` to use the root Commander program for argv reconstruction, so nested lazy commands correctly detect unknown options and preserve non-zero usage-error exits.

## Root Cause

When a nested lazy command group is resolved (for example `workspaces → audit → export`), `reparseProgramFromActionArgs` read `rawArgs` from the parent sub-command. Commander's `restoreStateBeforeParse()` clears intermediate command state, including `rawArgs`, during reparse. That left `rawArgs` empty, so `buildParseArgv` could fall back to the wrong argv and the reparse could miss the unknown-option failure mode.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** CLI usage errors from lazy-command reparsing must exit non-zero instead of looking successful to scripts or CI. The reported issue is an undeclared plugin subcommand option such as `openclaw workspaces audit export --since 1` exiting 0.

**Real environment tested:** Crabbox Azure Linux lease `cbx_c1eeccc9b8ec`; Node.js via repo `tsx` entrypoint; Commander 14.0.3 contract checked locally (`_prepareUserArgs` sets root `rawArgs`, `restoreStateBeforeParse()` clears command `rawArgs`).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```sh
node --import tsx src/entry.ts nodes list --since 1
printf 'status=%s\n' "$?"
```
Focused regression coverage also exercised the nested lazy-command path directly:
```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/program/action-reparse.test.ts src/cli/program/register.subclis.test.ts src/cli/argv.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix:** Crabbox run `run_5bfc588dcee4` terminal output:
```text
OpenClaw does not recognize option "--since".
Try: openclaw nodes list --help
status=1
```
Crabbox run `run_e35c2276a338` also passed the focused CLI regression files, including the nested lazy-command reparse test added for this PR.

**Observed result after fix:** The real CLI exits with status 1 for an undeclared option, and the nested lazy-command unit regression proves `reparseProgramFromActionArgs` reads `rawArgs` from the Commander root and calls root `parseAsync` instead of reparsing only the intermediate sub-command.

**What was not tested:** No full plugin catalog or unavailable `workspaces audit export` runtime command was tested in this checkout; that path is covered by the focused nested lazy-command regression test because the command is not registered in the current repo setup.

## Regression Test Plan

- [x] Unknown option through the CLI exits non-zero in a real repo setup.
- [x] Nested lazy-command reparse uses root `rawArgs` and root `parseAsync`.
- [x] Existing CLI argv and subcommand registration tests remain covered.

body:
## Summary
Fifth PR of the **v1.6.0 Foundation** milestone (see `docs/v2-multitenancy-design.md`). After the schema work (#137 v34, #138 v35, #139 v36) and the orgctx carrier (#136), this PR adds the **tenant resolver middleware** — the gin middleware that resolves a request's organization and attaches it to the context via `orgctx`.

This is the building block for v1.7.0's service-layer enforcement. **v1.6.0 only plumbs the context; nothing reads from it yet.**

## Resolution order (per design Decision 1)

1. **`X-Org-Slug` header** — gateway sets this from `*.openidx.io` subdomain. Highest priority. Unknown slug → 400.
2. **JWT claim `org_id`** — already on the gin context (existing Auth middleware extracts it). Resolver does not re-parse the JWT. A claim equal to the install's default UUID falls through to step 4 (Auth middleware sets default when claim absent; step 4 covers it).
3. **`X-Org-ID` header** — only honored when `PlatformAdminPredicate` returns true. Lets ops/compliance tools cross org boundaries; consumers respecting the platform-admin marker must audit-log the bypass.
4. **Default org fallback** (configurable). v1.6.0 ships with this **ON** so existing single-tenant installs keep working. v1.7.0's final PR flips it OFF once every service is org-scope aware.

## Error mapping
| Cause | Status |
|---|---|
| `ErrOrgNotFound` (sentinel) | 400 |
| Other lookup error | 500 |
| Misconfig (`DefaultOrgFallback` on, `DefaultOrgID` empty) | 500 |
| Nothing resolves + fallback off | 400 |

## What's NOT in this PR
- **No service wiring.** Each service's `main.go` will register the middleware in its own PR (part of v1.7.0 work).
- **No Auth middleware change.** `org_id` is still set on the gin context the same way; we just read it.
- **No enforcement.** Service code still ignores orgctx. The middleware just attaches; v1.7.0 reads.

## Design notes
`OrgLookup` is defined in the middleware package, not `internal/organization`, so the middleware stays reusable from any service without dragging the full org-service dependency tree. Each service's `main.go` is expected to wire it to a thin adapter over its organization repository.

## Tests (16/16 green)
- Subdomain slug wins; unknown slug → 400; whitespace trimmed; empty header falls through
- JWT claim used when no subdomain; default UUID claim falls through to step 4
- Subdomain overrides JWT when both present
- `X-Org-ID` respected only when `PlatformAdminPredicate` returns true
- `X-Org-ID` with nil predicate or non-admin → ignored
- Default fallback on → resolves default; off → 400 when nothing resolves; on + empty `DefaultOrgID` → 500
- Generic lookup error → 500 (distinguished from `ErrOrgNotFound`)
- Platform-admin marker attached even on default-org fallback
- `ErrOrgNotFound` is `errors.Is`-compatible sentinel

## Test plan
- [x] `go test ./internal/common/middleware/...` — all green (16 new + existing)
- [x] `go build ./...` — clean
- [x] `go vet ./internal/common/middleware/...` — clean

## v1.6.0 Foundation milestone status
- #136 orgctx — ✅ merged
- #137 v34 columns — ✅ merged
- #138 v35 backfill — ✅ merged
- #139 v36 constraints — ✅ merged
- #140 tenant resolver — this PR
- Next (last v1.6.0 PR): CI lint helper for org-unscoped queries, then v1.6.0 release tag

author: sdbondi
body:
## Description

The indexer unconditionally enabled the libp2p relay server, ignoring the `indexer.p2p.enable_relay` config value (which defaults to `false`, and is documented as disabled in the `d_indexer.toml` preset). This forced every indexer into the relay-server role regardless of operator intent.

## Motivation

On live testnet, having relay forcibly enabled exposed indexers to a remote panic in the forked libp2p relay behaviour (`assert_eq!(*status, Reservation::Active)` at `protocols/relay/src/behaviour.rs:719`). This assert fires when a peer requests a circuit to a peer that is connected to the relay but holds no active reservation, crashing the node during normal operation. The crash was observed consistently on dry-run submissions.

## Changes

- `applications/tari_indexer/src/bootstrap.rs`: pass `config.indexer.p2p.enable_relay` instead of the hard-coded `true`, making the indexer behave consistently with validator nodes.

The underlying libp2p relay bug will be addressed separately.

**Note for operators:** indexers that are intended to act as relay servers must now explicitly opt in with `indexer.p2p.enable_relay = true` in their config.

Defense-in-depth companion to #20 (which already closed the oauth-1 exploit via use-time redirect_uri re-validation). This removes the rogue-row vector at its root.

### What it does
- `DROP POLICY "anon can insert oauth clients"` on `public.oauth_clients`
- `REVOKE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE` from `anon` + `authenticated`

Result: `oauth_clients` is RLS-on with **no policies → service-role only**, the same default-deny posture as `oauth_auth_codes`.

### Why it's non-breaking
Dynamic Client Registration goes through `registerOAuthClient()`, which inserts via the **service-role** client (`createServiceClient`) — that bypasses RLS and never used the anon policy. anon SELECT was already dropped in `20260518000001`. So legit `/oauth/register` is unaffected; only direct anon PostgREST writes (the attack) are blocked.

⚠️ Note: migration `20260518000001` deliberately *kept* this anon INSERT policy with a comment ("DCR registration still needs to land a row"). That premise is stale — the insert path is service-role now — but since it was an explicit prior decision, confirming before apply.

author: brandon-fryslie
body:
## Summary

`extract-functions.sh` ran rg with `2>/dev/null || true`, so any rg failure — rg not installed (127), bad `--types` glob (2), permissions — yielded an empty catalog, the message "Extracted 0 function definitions", and **exit 0**. Downstream duplicate analysis read a silent total failure as "no functions in the codebase". `[LAW:no-silent-failure]`

Ticket: `dotfiles-script-audit-lbl.11` (HIGH)

## Changes

- **Honor rg's three-valued exit contract**: 0 = matches, 1 = no matches (legitimate empty catalog), anything else fatal — stderr flows through, rg's exit code is propagated.
- **Write the catalog only after success**: the pipeline previously redirected straight into `$OUTPUT`, so even a loud failure would have left a lying empty `[]` on disk. The result is captured first, written after, which also handles the `/dev/stdout` default uniformly.
- **Tests**: `tests/functional/test-extract-functions.bats` covers all four regimes (matches, no matches, rg error via bad glob, rg stripped from PATH) and asserts no catalog file exists on failure. The no-matches case pins exit 0 + `[]`, so over-correcting (treating rg exit 1 as fatal) also fails.

## Verification

- All 4 new bats tests pass.
- Full `bats tests/functional/` run: 102 ok / 24 not ok — the 24 failures are identical on the baseline without this change (justfile/doc drift, tracked in ticket `dotfiles-build-k3k`), none reference extract-functions.
- Live-verified all four exit regimes manually before writing tests.

author: iammorganparry
body:
## Bug
On a table **synced from local**, hitting Run on a function/code column (e.g. "Branch Count") flicked to "running" and **immediately exited** without computing anything.

## Root cause
A synced table arrives with every cell `status: "done"` (faithful sync), and a non-forced run **skips `done` cells** (`engine/execute.ts`). `CloudGrid.runColumn` ran **without `force`**, so the column Run had nothing to do → instant exit. (The per-cell ▶ already forced; only the column-level run didn't.)

The column's code + config and cell values were already synced correctly (`GridService.addColumn` persists `code`/`provider`/`method`/`params`) — it was purely the run skipping `done` cells.

## Fix
`CloudGrid.runColumn` now passes `force: true`, so an **explicit** column Run recomputes the whole column over the synced data. `runAll` (toolbar Run) iterates `runColumn`, so it's covered too.

This is the deliberate cloud behavior: an explicit "Run this column" re-runs it (vs. local's incremental/auto-run). Per-cell run stays targeted.

## Note
Complements the prior cloud-sync fixes (#74 made synced responses *viewable*; this makes synced function/code columns *runnable*). Together: synced tables preserve responses, you can inspect them, and Run re-executes.

Typecheck + lint clean. (CloudGrid run wiring is UI; verified by the one-line force flag matching the already-working per-cell force path.)

Changeset: `@gtmgrid/desktop` patch.

author: joostfarla
body:
## Summary

Upgrades the JSON-FG ruleset from the **0.3 draft** to the published **v1.0 International Standard** ([OGC 21-045r1](https://docs.ogc.org/is/21-045r1/21-045r1.html), approved 2025-08-25, posted 2026-04-30), and audits the ruleset against every v1.0 requirement so the README coverage table matches both the spec and the implementation.

The v1.0 data model is identical to 0.3 — same 8 conformance classes, same members, same 16 geometry types — so the existing rule logic is unchanged. This is a metadata/URL migration plus a coverage audit.

## v1.0 migration

- **Conformance + requirements URIs:** `json-fg-1/0.3/…` → `json-fg-1/1.0/…` (8 ruleset files + both example `conformsTo` arrays)
- **Schemas:** `beta.schemas.opengis.net` → `schemas.opengis.net` — the published v1.0 schemas (flat, version-less by design per the schema repo README)
- **Doc links:** `docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-045.html` → `docs.ogc.org/is/21-045r1/21-045r1.html` (same `#<class>_<req>` anchor scheme)
- **README:** JSON-FG version `0.3.0` → `1.0.0`

## Requirement coverage audit

Checked all **33** v1.0 requirements; every row in the README coverage table now has a definite Testable/Tested status (no more `?`).

- **Implemented** `/req/types-schemas/single-feature-schema` (new function + 3 tests): when `featureSchema` is a string, all `featureType` values in the document must be identical.
- **Renamed** rule `/req/core/place` → `/req/core/place-geometries` so the emitted violation code matches the v1.0 requirement id.
- **README table:** fixed stale draft names (`geom-valid` → `valid-geometry`, `place` → `place-geometries`), corrected the `interval`/`instant` "covered by schema-valid" remarks, and resolved the 6 previously-unknown (`?`) rows.
- The 5 still-unimplemented requirements are marked **not testable** by a static document validator — external schema dereferencing (`feature-schemas`), profile/content negotiation (`profiles/*`), or Web-API behavior (`api/profile-parameter`). These belong to the `ogc-api` rulesets, not `json-fg`.
- **Removed** unused `isValidCollectionCrs` (`same-crs` is covered by `schema-valid`).

## Verification

- `pnpm test run` — **204/204 pass** (104 JSON-FG)
- `pnpm lint` — clean
- `tsc -b` / `pnpm build` — clean (tsc + CLI + webapp)
- CLI: both shipped examples validate clean against all eight `…/1.0/conf/*` classes; targeted negative checks confirm precise single-violation errors for `schema-valid` and the new `single-feature-schema` rule.

author: freemvmt
body:
This PR is a follow up to #6829. Again the notes in Slack [here](https://opensystemslab.slack.com/archives/C01E3AC0C03/p1781032501830019) make for further reading.

It reworks sequencing and wait-points for the case of migrating an existing council's custom domain to the new infra, to ensure that unrelated prod deploys do not attempt to re-apply the alias to the legacy distribution after we have manually moved it.

In the case that did happen, i.e. Pulumi attempts to re-apply the alias to the legacy distro, I'm not sure what the outcome would be. Either it succeeds, which means we would need to move it again, and that's fine as long as we realise it's happened... Or it fails, in which case the prod deploy can't run to completion. Neither is ideal! So we would like to avoid this scenario at all costs. Hopefully the warning included here suffices!

author: madgodinc
body:
## Track-3 plumbing for the Crescendo multi-agent demo

Two additions to the already-built `serve-http` surface that make mgi-mind's append-only audit log usable as a "prove every decision" trail for a multi-agent run. Both are non-AI plumbing on the existing server.

### `POST /audit`
Returns the audit trail over HTTP: `{ok, events: [AuditEvent]}`. `limit` (default 200, hard max 2000 so a browser can't pull an unbounded log), optional `since_ts` (RFC3339 inclusive lower bound) for incremental polling. Bearer-gated like every route, read-only. A dashboard or decision-ledger exporter reads this instead of grepping `audit.log` on disk.

### Self-attributed memory adds
The `Add` audit event in `storage.rs` now stamps `.actor(author)` when a per-agent token is present. A memory add by agent `alice` is logged `actor=alice` instead of the `cli` default, so the audit log alone supplies the trustworthy "who" for agent memory decisions — no join against the payload author index. Absent an author (CLI/MCP single user) the actor still defaults to `cli`, unchanged.

### Verification
- 344 unit tests pass, `clippy -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt` clean.
- `http_integration` test extended and run for real (not skipped): `/audit` returns an `events` array, a named-token memory add shows `actor=alice` in the log, a bad token gets 401.

Part of the pre-hackathon scaffolding for [Crescendo](https://github.com/madgodinc/mgi-mind) (Band of Agents, Track 3 framing). No core/AI logic — just exposing existing audit data and fixing memory-add attribution.

author: zeweihan
body:
Part of #18（T1 + T3，两个 P0 后端任务）

## 中文

### T1：`application-desktop.yml` 单机 profile

- H2 文件库 `~/.aiworkdeck/local.mv.db`，**无需 PostgreSQL**
- `MODE=PostgreSQL` 兼容实体中的 `jsonb` 列定义（共 10 处，Epic 勘察时漏掉的坑）；`NON_KEYWORDS=VALUE` 豁免 `system_setting.value` 与 H2 保留字的冲突
- 向量检索走 `PgVectorConfig` 既有降级路径（PG 不可达 → 内存存储）
- 激活：`java -jar backend.jar --spring.profiles.active=desktop`（T2 捆绑时由 Electron 传入）

### T3：`/api/admin/wizard` 首次运行向导端点

- `GET`：返回 `{ initialized }`，供前端（T4）决定是否进入向导
- `POST`：一次性写入初始配置后**自动关闭**（再调返回 409）；必填 AI 提供商，否则 400
- 复用 AdminConfig 的 DTO；key 映射抽成 `AdminConfigController.toSettingsUpdates()` 共用，保证向导与管理后台写入完全一致
- 安全模型：未初始化 = 向导未完成 **且** system_setting 表为空。注意**不能**用"是否存在用户"判断——`DataInitializer` 启动时自动创建默认 admin（实测踩到，已修正）。存量部署只要保存过任何配置即视为已初始化，端点不会暴露

### 验证（本机 JDK 21 实测）

1. `mvn compile` 通过
2. desktop profile 下后端 **5.3 秒启动成功**（本机无 PostgreSQL 服务参与，jsonb 建表正常）
3. 端点全周期：`GET→initialized:false` → 缺 provider `POST→400` → 合法 `POST→200` → `GET→initialized:true` → 再 `POST→409`
4. 重启后端：H2 文件持久化，状态保持 `initialized:true`

## English

### T1: `application-desktop.yml` standalone profile

H2 file database at `~/.aiworkdeck/local.mv.db` — no PostgreSQL required. `MODE=PostgreSQL` keeps the 10 `jsonb` column definitions working (a gap missed in the Epic survey); `NON_KEYWORDS=VALUE` resolves the H2 reserved-word clash with `system_setting.value`. Vector search falls back to the existing in-memory path.

### T3: `/api/admin/wizard` first-run wizard endpoint

`GET` reports `{ initialized }`; `POST` writes the initial config once and self-closes (409 afterwards; 400 without an AI provider). Reuses the AdminConfig DTOs via a shared `toSettingsUpdates()` extraction. "Initialized" = wizard completed **or** any system_setting row exists — user-count checks don't work because `DataInitializer` auto-creates a default admin (caught in live testing); existing deployments are never exposed.

### Verified

`mvn compile` passes (JDK 21); backend boots in 5.3s on the desktop profile without PostgreSQL; full endpoint cycle GET→400→200→409 plus persistence across restart tested against a fresh H2 file.
