body:
## What this does

Adds a Shellcheck CI workflow and fixes the shell scripts so the tree passes it.

This revives #1431 by @yarikoptic, which went stale against `3.x`. The scripts have drifted since then, so the changes are re-derived against the current tree rather than a replay of the old diff.

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/shellcheck.yml`: installs shellcheck and runs it on every tracked file that starts with a shell shebang or a shellcheck directive. Matches the repo conventions (`actions/checkout@v5`, `ubuntu-24.04`, same branch triggers as `test.yml`), with `permissions: contents: read`.
- `scripts/dev-test.sh`: `uv run pytest $@` to `"$@"` (SC2068, real argument re-splitting bug).
- `scripts/release.sh`: shebang `#!/bin/sh` to `#!/bin/bash` (SC3040, `pipefail` is undefined in POSIX sh) and legacy backticks to `$(...)` (SC2006).

## Note on the file selection

The original detection also matched `src/pyinfra/connectors/util.py`, a Python file that embeds a `#!/bin/sh` heredoc as a string. Shellcheck cannot parse that file as shell and errors out, which would fail CI. The workflow grep now excludes Python files (`':!*.py'`), so only real shell scripts are checked. The earlier `build-public-docs.sh` SC2086 fix from the original PR is no longer needed: that script was rewritten upstream and is already clean.

## Verification

- `git grep -l '...' -- ':!*.py' | xargs shellcheck` exits 0 over all matched files.
- Workflow YAML parses, and both edited scripts pass `bash -n`.

author: gilbert09
body:
## Problem

The Airtable data warehouse source was scaffolded (registered with `unreleasedSource=True` and an empty stub) but had no sync logic, so users couldn't pull their Airtable bases into PostHog.

## Changes

Implements the Airtable import source following the warehouse source architecture (`source.py` / `settings.py` / `airtable.py` split):

- **Endpoints:** `bases` (meta API listing), `tables` (per-base schema fan-out), and `records` (per-base × per-table fan-out) against `api.airtable.com/v0`, authenticated with a personal access token (legacy API keys were disabled by Airtable in Feb 2024). The required PAT scopes (`data.records:read`, `schema.bases:read`) are listed in the caption per the skill's scope-documentation rule.
- **Parent-key injection:** table rows carry `_base_id` and record rows carry `_base_id` + `_table_id`, because record ids are only unique within a table — records use the composite primary key `(_base_id, _table_id, id)`.
- **Incremental sync:** `records` only, via the server-side `filterByFormula=IS_AFTER(CREATED_TIME(), "…")` filter on the `createdTime` field that record payloads actually carry. This is honest append-only incremental (catching updates to existing records requires a full refresh, since records expose no last-modified field to track as a watermark).
- **Pagination/rate limits:** opaque `offset` tokens per page chain. These expire after a few minutes of inactivity, so this is a `SimpleSource` — persisting them across worker restarts would hand back dead cursors. Requests are spaced for the 5 req/s per-base limit, and 429 retries start above Airtable's 30-second post-429 cooldown.
- 401/403 registered as non-retryable with scope guidance. All HTTP goes through `make_tracked_session()` with the token redacted.
- Removes `unreleasedSource` and ships as `releaseStatus=ALPHA`; regenerates `AirtableSourceConfig`; moves airtable to the Implemented table in `SOURCES.md`.

Airtable webhooks expire after 7 days of inactivity and need refresh churn, so pull-only is the right starting model.

## How did you test this code?

Automated tests only (no live Airtable credentials):

- `posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/airtable/tests/test_airtable.py` — transport: offset-token pagination, base→table→record fan-out with parent-key injection, CREATED_TIME formula construction, skip-tables-without-ids, credential validation status mapping, per-endpoint `SourceResponse` metadata incl. the composite record pk. Request spacing patched out in tests.
- `posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/airtable/tests/test_airtable_source.py` — source class: config fields, schemas (records-only incremental), non-retryable error matching, argument plumbing.
- Registry-level tests in `posthog/temporal/data_imports/sources/tests/` pass (58 tests total).

Endpoint behavior (meta API paths, offset semantics, formula filtering, rate limits) was verified against Airtable's Web API docs; live-API smoke testing wasn't possible without credentials, hence the alpha release status.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

author: hetchy-app[bot]
body:
## What & why

Members who belong to two (or more) WorkOS organizations previously had to fully log out and log back in just to reach the AuthKit organization picker — the only place the active org can be chosen. That is needless friction for anyone who works across orgs.

This adds a **"Switch organization"** item to the profile-avatar dropdown. It points at a new `/switch-org` route handled by `auth.SwitchOrgHandler`, which re-enters the hosted AuthKit flow with `prompt=login`. That re-presents the sign-in screen and, for multi-org users, the organization picker; the selected org returns through the existing `/callback`, which seals a fresh session bound to the chosen `org_id`. The link is only shown to users who actually belong to more than one organization, so single-org users aren't offered an action that would just silently sign them back into their only org.

## Why re-use the AuthKit round-trip

The app deliberately keeps no local list of a user's org memberships (WorkOS owns those), so it cannot render an in-app picker without a new membership-listing round-trip. Re-using the hosted AuthKit picker is the same surface users already see at first login, keeps the experience consistent, and avoids storing membership state locally. The handler is registered next to `/login`, `/signup`, and `/logout` and behaves identically to `/login` (it only arms a signed OAuth-state cookie and 302s to AuthKit), so it introduces no new auth/CSRF/open-redirect surface — the actual session mutation still happens at the state-gated `/callback`.

## Changes

- `internal/auth/auth.go` — new `SwitchOrgHandler` that delegates to the existing `redirectToAuthKitWithInvitation(..., promptLogin=true)` path, plus a `See also: SwitchOrg` cross-reference.
- `internal/auth/members.go` — new `UserHasMultipleOrgs` that lists active WorkOS org memberships filtered by `user_id` and short-circuits after the second row.
- `internal/bot/web.go` — register `/switch-org`.
- `internal/bot/web_pages.go` — populate a `MultiOrg` template var on the chat page (errors are swallowed → treated as single-org so a transient WorkOS hiccup hides the link rather than breaking chat).
- `internal/webui/templates/app.html` — gate the "Switch organization" item behind `{{if .MultiOrg}}` and add a divider before "Log out".
- `internal/auth/auth_test.go` — tests for the redirect behaviour and for `UserHasMultipleOrgs` (multi/solo/none + bypass).

## Validation

The change was rebuilt and the app restarted before probing. `make prepush` is clean (format, golangci-lint 0 issues, build). `go test ./internal/auth/ ./internal/webui/` passes, including the new `UserHasMultipleOrgs` tests (which also assert the `statuses=active` filter is sent to WorkOS).

Menu gating proof — left: the live single-org (AUTH_BYPASS) user's dropdown has **no** "Switch organization" item (only User settings, Organization settings, divider, Log out), confirmed both in the screenshot and by `curl /` returning HTML without the link. Right: rendering the actual embedded `app.html` template with `MultiOrg=true` shows "Switch organization" present, with a divider separating it from "Log out".

![Switch organization gating: single-org vs multi-org](https://hetchyhq-pr-attachments.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/org_01KRVBSPVP03GWP0Y7BMSTS3YM/1226012207/5fb3bd69-0705-4411-bcea-d0724310ec29/followup-dj6823q0vrf9/screenshot-000.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Checksum-Mode=ENABLED&X-Amz-Credential=AKIAY6YUC67TZM5YOLMF%2F20260611%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260611T123419Z&X-Amz-Expires=604800&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-id=GetObject&X-Amz-Signature=7dcc3c1d75b42cc62455b362fbdd2794ff667023b62d33814ef879b304bc672e)

| Check | Input | Expected | Observed | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Multi-org gating | user in 2+ active orgs | link shown, divider before Log out | shown (see screenshot, right) | ✅ |
| Single-org gating | user in 1 active org | link hidden | hidden (live screenshot left + `curl`) | ✅ |
| Zero-org gating | user in 0 active orgs | link hidden | hidden (unit test) | ✅ |
| Bypass mode | `UserHasMultipleOrgs` bypass | false → link hidden | matches (live app + unit test) | ✅ |
| Real-auth redirect | `SwitchOrgHandler` w/ WorkOS client | 302 to `…/authorize?…prompt=login` + state cookie | matches | ✅ |
| Bypass redirect | `SwitchOrgHandler` bypass mode | 302 → `/` | matches | ✅ |

The live AuthKit org-picker screen itself is not exercisable in the sandbox (WorkOS auth is bypassed via `AUTH_BYPASS=1`, with no live multi-org tenant); the redirect target, `prompt=login` parameter, and multi-org membership count are covered by unit tests against a mocked WorkOS memberships endpoint instead.


### Update — cache `UserHasMultipleOrgs` (latest [low] review comment)

`indexHandler` serves the SPA catch-all and called `UserHasMultipleOrgs` on every page render, making a WorkOS membership round-trip each time just to gate the link. This commit memoizes the result per user in a short-TTL (5 min) in-process cache on `auth.Service` and caps the membership listing at `Limit=2`, so single-org users no longer incur a wasted WorkOS call per render while membership changes are still picked up once the cached entry expires.

Proven by unit tests against a mocked WorkOS server (`go test ./internal/auth/...`, also under `-race`): `TestUserHasMultipleOrgsCaches` asserts a second call within the TTL serves from cache with zero WorkOS requests and that a call at the expiry boundary re-fetches; `TestUserHasMultipleOrgs` now also asserts `limit=2` reaches WorkOS. An independent code review of the diff returned no findings above LOW severity (mutex usage, TTL boundary semantics, and `Limit *int` pagination wiring all confirmed correct). The cache path cannot be exercised through the live app because `AUTH_BYPASS=1` makes `UserHasMultipleOrgs` return `false` and short-circuit before the cache; the live smoke screenshot below only proves the SPA render path that calls this function is intact (`/healthz` → 200, `/` → 200 on the rebuilt binary).

| Scenario | Expected | Observed | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First call, single-org user | WorkOS queried once, returns false | 1 request, false | ✅ |
| Second call within TTL | served from cache, no WorkOS request | 1 request total | ✅ |
| Call at expiry boundary (now == expires) | treated as expired, re-fetch | 2nd request issued | ✅ |
| `limit` query param sent to WorkOS | `limit=2` | `limit=2` asserted | ✅ |
| SPA home render after restart | renders, no regression | HTTP 200, link absent for single-org | ✅ |

![Agent SPA home render after the cache change (single-org bypass user, no Switch organization link)](https://hetchyhq-pr-attachments.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/org_01KRVBSPVP03GWP0Y7BMSTS3YM/1226012207/5fb3bd69-0705-4411-bcea-d0724310ec29/followup-dj68irlgxrpm/screenshot-000.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Checksum-Mode=ENABLED&X-Amz-Credential=AKIAY6YUC67TZM5YOLMF%2F20260611%2Fus-west-2%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20260611T125605Z&X-Amz-Expires=604800&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&x-id=GetObject&X-Amz-Signature=c7b65b58042d5257bf77db3de5dd329bbf81d72c89fce0584d7b6221921e5304)


Two follow-up commits keep CI green without changing the observable behavior above: `indexHandler`'s membership lookup was extracted into a small `userHasMultipleOrgs` method behind a test seam (mirroring the existing `followUpModeFn` pattern) with unit tests for both the multi-org and WorkOS-error paths, restoring `internal/bot` coverage above its required threshold; and the cache's read path now takes a `sync.RWMutex` read lock so concurrent page renders don't serialize on a warm entry. Both the `Test` and `review` checks pass on the final commit (`go test ./...` and the automated review), with only INFO/LOW advisory notes remaining.

author: jakechampion
body:
## What

Lowers the `for (k, v) in m` map-destructuring loop on the IR path,
completing the map read/traversal surface (after `get`/`has`/`get_or`,
`keys`/`values`).

This is a **pure `irlower` change** — no new IR ops and no backend edits.
It reuses the `map_keys` / `map_values` ops (from the keys()/values()
slice) plus the existing counted-loop, array-length, and array-index ops.

## How

The desugar snapshots `keys()` and `values()` into two hidden locals
once, then runs the same counted loop the `for x in arr` lowering uses,
binding `k = keys[i]` and `v = values[i]` each iteration:

```
ks = m.keys();  vs = m.values();  i = 0
loop { if !(i < ks.len()) break;  k = ks[i];  v = vs[i];  <body>;  i = i + 1 }
```

The two snapshots share iteration order on every backend — the live
parallel arrays on x86-64/arm64, and the probe-order snapshot on wasm
where `map_keys` / `map_values` walk the same slots — so `keys[i]` pairs
with `values[i]`.

The snapshot locals are deliberately **not** array-marked: on
x86-64/arm64 they alias the map's internal arrays (a borrow, no inc), so
the exit-sweep must not `dec` them; `arr_len` / `arr_get` are emitted
explicitly so they don't depend on the mark. `k` / `v` carry string-ness
(`mark_str`) for downstream dispatch when the key / value type is string.

## Tests

forkv sum-of-values (60), sum-of-keys (6), a pairing-sensitive `k*v`
reduction (20 — kept < 126 so it's a valid wasm exit code), and a
string-key variant (8), across the three differential suites, the
x86-64 absolute-exit oracle, and the wasm emit oracle.

Green locally: full x86-64 + wasm self-host oracle + IR-path suites +
fixpoint, and the complete arm64 IR differential suite.

## Map surface status

With this, the IR path covers the full map read/traversal API:
`map_new`, `insert`, `len`, `get`, `has`, `get_or`, `keys`, `values`,
and `for (k, v)` iteration. Next up is **i64** — the highest-leverage
remaining gap, since the compiler's own data structures use it
pervasively.

author: cybuletz
body:
## Problem

The dedicated app was collecting **0 responses** even when the Google Form had real responses.

Root cause: `ResponseCollector` was using the **Google Sheets API** (`spreadsheets().values().get()`) to read responses from a linked Sheet. But:
- No Sheet is ever linked to these forms (no "Link to Sheets" was clicked in the Forms UI)
- So every collect call returned empty rows → 0 responses

## Why the VS Code agent worked

The original `tools/survey/collect_responses.py` on `main` uses the **Google Forms API** directly:
```python
service.forms().responses().list(formId=form_id)
```
This works immediately — no Sheet required, no Drive lookup, no fallback chain.

## Fix

### `pm-toolkit/core/response_collector.py`
- Completely rewritten to use `forms().responses().list(formId=form_id)` — identical approach to the working VS Code agent
- Builds a `questionId → title` map from `forms().get()` to produce human-readable answer keys
- Drops all Sheets API and Drive API dependencies (`self._sheets`, `self._drive`, `get_linked_sheet_id()` removed)
- `collect(form_id)` now takes a **form ID** directly (not a sheet ID)

### `pm-toolkit/ui/survey_panel.py`
- `_collect_for()` simplified: calls `collector.collect(form_id)` directly — no intermediate sheet resolution step
- `_format_single()` updated to include `respondent_email` from the Forms API response
- Output message updated to reference the History tab instead of the CLI script

## No breaking changes
- `_SCOPES` already includes `forms.responses.readonly` — no OAuth re-auth needed
- `survey_store.py` unchanged — `sheet_id` field stays as `""` (unused)
- All existing survey history records continue to work as long as `form_id` is present

body:
feature: liste des concours

### Description

L'application permet déjà de créer un concours. Il est nécessaire de pouvoir afficher la liste des concours créés.

A partir de la page d'accueil, l'utilisateur doit pouvoir accéder à une page listant tous les concours créés grâce à un bouton "Liste des concours".

Sur la page de liste des concours, tous les concours créés doivent être affichés.
Chaque concours doit être présenté avec sa date, son lieu et son organisateur. Les concours doivent être triés par date décroissante (du plus récent au plus ancien). Si aucun concours n'a été créé, un message indiquant "Aucun concours disponible" doit être affiché.
Chaque ligne de la liste doit avoir une dernière colonne avec des boutons d'action permettant de consulter les détails du concours, de le modifier ou de le supprimer. Ces fonctionnalités seront développées dans des tâches ultérieures. Les boutons d'action doivent être présents mais inactifs pour le moment.
La page de liste des concours doit aussi avoir un bouton "+" permettant de créer un nouveau concours. Lorsque l'utilisateur clique sur ce bouton, il doit être redirigé vers le formulaire de création d'un concours.

### Use Cases

1. En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux accéder à une page listant tous les concours créés depuis la page d'accueil.
2. En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux voir les informations de chaque concours (date, lieu, organisateur) dans la liste des concours.
3. En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux que les concours soient triés par date décroissante dans la liste des concours.
4. En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux voir un message indiquant "Aucun concours disponible" si aucun concours n'a été créé.
5. En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux voir des boutons d'action (gérer supprimer) pour chaque concours dans la liste des concours, même s'ils sont inactifs pour le moment.
6. En tant qu'utilisateur, je veux pouvoir cliquer sur un bouton "+" dans la page de liste des concours pour être redirigé vers le formulaire de création d'un concours.

### Expected Changes (optional)

- ajout d'un bouton "Liste des concours" sur la page d'accueil
- ajout d'une page de liste des concours accessible depuis la page d'accueil
- affichage de tous les concours créés sur la page de liste des concours avec les informations suivantes : date, lieu, organisateur
- affichage d'un message "Aucun concours disponible" si aucun concours n'a été créé
- ajout de boutons d'action (gérer, supprimer) pour chaque concours dans la liste des concours, même s'ils sont inactifs pour le moment
- aucune modification du modèle de données n'est nécessaire pour cette fonctionnalité

### Acceptance Criteria (optional)

- [ ] la page d'accueil présente un bouton "Liste des concours"
- [ ] la page de liste des concours affiche tous les concours créés avec les informations suivantes : date, lieu, organisateur
- [ ] les concours sont triés par date décroissante dans la liste des concours
- [ ] si aucun concours n'a été créé, la page de liste des concours affiche un message "Aucun concours disponible"
- [ ] chaque concours dans la liste des concours présente des boutons d'action (gérer, supprimer) même s'ils sont inactifs pour le moment
- [ ] la page de liste des concours présente un bouton "+" permettant de créer un nouveau concours et redirige vers le formulaire de création d'un concours lorsqu'on clique dessus
- [ ] la documentation utilisateur est mise à jour pour inclure les nouvelles fonctionnalités

author: teetangh
body:
## What

PR-2 of the train (stacked on #854). Read-path fixes for 100s–1000s of concurrent users, driven by a 3-agent RCA over frontend/backend/DB — every agent claim was re-verified against live routes before acting (two were refuted: events `count()` was already parallelized; search already had `s-maxage`).

### Security fix found during live verification (commit `fcf52b62^..`)

**Ownership filter silently dropped for sessions with a missing profile id.** Prisma ignores `undefined` in where clauses, so `consultantProfile: { id: undefined }` matched **every** consultant's consultations/subscriptions on the collection GETs — verified leaking cross-consultant rows (requester PII) with a real session. Root cause chain: the seed never wrote the denormalized `User.*ProfileId` columns the session layer reads (29/30 consultants + 40 consultees desynced in dev). Fixed with the participants-route `?? "__none__"` idiom on both GETs, the seed now syncs the columns, and the 76 dev rows were repaired. Item routes were already fail-closed.

### Perf fixes

- **Requests tab**: deleted `/api/dashboard/consultant/[id]/requests` — six unbounded datasets with 4-level includes, prefetched on every dashboard load, **zero data consumers** (page bound it to `_requestsData`, never read; the tab self-fetches paginated `/api/events/*`). Page renders the tab immediately — one loading phase instead of two.
- **Planner**: webinar participant counts computed in-memory from already-fetched rows (was a second identical query); duplicate profile fetch removed; slot users slimmed to display fields. Verified live.
- **Availability** (#309 live half): `removeBookedSlots` include filtered to candidate times (was unbounded — 200-slot subscriptions returned all 200 rows per picker request); `Cache-Control: s-maxage=15, swr=60` — a popular consultant's day costs one origin hit per 15s.
- **Participants routes**: display-field selects, waitlist cap 500 + truncated flag, DELETE no longer loads the whole roster, rate limiters added (had none).
- **Events routes**: `user: true` → display selects (GET+PATCH), `payment` slimmed to `{id, paymentStatus, amount, currency}` at all 4 sites.
- **Explore trending**: rank step (all plans × 30-day slots, JS sort) shared across requests via `unstable_cache` 60s (was per-request).
- **Indexes** (additive, pushed): `Consultation(consultationPlanId, requestStatus, requestedAt)` + Subscription mirror (requests-tab hot path), `Waitlist(status, expiresAt)` (cron range scans).

### Ops (done, no code)

`PG_POOL_MAX=1` set in Netlify production env — each serverless function opened a default 10-connection pool; at Netlify concurrency that exhausts Supabase's cap (the #852 knob exists for exactly this).

## Verification

tsc clean, 1355/1355 jest, lint adds no errors; planner/events/availability smoke-tested live (200s, shapes intact, counts correct); authz leak re-tested closed (0 rows for the degenerate session).

## Follow-up

PR-2.5 (next): frontend cache-first tab smoothness from the same RCA — refetchOnWindowFocus default, keepPreviousData, Stream SDK out of layouts, poller consolidation.

Part of the post-#837 hardening train. Touches the live half of #309.

## Что изменилось

Удалён мост `htmx:load` → `Alpine.initTree(...)` из `app/templates/base.html`; тест `test_import_page_uses_htmx_upload_form` теперь проверяет его отсутствие.

## Зачем

Alpine 3 сам инициализирует добавленный htmx-ом DOM через MutationObserver, поэтому ручной вызов инициализировал каждый свопнутый фрагмент дважды. Секция «Тело сообщения» в панели шаблона получала два экземпляра `templateBodyEditor` и задвоенные обработчики кликов, что давало два пользовательских дефекта:

1. **JSON отображался дважды** — `startEdit()` срабатывал в обоих экземплярах и над одной textarea создавались два CodeMirror.
2. **Невалидный JSON «сохранялся» с уходом со страницы** — `save()` срабатывал дважды: лишний экземпляр синкал в форму старый валидный текст, проходил валидацию и отправлял его на сервер; панель перерисовывалась с тостом «Тело шаблона обновлено», а реальная ошибка валидации лишь мелькала.

## Проверка

- Все 375 тестов проходят (`uv run pytest`).
- Минимальный статический репро (htmx 2.0.4 + Alpine 3.14.1, та же схема загрузки панели) в браузере: с мостом — 2 инициализации компонента и 2 вызова обработчика на один клик; без моста — ровно по одной.
- Рекомендуется ручная проверка в окружении с БД: «Редактировать тело» → один редактор; невалидный JSON + сохранение → остаёмся на форме с ошибкой; валидный JSON → сохраняется.

author: mremond
body:
Busy rooms render the entire message backlog into the DOM with no virtualization. On WebKitGTK (Linux/Tauri) the message-list scroll-correction `ResizeObserver` reflows that whole tree every frame, pinning a CPU core at idle in large rooms.

Apply `content-visibility: auto` to message rows so the browser skips layout/paint for off-screen messages. Since that also paint-clips the floating hover toolbar and dropdowns, the hovered / focused / keyboard-selected row is decontained.

Covers both rooms and 1:1 chat (shared `MessageList` row). Note: the WebKitGTK CPU loop can't be reproduced on macOS (WKWebView), so the idle-CPU improvement needs verification on a Linux build.

author: radakam
body:
## Changes

Adds a computed, read-only `volume_path` to `resources.volumes.*` so configs can use `${resources.volumes.<key>.volume_path}` instead of hardcoding `/Volumes/<catalog>/<schema>/<name>` (databricks/cli#4233).
- `Volume.VolumePath` (`bundle:"readonly"`) + `ComputeVolumePath()`.
- `InitializeVolumePaths` mutator: computes the path, rejects a user-set value.
- `ResolveVolumePathReferencesOnlyResources` mutator: resolves `${...volume_path}` referrers, erroring if the referenced volume does not exist.
- `extractReferences` now gates references on the resource's state type (ripples through `ExtractReferences`, `migrate/build_state.go`).
- Terraform: drop `volume_path` in `convert_volume.go`, remove from `terraform_dabs_map`.

## Why
The path is fully determined by `catalog_name`/`schema_name`/`name`, so deriving it removes duplication and makes a reference depend on those components, not the volume itself. It's computed at `initialize` and never persisted (not sent to the API, dropped before Terraform apply), after `PythonMutator` since the PyDABs model doesn't declare it. Only *pure* `${resources....}` components are resolved locally to compute the path; any other value — literal text, mixed literal+reference, or a reference not resolvable at initialize — is embedded verbatim and resolved later during plan/deploy. A reference in a readonly field can't resolve against state, hence the `extractReferences` gating.

## Tests
* Unit: `ComputeVolumePath` (plain + embedded pure reference), `InitializeVolumePaths` (basic, unresolved reference embedded verbatim, user-set value rejected, cross-volume pipeline), `ResolveVolumePathReferencesOnlyResources` (resolves only `volume_path` referrers, errors on missing target), and `extractReferences` dropping the readonly field.
* Acceptance: `computed_volume_path` and `volume_path_contains_id` (resolution at validate/deploy, both engines); `volume_path_job_ref` (job-parameter case, direct-only since the embedded `creator_user_name` is only known after deploy); `set-volume-path` (user-set value rejected). Invariant configs run `volume_path_job_ref` (via `${resources.jobs.foo.id}`) on both the direct `no_drift` and Terraform-seeded `migrate` suites.

author: hetcreep
body:
### What

`[TargetType]` and `[TargetAssembly]` now allow multiple instances on one patch method.

### Why

The docs say you can specify additional `[TargetType]` attributes to target more types, and the discovery code already reads them with the plural `MetadataHelper.GetAttributes<TargetTypeAttribute>(method)` / `GetAttributes<TargetAssemblyAttribute>(method)` (`AssemblyPatcher.cs`). But both attributes were declared `[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method)]` without `AllowMultiple = true`, so the C# compiler rejects a second one with **CS0579: Duplicate 'TargetType' attribute** before runtime ever sees it.

Setting `AllowMultiple = true` makes the attribute declarations match both the documentation and the plural consumer. Single-attribute usage is unchanged; this only stops the compiler from rejecting the second attribute.

`[TargetAssembly]` is the sibling attribute consumed the same plural way, so it gets the same fix for consistency.

Fixes #849

Built across net35/net46/net6.

#432 で追加した「新しいタブで開く」で画像 URL を開くと、黒背景の中央に画像が小さく低解像度（ガビガビ）で表示され、リロードすると正しく表示される問題を修正します。

## 原因

新規タブの初回ロードは `GeckoView.setSession()` 直後の `restoreSession` で実行されますが、この時点では GeckoView の Surface サイズが未確定です。Gecko の画像単体表示（ImageDocument）はロード時に一度だけ shrink-to-fit スケールを計算するため、未確定 viewport を基準にスケールが誤計算され、その後正しいサイズになっても再レイアウトされません。リロードはサイズ確定後の再ロードなので直ります。

## 変更内容

初回ロードを GeckoView のサイズ確定（width/height > 0）後まで遅延します。

- `BrowserSessionController` (browser-engine-gecko)
  - `restoreSession` は `open` + `setActive` までにとどめ、`BrowserTab.pendingInitialLoad` を立てる
  - ロード本体（referrer 付き `load` / `loadUri`）は新メソッド `performInitialLoadIfPending` に分離。サイズ確定待ち中にタブが閉じられた場合はロードしない
- `GeckoBrowserTab` (app)
  - `LaunchedEffect(session, browserTab, geckoView)` で、既存の `scheduleStableSizeAttach` と同じ `postOnAnimation` パターンによりサイズ確定を待ってから `performInitialLoadIfPending` を呼ぶ
  - レイアウトが進まない異常系で白画面にならないよう `STABLE_TIMEOUT_MS`（1000ms）経過後は強制ロード

## デグレ防止

| 経路 | 影響 |
|---|---|
| タブ復元（pendingSessionState） | `restoreState` 経路は従来どおり即実行 |
| target=_blank / window.open（pendingInitialUrl） | 早期 return のまま。Google Pay 等のポップアップ決済に影響なし |
| 既存タブ表示・切替（session.isOpen） | 早期 return のまま |

`BrowserSessionLifecycleControllerTest` に遅延ロードの状態遷移（遅延・referrer 付きロード・二重実行防止・クローズ時スキップ）のテストを追加しています。

## 確認

- [x] `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` ビルド成功
- [x] `./gradlew detekt` 指摘 0 件
- [x] `./gradlew test` 全件通過（追加テスト含む）
- [ ] 実機確認: 画像を「新しいタブで開く」で初回から正しいスケール・解像度で表示されること

author: oleg-kozlyuk-grafana
body:
**What this PR does**:

Replaces `protoc-gen-gogofaster` with the [wiresmith](https://github.com/grafana/wiresmith) protobuf compiler — pinned to the tagged **v0.9.0** release — for all of Tempo's own protos. The wire format and all stored-data shapes are unchanged, and the generated Go API mirrors gogo's, so call sites and the gRPC/codec integration keep working. OTLP ingest decode gets faster and allocates less; everything else is at gogo parity.

## Performance

Benchstat-grade, `pkg/ingest` decode benchmarks, Apple M4 Pro, n=20 alternated binaries, vs the gogo baseline (`7c61b2b70b`, measured at migration time):

| Bench | gogo | wiresmith | vs gogo |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BenchmarkEncodeDecode` | 148.2µs / 1.227Mi | 150.0µs / 1.228Mi | **parity** (time p=0.64, mem p=0.66, 2004 allocs equal) |
| `BenchmarkGeneratorDecoderOTLP` | 89.74µs | 88.30µs | time **parity** (p=0.068); **−6.75% bytes / −5.57% allocs** |
| `BenchmarkGeneratorDecoderPushBytes` | 168.6µs | 166.6µs | **−1.22%** (p=0.008) |

On top of that, profile-driven pointer elimination on the highest-allocation repeated fields in the OTLP decode path (`ResourceSpans.scope_spans`, `ScopeSpans.spans`, `Span.attributes`, `Span_Event.attributes`, `Span_Link.attributes` became value-typed slices; wire format unchanged):

| Benchmark | sec/op | B/op | allocs/op |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BenchmarkGeneratorDecoderOTLP` | **−11.03%** (p=0.000) | −1.82% (p=0.045) | **−16.62%** (p=0.000) |

## What & why

gogo/protobuf is archived and unmaintained; wiresmith is Grafana's replacement compiler, generating a gogo-shaped Go API (same field shapes, `Marshal`/`Unmarshal`/`Size` methods, JSON tags) on the standard proto wire format. This makes the migration an API-shape-preserving codegen swap, not a behavior change. The `make gen-proto` pipeline (buf + docker + gogofaster) is replaced by the wiresmith CLI, installed from the go.mod pin (CI installs it the same way).

## Scope

- Patched OTel protos `pkg/tempopb/{common,resource,trace}/v1` — annotated sources checked in under `pkg/tempopb/.wiresmith-proto/`, kept in sync with the `opentelemetry-proto` submodule pin (see migration notes).
- `pkg/tempopb/tempo.proto` + `backendwork.proto`, `modules/frontend/v1/frontendv1pb/frontend.proto`, `tempodb/backend/v1/v1.proto`.
- `(wiresmith.options.no_presence_all)` on all Tempo protos (gogo `nullable=false` parity); `(wiresmith.options.pointer)` preserves gogo's `[]*T` shapes except the five hot OTLP fields above; customtype envelopes carry the dskit httpgrpc fields.
- go.mod pins `github.com/grafana/wiresmith v0.9.0` (tagged release); changelog entry via `.chloggen/`.

## Migration notes (why parts of the diff look the way they do)

- **`CompactedBlockMeta` (the one `gogoproto.embed` in the repo)**: wiresmith has no embed option, so the field became named (`BlockMeta`, ~33 call sites `x.Field` → `x.BlockMeta.Field`) with `jsontag "-"`, and a hand-written `MarshalJSON` reproduces the exact flat JSON shape gogo's struct-embedding produced (stored `meta.compacted.json` / tenant-index `"compacted"` entries depend on it; the read path is upstream's own unchanged `UnmarshalJSON`). Shape equivalence was audited field-by-field and is pinned by golden tests, including **frozen gogo-produced wire bytes** decoded by the new code.
- **Wire presence divergence (deliberate, read-compatible)**: gogo always emitted `nullable=false` message fields, even zero-valued; wiresmith's `no_presence` follows canonical proto3 and omits zero values. Concretely: zero-valued `stdtime` fields and empty `DedicatedColumns` no longer produce bytes on the wire. Decoders on both sides treat absent and zero-valued identically (verified in both directions), no production path writes zero times, and the chosen behavior is locked in by tests so it can't silently flip.
- **Value-typed slices**: dropping pointers makes `for _, x := range s { x.Field = … }` mutate a copy — a silent no-op. A full-repo audit against the complete 23-field shape-change inventory found and fixed 6 such sites across the branch's lifetime (with regression tests); everything else verified index-based or read-only. New code touching these slices should mutate via `s[i]`/`&s[i]`.
- **OTLP proto snapshot sync**: upstream regenerates from the `opentelemetry-proto` submodule; this branch generates from the checked-in annotated snapshots. The snapshots are synced to the current submodule pin (`30b9cc9`, #7520), including the new `EntityRef`/strindex fields (same Go shapes as gogo's, round-trip tested). When the submodule pin moves, the snapshots must be re-synced — the vendor-check CI job catches a forgotten regen, and the snapshot diff is part of that flow.
- **jsonpb stays on gogo**: golang/protobuf's jsonpb panics on wiresmith messages (reflection-based), so `pkg/httpclient` + `modules/querier` keep gogo jsonpb via small shims. One behavior nit found by the e2e API suite (empty JSON array decoding to non-nil vs nil slice) was adjusted in a test helper.
- **Generated `Equal`/`Clone`**: restored marshal-free deep-compare/deep-copy at ~25 call sites (frontend combiner's `cloneProto`, vulture's trace equality, etc.) that previously round-tripped through `Marshal` bytes.
- **`cmp.Diff` gotcha**: the generated `Equal(any) bool` method is now preferred by `go-cmp`, making float comparisons bit-exact; tests needing tolerance add an explicit `cmp.Comparer` (done in `tempodb_metrics` tests).
- **gRPC**: server impls embed `Unimplemented*Server`; `pkg/gogocodec` keeps working unchanged because it dispatches on Marshal/Unmarshal duck-typing rather than gogo-specific interfaces.
- **Makefile staging**: proto sources are staged under build-tree subdirectories matching their import paths so wiresmith's path-derived keying preserves the committed `// source:` headers and registration names.
- **Kept workarounds with upstream tracking**: `StableString()` (deterministic proto-text where generated `String()` is `%v`-based), the dskit httpgrpc customtype envelopes, and a `Size_` customname (field/method collision) — each maps to an open item in the wiresmith tracker where the compiler-side fix, if any, will land.

## Validation

- **Full CI matrix green** (unit suites, all six e2e integration suites, lint, vendor-check regen gate).
- **Golden compatibility fixtures** (`tempodb/backend/wiresmith_custom_test.go`): the gogo-era flat JSON shape, degenerate cases (zero times, empty dedicated columns), and frozen gogo-generated wire bytes (`CompactedBlockMeta` 307 B, `TenantIndex` 617 B, generated at upstream `6bf6ee34f`) all decode and round-trip correctly under the new code — direct evidence that data already in production buckets stays readable.
- **Mixed-version cluster e2e** (rolling-upgrade simulation; gogo image from the merge base vs wiresmith image from this branch, run locally via the `integration/` framework):

| Scenario | Topology | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Sanity | all-gogo; all-wiresmith | pass |
| Upgrade front first | wiresmith distributor+frontend / gogo querier+live-store | pass |
| Inverse | gogo distributor+frontend / wiresmith querier+live-store | pass |
| Metrics-generator | distributor and generator on opposite versions, both directions (Kafka records cross-version, remote-write asserted) | pass |
| Bucket handoff | each version writes/flushes/compacts, the other reads the same bucket cold (incl. `index.pb.zst` tenant index + `meta.compacted.json`), compacts again, both directions | pass |

  Trace-by-ID and TraceQL results content-equal in every scenario; zero proto/unmarshal errors across all container logs. Re-validated at the final head with a rebuilt image (sanity + cross-version + bucket-handoff smoke, 3/3). The harness isn't part of this PR to keep the diff focused — happy to contribute it to `integration/` if wanted.
- **Regen byte-stability**: `make gen-proto` at v0.9.0 is byte-identical across repeated runs; the vendor-check CI job re-verifies this on every push.

body:
## Summary
This PR replaces the string-based icon system in the navigation menu with strongly-typed Material Design icons from the IconPacks.Avalonia.Material package. This improves type safety and provides a more robust icon rendering solution.

## Key Changes
- **New Converter**: Added `PackIconMaterialKindToGeometryConverter` to convert `PackIconMaterialKind` enum values to `StreamGeometry` objects for use with `PathIcon`. This works around binary compatibility issues with the IconPacks.Avalonia.Material control styles on Avalonia 12.
- **Updated NavigationItem Model**: Changed the `Icon` property from `string` to `PackIconMaterialKind` enum type for type safety
- **Updated MainWindowViewModel**: Replaced string icon values (`"CameraIcon"`, `"LupenIcon"`) with strongly-typed enum values (`PackIconMaterialKind.Camera`, `PackIconMaterialKind.Magnify`)
- **Updated MainWindow View**: 
  - Registered the new converter as a window resource
  - Changed the navigation item template from displaying text to using `PathIcon` with the converter binding
- **Added Dependency**: Added `IconPacks.Avalonia.Material` NuGet package (v2.0.0)

## Implementation Details
The converter directly accesses the icon data from `PackIconDataFactory<PackIconMaterialKind>.DataIndex` rather than using the bundled `PackIconMaterial` control, which avoids the binary compatibility issues mentioned in the IconPacks.Avalonia GitHub issue #41.

author: tissugalon
body:
### 💡 What
Added a confirmation dialog that appears when users click the "Clear Cart" button on the POS screen.

### 🎯 Why
Clearing the entire cart is a destructive action. Previously, the cart was cleared immediately upon clicking the trash icon. A misclick could cause users to lose all their inputted items, leading to frustration. The confirmation dialog acts as a necessary safety net.

### 📸 Before/After
- **Before:** Clicking the trash icon immediately emptied the cart.
- **After:** Clicking the trash icon displays an alert dialog ("Clear Cart") asking "Are you sure you want to clear all items from the cart?" with Cancel and Clear Cart (destructive) options.

### ♿ Accessibility
- Utilized `showShadDialog` with semantic structural elements.
- The confirm action uses `ShadButton.destructive` to clearly indicate a destructive action visually (red text/button) and semantically.
- Included translation strings for English and Indonesian languages (`app_en.arb`, `app_id.arb`).

body:
## Summary

This PR introduces `cross_sample_null_zeta`, a new honest significance test for Manifold Coherence ζ that compares same-input layer pairs against unrelated control samples. It also deprecates `permutation_test_zeta`, which produces uninformative p-values on real activations due to near-zero-variance nulls when permuting high-dimensional flattened vectors.

Additionally, the PR makes distributed/dual-node features optional by moving `pyzmq` to an optional dependency group and adding graceful import handling.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Deprecation
- [x] Refactor

## Changes

### Core metrics (`unitarity_labs/core/metrics.py`)
- **New function `cross_sample_null_zeta`**: Implements an honest significance test by computing ζ for the same input pair and comparing it against the distribution of ζ scores from unrelated control inputs. Returns a dict with matched score, null statistics, gap, z-score, and control count.
- **Deprecate `permutation_test_zeta`**: Added deprecation warning explaining that permuting flattened high-dimensional vectors produces near-zero-variance nulls, yielding uninformative p~0 results. Users are directed to use `cross_sample_null_zeta` instead.

### Optional dependencies (`pyproject.toml`)
- Moved `pyzmq`, `msgpack`, and `reedsolo` from core dependencies to a new `[project.optional-dependencies]` section under `dist`.
- Core package now has minimal dependencies; distributed features are opt-in.

### Distributed features (`unitarity_labs/core/dual_link.py`)
- Made `zmq` import lazy: moved from module-level to `__init__` method with try/except.
- Added informative `ImportError` directing users to install with `pip install 'unitarity-lab[dist]'`.
- Added local `import zmq` in `recv_partner_basis` for zmq constants.

### Package initialization (`unitarity_labs/core/__init__.py`)
- Wrapped `DualNodeEntanglementBridge` and `register_dual_node_hook` imports in try/except.
- Set to `None` if `pyzmq` is not installed, allowing the package to load without distributed features.

### Tests (`tests/test_hardening.py`)
- Updated `test_permutation_test_reproducibility` to suppress deprecation warnings.
- Added `test_permutation_test_emits_deprecation_warning` to verify the warning is raised.
- Added new test class `TestCrossSampleNullZeta` with four tests:
  - `test_positive_control_gap_and_zscore`: Verifies gap > 0 and z_score > 2 for correlated sink vs random controls.
  - `test_negative_control_gap_near_zero`: Verifies gap ≈ 0 for independent data.
  - `test_empty_control_sinks_raises`: Verifies ValueError on empty control list.
  - `test_return_keys_and_n_controls`: Verifies all required keys and correct n_controls value.

## Validation

- [x] New unit tests added for `cross_sample_null_zeta` (4 tests covering positive/negative controls, error handling, and output structure)
- [x] Existing test updated to handle deprecation warning
- [x] Deprecation warning properly emitted and tested
- [x] Optional dependency handling tested implicitly through import guards

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added for new functionality and deprecation
- [x] Deprecation documented in docstring with migration path
- [x] No sensitive data added
- [x] Optional dependency structure reduces attack surface for users not needing distributed features

## Related issues

body:
Fixes the five critical findings from the pre-submission security audit, repairs CI (which was red on main for three separate reasons), and documents the fraud-detection/protected-customer-data decision.

## Critical fixes

1. **Reinstall bricked the app** — `app/uninstalled` set `shop.isActive = false` and nothing ever reset it, so after reinstall webhooks, click tracking, and portal signups were silently disabled. The dashboard loader now reactivates the shop and stores the fresh access token. (Shopify reviewers routinely uninstall/reinstall during review.)
2. **Cross-tenant portal login** — the form login at `portal.login.tsx` looked up affiliates by email alone (no shop scoping), could log a user into the wrong shop's account, and bypassed the lockout that the JSON API login enforces. Now requires the store domain (same field signup already has, pre-filled from `?shop=`), scopes by `shopId`, and applies the 5-attempt/15-minute lockout.
3. **Payout double-spend race (portal API)** — the `pendingCommission` balance check ran outside the transaction; concurrent requests could both pass it. The decrement is now conditional (`pendingCommission >= amount`) inside the transaction and is the authoritative check.
4. **Payout double-spend race (portal form)** — `portal.payouts.tsx` duplicated the same vulnerable logic; a double-submit created duplicate payout requests. Same atomic fix applied.
5. **Failed auto-payouts lost affiliate money** — the cron zeroed `pendingCommission` before calling Razorpay; on failure the payout was marked FAILED but the balance was never restored. The pre-tax base amount is now restored in the same transaction.

## CI repairs (CI was failing on main)

- `env.server.ts` used Zod v3's `error.errors` (v4 renamed it to `issues`) — `tsc --noEmit` failed repo-wide.
- 26 pre-existing ESLint errors (unused imports/vars, explicit `any`, unescaped entities, dead toast effects) — the lint step failed on every branch.
- The "Validate Prisma" step never had `DATABASE_URL` set, so `prisma validate` failed with P1012. A dummy value is now provided (validate doesn't connect to a database).

All four CI steps (`tsc`, ESLint, `prisma validate`, build) verified green locally before push.

## Decision (ADR included)

**Fraud detection stays; we'll request Level 2 Protected Customer Data.** Commission attribution already requires `read_orders`/`orders/create`, which is protected customer data (Level 1) regardless — dropping fraud detection wouldn't avoid the Partner Dashboard process, only the email field request. Both GoAffPro and UpPromote ship fraud protection, and it's a PREMIUM plan selling point. See `docs/decisions/2026-06-11-keep-fraud-detection-request-level-2-pcd.md`. A session retro with the remaining high-priority items is in `docs/retros/`.

## Summary

Adds build and test execution capabilities to `dev-angular-mcp` and `dev-dotnet-mcp` servers, replacing direct shell invocation with MCP-mediated build/test operations. Implements structured output parsing (errors, warnings, summary) and enforces MCP-first workflow via updated skill documentation.

## Key Changes

### MCP Server Implementations

**Dev.Angular.Mcp:**
- New `AngularRunner` service with `BuildAsync()` and `TestAsync()` methods
- Parses `ng build` and `ng test` output using regex patterns for TypeScript/Webpack errors and Karma test results
- New tools: `build_angular_project()` and `test_angular_project()` in `AngularTools`
- Comprehensive test suite (`AngularRunnerTests`) covering success/failure parsing, ANSI stripping, deduplication

**Dev.Dotnet.Mcp:**
- New `DotnetRunner` service with `BuildAsync()` and `TestAsync()` methods
- Parses `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` output for C# compiler errors/warnings and test failures
- New tools: `build_dotnet_solution()` and `test_dotnet_solution()` in `DotnetTools`
- Comprehensive test suite (`DotnetRunnerTests`) covering .NET-specific output formats, theory tests, Windows line endings

**Common Features:**
- Timeout handling (300s build, 600s test) with graceful process termination
- ANSI code stripping for clean output
- Error/warning deduplication and capping (50 errors, 20 warnings)
- Structured result model: `success`, `errors[]`, `warnings[]`, `summary`, `exitCode`
- Cancellation token support

### Skill & Documentation Updates

- **dev-angular-mcp/SKILL.md**: Updated to document `build_angular_project` and `test_angular_project` tools; clarified container path requirements (`/workspace/...`)
- **dev-dotnet-mcp/SKILL.md**: Updated to document `build_dotnet_solution` and `test_dotnet_solution` tools; clarified container path requirements
- **implementation-workflow/SKILL.md**: Replaced build-log-filter-centric workflow with MCP-first enforcement; added hard gate for MCP availability
- **build-log-filter/SKILL.md**: Clarified that `ng build/test` and `dotnet build/test` are out-of-scope when MCPs are available
- **verification-commands.md**: Added MCP-based build/test examples with `/workspace/` path conventions
- **dev-tooling-mcp/SKILL.md**: Updated router to include build/test operations
- **angular-developer/references/op-tooling.md**: Added build/test MCP tools to scaffolding table
- **mcp.json**: Added volume mount `${workspaceFolder}:/workspace` to both Angular and .NET MCP containers
- **silent-shortcut-prevention.md**: Expanded documentation on enforcement principles and MCP-first workflow

### Configuration

- Updated `Program.cs` in both MCP servers to register `AngularRunner` and `DotnetRunner` as singletons
- Added `JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull` to Angular MCP JSON options for cleaner serialization

## Implementation Details

- **Regex-based parsing**: Uses C# 7.0+ `[GeneratedRegex]` attributes for compile-time regex optimization
- **Process management**: Leverages `System.Diagnostics.Process` with async I/O and linked cancellation tokens
- **Error recovery**: Graceful handling of process timeouts, cancellations, and missing executables
- **Output filtering**: Internal ANSI stripping ensures LLM receives only structured data, never raw console output
- **Container paths**: All path parameters use `/workspace/...` convention (Docker mount: `${workspaceFolder}:/workspace`)

## Testing

- 13 tests for `DotnetRunner` covering build success/failure, error extraction, warning deduplication, theory tests, Windows line endings, ANSI stripping
- 9 tests for `AngularRunner

author: nicolegros
body:
## Summary

Adds keyboard-based scrollback support for direct shell sessions (non-tmux).

With tmux, scrolling is natively handled by tmux's copy mode. For direct shell sessions, xterm.js sends PageUp/PageDown as escape sequences to the PTY rather than scrolling its own buffer. This PR intercepts scroll keybindings and calls xterm's native scroll API.

## Keybindings

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Shift+PageUp | Scroll one page up |
| Shift+PageDown | Scroll one page down |
| Shift+ArrowUp | Scroll one line up |
| Shift+ArrowDown | Scroll one line down |

## Changes

- `src/lib/terminal-keys.ts`: Added `scroll_page_up`, `scroll_page_down`, `scroll_line_up`, `scroll_line_down` action types and matching rules
- `src/components/Terminal.svelte`: Handle scroll actions via `term.scrollPages()` / `term.scrollLines()`
- `src/lib/__tests__/terminal-keys.test.ts`: Added tests for all 4 scroll keybindings

## Testing

- All 89 vitest tests pass
- Vite build succeeds

author: gmtmaster
body:
## Overview

This PR introduces the first implementation of multi-tenant account support for Goose.

Previously, all devices and uploaded metrics effectively belonged to a single shared environment. This worked well for local development but made it difficult to run multiple devices for different users on the same backend instance.

The goal of this work is to allow multiple users to share a single Goose server while keeping their devices, API tokens, and uploaded metrics isolated from each other.

A common use case is running Goose for family members or friends without needing to deploy a separate backend for every person.

---

## What Was Added

### iOS Account System

Added account creation and login support directly inside the iOS application.

Features:

* User registration
* User login
* Session persistence
* Account management flow
* Authentication-aware UI

This allows each user to authenticate against the backend before interacting with devices or uploading metrics.

---

### Backend Authentication

Added backend authentication infrastructure:

* User table
* API token management
* Account ownership validation
* User isolation layer

Each registered user receives their own API token.

The API token is used to:

* authenticate requests
* identify the owning account
* associate uploaded metrics with the correct user

---

### Device Ownership Model

Introduced device ownership support.

Each device can now be associated with a specific account.

This allows:

* multiple devices on one server
* separation of user data
* prevention of accidental cross-account access

The backend now validates ownership before serving account-specific resources.

---

### Multi-Tenant Data Isolation

Added ownership-aware database logic.

The system now tracks:

* users
* API tokens
* device ownership relationships

This creates a foundation for future production deployments where multiple users share a single backend instance.

---

### Friendly Device Names

Added support for friendly device naming.

Users can assign human-readable names to devices instead of relying solely on identifiers.

Examples:

* Adam's WHOOP
* Office Band
* Dad's Device

---

### Automated Tests

Added coverage for:

* authentication flow
* token validation
* device ownership
* multi-tenant isolation
* device management functionality

New tests were added to verify that users cannot accidentally access resources owned by other accounts.

---

## Mock Metrics Testing

A temporary mock metrics ingestion system is included.

Purpose:

* validate end-to-end account isolation
* verify metric ownership logic
* test multi-device scenarios without requiring physical hardware

The mock system successfully inserts metrics into the database and associates them with the correct account.

This allowed verification that multi-tenant separation is functioning as expected.

---

## Current Status

### Verified

* User registration
* User login
* Session persistence
* API token generation
* Device ownership
* Multi-user isolation
* Mock metric ingestion
* Database ownership relationships

### Still Under Development

Live device ingestion remains under development.

At the time of implementation, I did not have access to multiple physical devices to fully validate real-world uploads across several accounts.

The ownership and authentication infrastructure is complete and tested using mock data, while live device validation will follow once additional hardware testing is available.

---

## Motivation

The primary motivation was to enable a single Goose deployment to support multiple users.

Instead of hosting:

* one server per user

a single instance can now support:

* multiple accounts
* multiple devices
* isolated user data

This significantly simplifies self-hosting for families, friends, and small groups sharing the same backend.

---

## Notes

The mock ingestion path is intentionally left in place for development and testing purposes until live multi-device validation is completed.

No breaking changes are expected for existing single-user deployments.

author: shosho-chang
body:
## 做了什麼

Centaur Zettelkasten **每日迴圈** scheduled job（規格 v0.2 §2 三迴圈 / §5 每日回顧 + Prompt 規格 v0.1 P-1/P-2），與 N523 UI 解耦——只算資料、寫 log、ping Nami。

- **`agents/robin/daily_review.py`** — `run_daily_review(now, weekly, ...)` 主入口：
  - ① 掃 `KB/Annotations/` 昨日 delta（per-item `created_at`）→ **P-1** 候選篩選 + 建議卡名（強訊號置頂、純 highlight 排除、上限 7）
  - 每候選 FTS5 撈 top-k 既有卡 → **P-2** 判 typed-edge 真關係 + 方向（每組上限 3，`internal_rationale` 從 LLM 收回但**不入輸出**）
  - ② `KB/Fleeting/` `status: open` 掃描（AI 只讀不改字）
  - ③ 每週清掃（`weekly=True`）：stale seedling（>30 天）、孤兒卡（`kb_wikilinks`+`kb_typed_edges` link-graph 程式算）、「之後再說」14 天過期歸檔
  - `KB/log.md` append + Nami Slack ping
- **`shared/schemas/daily_review.py`** — N523 消費契約（見下）
- **兩個 LLM seam**（`_ask_p1_llm` / `_ask_p2_llm`）module-level，測試 monkeypatch 不打 API
- defer/skip 狀態存 vault-side JSON（`KB/.centaur/daily_review_state.json`），跨每日 run 持久

## 輸出 schema（N523 契約）

`DailyReviewBundle`（`schema_version=1`，closed-set 協定，`extra="forbid"`）：

| 欄位 | 型別 | 說明 |
|------|------|------|
| `generated_at` / `review_date` | str | job 時刻 / 被回顧日 |
| `weekly_sweep` | bool | 今天是否含清掃區 |
| `candidates` | `list[CandidateCard]` | P-1 候選 + P-2 chips |
| `fleeting` | `list[FleetingItem]` | open fleeting |
| `sweep` | `list[SweepItem]` | stale/orphan/expired（每週才填）|
| `warnings` | list[str] | 非致命問題留痕 |

- **`CandidateCard`**：`candidate_id`（穩定 hash，dedup/skip 用）、`suggested_title`（宣告句）、`why`、`source_refs: list[SourceRef]`（`anchor`+`literature_path`+`quote`+`note`，原文照錄）、`edges: list[TypedEdgeChip]`、`priority`、`strong_signal`
- **`TypedEdgeChip`**：`edge_type`（support/refute/extend）、`direction`（forward/reverse）、`target_card`、`target_title`。**刻意不帶 rationale**——紅線：理由留人（規格 P-2 規則 4）
- **`FleetingItem`** / **`SweepItem`**（`kind`: stale_seedling/orphan_card/expired_defer）

## 測試結果（本機 Windows）

> ⚠️ stacked PR 對非 main base CI 不跑，以下為本機證據。

- **新測試 `tests/agents/robin/test_daily_review.py`：33 passed**
  - 過期歸檔 14 天確定性測試（含邊界 13/14 天、壞日期、空佇列）
  - 孤兒卡 / stale seedling 偵測（link-graph 程式邏輯，含 30 天邊界）
  - P-1 強訊號置頂（《卡片盒筆記》mock fixture，「必須重複三次」/「這句是我想的」）+ LLM 漏標安全網
  - P-2 **財富階梯 ↔ wingate 表面相似負面測試**（必須丟棄）+ 真關係保留 + 每組上限 3 + FTS 無命中不浪費 LLM call
  - 輸出 schema round-trip + `extra="forbid"` + rationale 不外露斷言
  - 端到端 orchestrator（skip 過濾、每週清掃、過期歸檔）
- **回歸 `pytest tests/shared tests/agents/robin --ignore=tests/agents/foundry`：2161 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed**
  - 唯一失敗 `test_log.py::test_json_formatter_handles_non_string_extra`（`\` vs `/` 路徑分隔）是**任務文件列明的 7 個 Windows pre-existing 失敗之一**，CI(Linux) 會綠，非本 PR 造成
- **ruff check 全綠**（三檔 `ruff check` + `ruff format`）

## 依賴

- N521 Literature writer（#876，本 PR base）
- N520 permanent-layer / indexer / `kb_typed_edges`（#874）

## 誠實列：rough / 主觀待驗

- **候選品質須 修修 早上實看**：P-1/P-2 的 prompt 照 Prompt 規格逐字搬，但真實《卡片盒筆記》annotation 跑出的候選排序與 typed-edge 判斷品質只有真 LLM + 真 vault 才驗得到（測試全 mock）。task §5 的「以真實 annotation 跑出置頂含兩條」屬人工 UAT，未自動化。
- **Nami 通知沿用 Franky Slack bot**（`post_plain`）——Nami 專屬 bot identity 尚未上線，留 TODO 待 N526。通知失敗不中斷 job（best-effort）。
- **defer/skip 狀態的寫入端是 N523**：本 job 只讀 + 每週過期歸檔。state 檔格式（`skipped` list + `deferred` dict）是與 N523 的隱性契約，未獨立 schema 化。
- **孤兒偵測依賴 kb_index.db 已 reindex**：若索引未含某卡的 typed-edge / wikilink，會誤判為孤兒。job 不主動 reindex（假設排程上游已跑 indexer）。
- **schedule 設定未落地**：task §4 提「schedule 設定」，本 PR 只交付可被排程呼叫的 `run_daily_review` 入口；實際 cron/scheduler 掛載點待與部署側對齊（早上時刻、weekly 旗標的週判定）。

## Summary

Part B of the mobile beer-catalogue chantier: the screens implementing **UC1 browse / UC2 search / UC3 beer fiche** (+ brewery & style fiches reached by tap), consuming the deployed Python encyclopedia API. The merged UML conception study (`docs/architecture/diagrams/mobile-catalog/`, PR #1213) is the contract — every layer conforms to its diagrams (ADR-0013).

- **Feature `src/features/beer-catalog/`** (strict layering, mirrors scan/recipes):
  - `domain` — `CatalogBeer` / `CatalogBeerDetail` / `CatalogBrewery` / `CatalogStyle`, `Page<T>` + `PaginationMeta`; raw ADR-0017 interval bounds only (no derived scalars).
  - `data` — snake_case DTOs + mappers (`abv` string→number, `website_url`→`website`), single egress `request()` with `auth:false` + `baseUrl env.encyclopediaUrl` + `encyclopediaUrlIsConfigured` 503 guard; named errors `CatalogNotFoundError` / `CatalogUnavailableError` (aborts pass through).
  - `application` — ONE paginated hook `useBeerCatalogPagination` (`useInfiniteQuery`, pure 1-based `computeNextPageParam`, `keepPreviousData`) serving browse AND search; `useDebouncedValue` (300 ms, min 2 chars); `useBeer` with cache-primed `placeholderData` (list row → instant partial fiche); view-model builders (midpoint + SRM→EBC + fallback labels live at the VM, per diagram 10).
  - `presentation` — infinite FlatList (guarded `onEndReached`, footer spinner / inline next-page error via `isFetchNextPageError` + retry / end-of-list), debounced search (prompt/empty/results), beer fiche (hero colour, intervals, legal block + provenance held while placeholder, tappable brewery/style rows → navigation), brewery & style fiches. FR copy in constants; theme tokens only.
- **Wiring** — `app/(app)/beer-catalog/{index,search,beer/[id],brewery/[id],style/[id]}`; hidden Tabs entry (`href:null`, dock frozen per #613); Dashboard "Voir plus" entry "Catalogue bières".
- **core/http** — additive `signal?: AbortSignal` forwarded to `fetch`: a superseded search now truly aborts the network request (conception 03 target).
- **Tests** — ~130 new (mappers, API paths/options/error mapping, pagination math edges, debounce fake timers, view-model, screens incl. next-page-error + non-tappable-row cases, signal propagation). One real bug caught pre-merge by the tests (composite `onPress` made the non-tappable fallback row navigate — renamed to `onNavigate`).

## Notes for reviewers

- **Known divergence (tracked in the conception)**: the API returns `brewery_name`/`style_name` **null** on list/search/detail today (only `import-by-ean` resolves them) — the VM shows fallback labels until the API resolves names on those endpoints.
- **No demo-data branch**: the encyclopedia has no demo dataset (same as the scan import path); screens always read the live public API.
- **Offline banner deferred** (needs NetInfo): stale cache stays rendered and errors offer retry; the visual banner is a fast-follow.
- **Pre-existing flaky suites**: `scan/BeerInfoCardScreen` and `recipes/RecipeDetailsScreen` fail in *full-suite* runs **on main too** (pass standalone) — not introduced here.
- Local pre-push review reconciled (1 Must Have layering fix + Should/Nice items in the second commit); the Codex helper failed again on a CLI arg (`scripts/codex-review.sh` follow-up).

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run ci:check` green (lint + typecheck + format).
- [x] Feature suites green (~130 new tests, H/S/E).
- [x] Conforms to the mobile-catalog conception diagrams (ADR-0013).
- [x] No forbidden patterns (`any`, default exports in src/, direct fetch, hardcoded tokens).
- [ ] CodeRabbit + Codex auto-review addressed.
- [ ] Manual end-to-end run against the Fly encyclopedia.

Relates to epic #1128. Conception: #1213.

author: norcx
body:
## Summary
- Add flavor-specific zombie battle VFX for dance, flag, armor/machine, pool, ice, paper, football, vehicle, and boss profiles without changing combat values.
- Tone down `Hit` VFX by removing the old star/slash/rod-style read as a steel bar; use colored impact flashes, small dust/tick accents, stronger recoil, and light green zombie blood drops instead.
- Sync card-result feedback with plant animation impact timing so pea shots do not trigger zombie hit/death feedback, damage numbers, or HP/block visual refresh before the projectile reaches the target.
- Move result-feedback timing into the card animation system, with defaults for projectile, line sweep, slam, and trap animations plus per-card `feedbackDelayMs` overrides for plants whose attack timing differs.
- Fix the zombie VFX preview so `Hit` restores each sprite to its original pose after playback, including rapid repeated clicks.
- Rework `Death` into a collapse/dust/afterimage read, and make preview Death play one zombie at a time then restore the preview sprite.
- Replace the round bite arcs with jagged tooth marks, and separate bite/claw reads so teeth appear above while claw rakes appear below.
- Add pool-zombie break-wave accents during attacks, plus lightweight Dave hurt feedback with scratch marks, flinch tint, and breath puffs when attacks target Dave.
- Expand the Zombie VFX Preview roster to cover every non-boss zombie plus Dr. Zomboss; add coverage checks so all 30 enemy ids have VFX profiles.
- Keep `Next Attack`/`Death` preview cycling for checking individual zombie attack/death effects.

## Validation
- `node --test test\battle-card-animation-system.test.js`
- `node --test test\zombie-battle-vfx.test.js`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npx prettier --check src\ui\battle\zombieBattleVfx.ts test\zombie-battle-vfx.test.js`

author: a-canary
body:
## Problem (P0, live)

The factory tick was in a CPU hot loop. `~/.cache/arc-factory.log` showed `reapWorktrees()` retrying `git worktree remove` on **main checkouts** every ~5s:

- `/home/aaron/repos/llm-judge` (×2 — rows `llm-judge-ci-minimum-lint-test`, `clarify-docs-plugin-json-drop-provider-m`)
- `/home/aaron/repos/discord-bridge` (`000046-hygiene-discord-bridge-improve-architect`)
- `/home/aaron/repos/conjecture` (`000048-hygiene-conjecture-improve-architecture`)

Each is a **merged** row whose `worktree_path` was misrecorded as a repo's main checkout. In `reapWorktrees()`: the dir exists, `findParentRepo` succeeds, then `git worktree remove` fails with `fatal: '...' is a main working tree`. That path `continue`s **without nulling the row**, so every tick revisits it forever. (`CPU: 2h 32min` on a 1d19h-old service.)

## Fix

- `isMainWorktree(path)`: a main tree has `--absolute-git-dir == --git-common-dir`; a linked worktree's git-dir is `.git/worktrees/<name>`. Robust, no error-string parsing.
- Guard in `reapWorktrees()` before the `git worktree remove`: on a main-tree path, **null** `worktree_path`/`branch` and log `outcome=main-working-tree` instead of attempting the doomed remove. Runs before `git branch -D`, so a branch on the main checkout is left intact.
- New `main-working-tree` `ReapedWorktree` outcome + regression test (real repo, merged row pointed at the main tree; asserts HEAD + branch untouched, columns nulled, one-shot).

## Tests

- `worktree-reaper.test.ts`: **17 pass** (16 prior + new regression)
- `factory.test.ts`: **28 pass**
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean

## Data cleanup (applied separately to live ledger)

The 4 already-misrecorded rows have their `worktree_path`/`branch` nulled directly to stop the live loop immediately; this code change prevents recurrence.

body:
fixes https://github.com/open-metadata/ai-platform/issues/648


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97d64121-b1e5-493d-ba59-49be67ad2b16

added as well navigation between files <> memories

## Describe your changes

Adds the Company Context knowledge-pill pipeline: uploading a file to the Context Center now runs text extraction (`Analyzing`) followed by LLM-driven knowledge-pill extraction (`ExtractingContext`), producing `ContextMemory` entities linked back to the file via `sourceFile` and indexed for semantic search.

**Backend**
- `ContextFileProcessingService` (renamed from `ContextFileExtractionService`): two-stage async pipeline on separate bounded pools (CPU-bound text extraction, network-bound LLM calls). Queue rejection and LLM failures resolve to a `Failed` status with `processingError`, preserving the already-extracted text.
- `ContextMemoryExtractor`: chunks extracted text (paragraph-aligned, 60K chars, max 8 chunks), one LLM call per chunk, dedupes pills by question, creates `ContextMemory` rows with `sourceType=FileExtraction`.
- Generic `LLMCompletionClient` layer (OpenAI/Azure, Bedrock, Google, Anthropic, noop) behind `llmConfiguration`, concurrency-bounded, with structured-JSON parsing and one retry. The provider client is only constructed when `llmConfiguration.enabled=true`, so incomplete creds cannot fail startup while the feature is disabled.
- `ContextMemory.sourceFile` relationship (schema + repository + mapper + batch fetch), `ContextFile.memoryCount`, cascade delete of extracted pills with the file.
- `/system/validate` gains an Object Storage step that runs a live write/read/delete probe.

**MCP**
- `search_company_context`: semantic search over extracted pills (entityType + sourceType filtered), VIEW authorization on contextMemory.
- `get_company_context`: fetch a pill by FQN with the same authorization. Both tools validate params and declare them `required` in tools.json.
- `sourceFile` is now part of the contextMemory search index doc + mapping so search results carry it (existing deployments need an index recreation/reindex to pick up the new field).

**UI**
- `DocumentStatusBadge` showing Uploaded/Analyzing/Extracting Context/Processed/Failed/Unsupported on each Context Center document row.

**Config**
- `objectStorage` in `conf/openmetadata.yaml` is env-overridable and disabled by default (`ASSET_UPLOADER_ENABLE=true` + provider settings to enable).

## Type of change

- [x] Feature

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Unit: `ContextFileProcessingServiceTest` (incl. LLM rejection/failure paths), `ContextMemoryExtractorTest` (chunking, dedupe, caps), `LLMCompletionClient*Test`, `LLMClientHolderTest` (disabled config never builds a provider client), `SystemRepositoryObjectStorageValidationTest` (live in-memory probe), `GetCompanyContextToolTest` / `SearchCompanyContextToolTest` (param validation, authorization denial), `DocumentStatusBadge.test.tsx`.
- Integration: `CompanyContextPipelineIT` — uploads a file, waits for `Processed`, and when an LLM provider is configured asserts pills exist, link back via `sourceFile`, and match `memoryCount`.
- `mvn spotless:check` clean on openmetadata-service and openmetadata-mcp; UI checkstyle sequence run on touched files.

body:
## Summary

Rebuilds the container image on [Docker Hardened Images](https://docs.docker.com/dhi/) and hardens the runtime configuration. This is the follow-up commit that just missed PR #1.

## Changes

- **Dockerfile** now follows the official DHI multi-stage pattern:
  - Build stage `dhi.io/python:3.13-dev` installs dependencies into a virtual environment.
  - Runtime stage `dhi.io/python:3.13` only receives the venv and the application — it has **no shell, no package manager**, and runs as the **non-root user (uid 65532)**.
  - `BUILD_IMAGE` / `RUNTIME_IMAGE` build args allow pointing at an organization's mirrored DHI namespace.
  - `/data` is pre-owned by uid 65532 so named state volumes inherit correct permissions.
- **docker-compose.yml** hardening:
  - `group_add: ${DOCKER_GID}` so the non-root user can read the Docker socket (`export DOCKER_GID=$(stat -c '%g' /var/run/docker.sock)`).
  - `read_only` root filesystem with a `tmpfs` for the heartbeat file, `cap_drop: ALL`, `no-new-privileges`.
- **CI** logs into `dhi.io` before building, since hardened base images require authentication.
- **README** documents the hardened-image setup, socket-group requirement, and bind-mount ownership note.
- Docker connection errors now hint at the socket-group requirement.

## ⚠️ Action required before merging

Add the repository secrets `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` and `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` (Docker Hub credentials with DHI access). Without them, the `main` image publish job will fail at the `dhi.io` registry login. Local builds need `docker login dhi.io` first.

## Testing

- 59/59 pytest cases pass (no Python behavior changes besides an improved error message).
- The image build itself could not be exercised in the sandbox (no Docker daemon); the first authenticated CI build on `main` is the verification step.

author: orolol
body:
The dmtp regime grid (chat/code × 1K/8K/32K) re-run on current main exposed a single collapsed cell: chat@8K MTP4, acceptance 0.770 → 0.589 (62.4 → 44.9 tok/s). A/B on the identical prompt, bit-reproducible: FP8=0 restores 0.770/63.1 exactly.

**Mechanism** (per-position acceptance): position 1 unchanged (0.80), positions 2-4 collapse (0.8/0.8/0.73 → 0.53/0.53/0.47). The MTP head recursion feeds each step the previous step's lm_head argmax — low-margin FP8 flips **compound down the draft chain**. The offline probe (0/28 flips) tested isolated positions and structurally could not see composition; recorded as a verify-perturbation class rule in DAILY.

**Fix**: `QWEN36_LM_HEAD_FP8` becomes tri-state **auto = ON iff mtp==0** (`=1`/`=0` force). Validated: chat@8K MTP4 (auto→BF16) **64.7 / acc 0.787** — above the pre-merge 62.4 thanks to the cycle work; MTP=0 @3K (auto→FP8) **61.6 tok/s** cell record with −1.18 GiB; parity floor sane; the synthetic MTP=4 gate returns to its BF16 baseline.

Also ships the full regime grid on current main in DAILY (DFlash code 1K/8K at 215.6/117.7 with AL 9.4-9.5 intact, +7% at 8K from the qh-grid verify) and the routing defaults it implies.

author: kfurufuru
body:
## 背景

2026-06-11 の 07-site 退避（PR #7/#8/#10）で「機微語が残っていないこと」の検証を生バイト grep で行い、search_index.json の `\uXXXX` エスケープにより**何を聞いても「不在」と返る空振りPASS（vacuous pass）**が発生した（正対照を入れて初めて検証器の故障が発覚）。本PRはこの事故クラスの恒久対策を ei-wiki 本体の CI に組み込む（.secretary 側 PR #214/#220 の水平展開）。

## 変更内容

### 1. scripts/check_public_leak.py 新設（漏えい検査・正対照つき）

- **FORBIDDEN 13パターン**: `07-site` / `ei-wiki-private` / コンビナート / 実名（漢字・異体字・ローマ字）/ メール指紋 / ローカルパス / 鶴見 等を built `site/` 全数走査
  - 採用前に docs/ 全数調査で各語の正当用途 0 件を確認。**「三菱」は機器メーカー用途 16 件（MELPRO-D / NF125-SV / FR-A800 / MELSEC 等）があるため意図的に対象外**
- **生バイト grep はしない**: HTML 実体・URL%・`\uXXXX`（ensure_ascii 形）の復号ビュー＋NFKC シャドーを走査。**sitemap.xml.gz は gzip 展開して走査**（コンテナをスキップしない）。zip/pdf は site/ に存在した時点で NG
- **正対照3層**（検出器が死んだら「漏えい 0 件」ではなく FAIL する構造）:
  1. `--self-test`: 全パターンが自分の正対照サンプル（FORBIDDEN 第3列）を検出できるか＋エンコード形プローブ（\uXXXX・HTML実体・URL%・全角・ゼロ幅・gzip）
  2. site 正対照: 「確実に存在する公開語」（search_index 復号後の `計装`・sitemap 展開後の `03-keiso`・index.html の `計装`）が見えるか
  3. `scan_site` 冒頭で self-test を内蔵実行（CI の独立 step に依存しない）

### 2. CI 組み込み（pr-check.yml / deploy.yml）

build 後に `--self-test` → 漏えい検査。deploy.yml では検査失敗で build job が落ち、**deploy job に到達しない fail-closed ゲート**になる。

### 3. footer の実名ローマ字を公開アカウント名へ（mkdocs.yml）

検査器の初回実走査が、**全ページ footer の `© 2026 Furutachi`（実名ローマ字）294 件の露出を実検出**。記入例の漢字姓を PR #9 でプレースホルダ化した方針と同じ向きで、公開アカウント名 `kfurufuru` に変更した。

## 検証

- 正常系: `mkdocs build --clean` → **169 ファイル走査・漏えい 0 件・site 正対照 3/3 検出**（copyright 修正前は 294 件検出＝検出器の感度実証）
- adversarial 11/11 PASS:
  - E1 生の漏えい語 HTML 注入 → exit 1
  - E2 `\uXXXX` エンコード漏えいを JSON 注入（事故同型）→ exit 1・復号後検出ラベル
  - E3 gzip 内漏えい → exit 1（展開層）
  - E4 .zip コンテナ設置 → exit 1（存在自体 NG・名指し）
  - E5 search_index.json 削除 → exit 1（正対照喪失＝空振り防止）
  - E6 検出器沈黙化 → `--self-test` exit 1／E6b 同状態の site 走査も内蔵 self-test が exit 1
  - E7 site 不在 → exit 2

## 変更しなかった箇所

docs/ 本文・nav・既存ページ（一切無変更）。`mkdocs.yml` は copyright 行のみ。

## マージ時の挙動

main へのマージで deploy.yml が走り、**新ゲートを通過した上で**全ページ footer が `kfurufuru` 表記で再公開される（コンテンツ変更は footer のみ）。

body:
## Contexte

Lot **« Page voyage — UI/UX »** de la recette #649. Tous les correctifs portent sur la page d'un voyage (`trip-planner.tsx` et ses sous-composants) en respectant le design system existant (tokens Tailwind, couleur `brand`, icônes `lucide-react`, i18n `fr`/`en` au tutoiement).

## Items traités

1. **Top bar** — les actions du trip (téléchargements GPX/FIT, undo/redo, partage, configuration) quittent la top bar globale et passent sur la ligne du **titre du voyage**, alignées à droite, via un nouveau composant `TripActions`. La top bar globale ne porte plus que les contrôles app-wide. Le **bouton de fermeture** du trip (qui ne faisait que revenir à « Mes voyages ») est **supprimé**. Modif de `top-bar.tsx` limitée au strict retrait des actions du trip (compatible avec le lot logo-langue/thème).
2. **Bloc d'étape** — suppression de la **timeline verticale** ; la **timeline horizontale** est désormais **toujours affichée au-dessus des jours** (sticky). Opacité de la bordure de l'étape active réduite (`ring-brand/40` → `ring-brand/20`). L'étape devient **active au scroll** (scroll-spy via `IntersectionObserver`). En mode **liste** les cartes occupent **100 %** de la largeur ; le bloc **difficulté** passe en cellule compacte alignée sur « Distance »/« Dénivelé » (vue **carte+liste** inchangée : jauge complète).
3. **Distance** — crayon déplacé **à côté de la valeur** + **tooltip** expliquant l'impact sur les autres étapes. Saisie revue (input + suffixe `km`, boutons confirmer/annuler, plus de troncature).
4. **Dénivelé** — icône de **montagne** dans le titre ; **flèche rouge** (montée) placée devant le D+, en miroir de la flèche bleue devant le D-.
5. **Budget** — suppression de « 2 repas + hébergement » ; **icône d'information** avec **tooltip** sur le mode de calcul.
6. **Alertes** — marge ajoutée sous la dernière alerte, avant la barre horizontale.
7. **Crayons d'édition** — pictogramme crayon à côté des **dates** et du **profil** pour signaler qu'ils sont modifiables.
8. **Bloc « Dates non renseignées »** — repositionné **sous les infos du trip**, **au-dessus** de « Les données détectées… », style d'alerte (amber) conservé.
9. **Progress bar de création** — **masquée une fois le trip chargé** (Acte 3) ; elle reste sous le header pendant la création. Supprime aussi la duplication de la barre des jours dans le header collant (source unique : la barre sticky au-dessus des jours).

- **Baselines visuelles** (`tests/visual/**`, non exécutées en CI) à **régénérer** (`make visual-test`) : la barre de config (bouton supprimer) et la page voyage ont changé.
