author: naimkatiman
body:
> Stacked on Phase 3 (PR #115). Base will retarget to `main` once #115 merges. Diff here is Phase 4 only (18 commits, aa1ca52..04a3b56).

## The headline: the walk-forward gate FAILED on paper — and that is the machinery working

Phase 4 builds the honest measurement + shadow machinery the umbrella plan specified, then measures the current strategies against the gate. The measurement says: **do not deploy.**

Per-regime walk-forward on BTC/ETH/SOL H1 (2024-06 → 2026-06), after crypto-perp costs + live ATR geometry (`docs/research/experiments/regime-routed-walkforward-...json`, REGISTRY 2026-06-11):
- **Trend route** (momentum + EMA-50-slope + ADX≥20, the only cells with trustworthy sample size n=142–203): **NEGATIVE on all three symbols** (−0.19% to −0.67% expectancy/trade after costs).
- **Volatile / range routes** (vwap-ema-bb mean-reversion): fire too rarely under live H1 geometry — every positive cell is THIN (<30 trades) and inconsistent across symbols.

So the current entry rules have **no deployable per-regime edge after costs** (consistent with Phase 2's −11% live-geometry+costs baseline). The regime engine is correct; it can only route edge that exists. **Live activation of routing/calibration on the Pro broadcast is correctly BLOCKED.**

## What shipped (all behind the gate, nothing changes live behavior)

- **Honest strategy attribution** — both `signal_history` writers (cron + request path) now stamp the strategy that ACTUALLY ran (`scanner` / `classic`), killing the `hmm-top3` misattribution that poisoned the per-strategy track record.
- **Pure regime→strategy router** + trend-route filter (EMA-50 slope + ADX≥20), additive.
- **Calibration features persisted at emission** (migration 051: `pre_boost_confidence`, `mtf_agreement`, `confluence_bonus`, `cost_estimate_pct`) — additive nullable, forward-accruing.
- **Regime-conditioned backtest harness** — drives entry modules directly (dodges the top-3 window cap); 329-bar window saturates the atrPercentile to match the live writer's regime labels.
- **Offline confidence calibrator** (isotonic + logistic, time-ordered holdout) REPORTED through `/api/calibration` — published confidence unchanged; thin-slice metrics nulled.
- **Shadow recorder** (`TRADECLAW_STRATEGY_ROUTER_MODE`, default `shadow`) — logs the would-be router + calibrated-confidence decisions to NDJSON, changing nothing live. This is the forward-data engine to ever revisit the gate.

## Cardinal invariant (verified at branch level)

Published confidence is unchanged, the live broadcast set is unchanged, and recorded rows carry the same broadcast decision as before — only the additive calibration columns + the honest strategyId differ. The calibrator is reporting-only; the shadow recorder only writes NDJSON. No path feeds calibratedConfidence or the router selection back into a published/recorded field.

## Operator actions (also in docs/operators/strategy-dispatch.md)

- [ ] Review migration `051_calibration_features.sql` — auto-runs on deploy (additive nullable, safe).
- [ ] Keep `TRADECLAW_STRATEGY_ROUTER_MODE` unset or `shadow` in prod. Do NOT flip to `active` — `active` does not even enforce in this build; activation is a future operator step.
- [ ] Do NOT activate routing/calibration: the pre-registered gate (per-regime cost-adjusted expectancy > 0 on walk-forward AND ≥4wk shadow) is FAILING on the walk-forward half. The path forward is improving the entry strategies, not flipping the switch.

## Test plan

- [x] Full jest suite green in the worktree: 1315 passed / 0 failed (`--modulePathIgnorePatterns=standalone`).
- [x] `npm run build:all` green (Turbopack, 330 pages) — the final-review-caught `.js`-extension bug is fixed (04a3b56).
- [x] `npx tsc` clean for apps/web and packages/strategies.
- [x] Every commit passed two-stage review (spec + quality); final whole-branch review verdict after the build fix: READY FOR PR.
- [x] Calibrator determinism + known-miscalibration recovery; shadow-recorder invariant test (decisions byte-identical shadow-on vs off); regime-backtest determinism + 329-window saturation.

## Decision this PR puts in front of you

The machinery is honest and complete; the evidence says the current edge isn''t deployable. Next move is a strategy question, not an engineering one: **rethink the entry strategies** (Phase 4.5) and/or **accrue ≥4wk shadow data** and re-evaluate. Phase 5 (execution/webhook) stays gated on this evidence.

author: notanissue
body:
Fixes an intermittent hang in test_pipeline under WSL2's GPU paravirtualization.

## Root cause (confirmed by isolation)
Gather workers busy-spin (`_mm_pause`) when idle, for low dispatch latency. Under
WSL2's GPU-PV that starves the CPU scheduling the VM<->host GPU command/event path
needs, so the GPU stops progressing and a synchronizing thread waits forever.
Native Linux uses GPU interrupts (CPU load and GPU progress decoupled), so it
doesn't occur — an environment interaction, not a code bug.

Isolation evidence: removing the workers OR making idle workers yield the core both
eliminate the hang (10/10); a blocking-sync flag does NOT (workers still spin).

## Fix
After a short busy-spin (256 iters), a long-idle worker `nanosleep`s ~20us to free
the core. Short idle still spins, so tight back-to-back gather keeps low dispatch
latency.

## Result
test_pipeline stable (10/10) → promoted from a manual bench to a registered ctest.
Full suite 11/11 (×3).

author: luka380
body:
…ck safety; VERSION 4.0.0->4.1.0

Root-caused live on two EXBanka stacks (bank1 111 <-> bank2 222): a cross-bank option accept whose premium currency the seller has no account for silently destroyed the listing and formed no contract ("saga faulted, listing deleted, not enough money for premium when we had both").

Two compounding defects, both fixed:

1. No FX, buyer-currency denomination. The cross-bank settlement denominates the premium in the BUYER's bid-account currency; the seller-credit leg resolved the seller's "first active <that-ccy> account" and voted NO_SUCH_ACCOUNT when none existed -> the NEW_TX rolled back. Now interbank-service's PostingExecutor (seller's bank) FX-converts the credit via exchange-service so it lands in the seller's own account currency (reserveIncomingCredit -> fxReserveCredit). Purely additive: with no converter wired the pre-FX NO_SUCH_ACCOUNT/NO_SUCH_ASSET behaviour is kept. Wired EXCHANGE_GRPC_ADDR into interbank-service (config + main + compose).

2. False success + listing loss. InitiateOutboundTxWithPostings always returned Status:"pending", so the inbound accept consumed the listing and reported "accepted" even on a peer NO vote. It now returns the row's real terminal status; PeerOTCGRPCHandler.AcceptNegotiation reverts the claim and returns FailedPrecondition (no listing consume) on rolled_back/failed.

Live-verified: buyer pays 40 CHF in their currency, seller receives the FX-equivalent (~5106 RSD) in their RSD account, contract active, shares reserved, SI-TX committed both sides.

Tests: executor FX unit tests (fallback+convert / no-converter fail-closed / same-currency no-FX); inbound-accept rollback-safety unit test; updated the outbound happy-path status assertion. make ci green (build/test/lint/gofmt/tidy).

body:
## Summary

Adds comprehensive support for persisted timeline sequences and sketch documents as first-class workflow types. Introduces `RenderTimelineNode` for video export, `TimelineTranscriptNode` for script extraction, `AddClipsToTimelineNode` for programmatic timeline building, and sketch rendering/manipulation nodes (`RenderSketchNode`, `SketchLayersNode`, `CreateSketchNode`). Includes property editors for both types with direct navigation to their respective editors.

## Key Changes

**Timeline Nodes** (`packages/video-nodes/src/nodes/timeline.ts`):
- `RenderTimelineNode`: Renders timeline sequences to MP4 via ffmpeg — normalizes video/image clips to sequence resolution, concatenates in start order, mixes audio tracks at timeline offsets with per-clip gain/delay
- `TimelineTranscriptNode`: Extracts transcript text and line array from timeline's transcript data
- `AddClipsToTimelineNode`: Programmatically adds clips to a timeline sequence with media asset references

**Sketch Nodes** (`packages/image-nodes/src/nodes/sketch.ts`):
- `RenderSketchNode`: Composites visible raster layers (respecting opacity, blend modes, visibility, parent group hierarchy) and renders designated mask layer separately
- `SketchLayersNode`: Lists sketch layers with metadata (name, visibility, opacity, blend mode)
- `CreateSketchNode`: Creates new sketch documents with specified dimensions

**Type System & API**:
- Added `sketch` and `timeline` as new data types in `web/src/config/data_types.ts`
- Extended `ProcessingContextModelInterfaces` with `getImageDocument`, `createImageDocument`, `getTimelineSequence`, `createTimelineSequence`, `updateTimelineSequence` methods
- Implemented model interface methods in `packages/websocket/src/unified-websocket-runner.ts` using `ImageDocument` and `TimelineSequence` models
- Added `SketchRef` and `TimelineRef` types to `packages/protocol/src/api-types.ts`

**Property Editors**:
- `SketchProperty.tsx`: Dropdown to select persisted sketches with button to open sketch editor
- `TimelineProperty.tsx`: Dropdown to select persisted timelines with button to open timeline editor
- Both support inline payloads and persisted document references

**Constant Nodes**:
- `ConstantSketchNode` and `ConstantTimelineNode` in `packages/core-nodes/src/nodes/constant.ts` for workflow inputs

**Tests**:
- `packages/video-nodes/tests/timeline-nodes.test.ts`: Behavior tests for timeline rendering, transcript extraction, and clip addition (ffmpeg/ffprobe mocked)
- `packages/image-nodes/tests/sketch-nodes.test.ts`: Behavior tests for sketch rendering, layer selection, opacity/blend wiring (GPU compositing mocked)

**Integration**:
- Exported new nodes from `packages/base-nodes/src/index.ts` and `packages/image-nodes/src/index.ts`
- Added `@nodetool-ai/timeline` dependency to `packages/video-nodes/package.json`
- Registered property resolvers in `web/src/components/node/PropertyInput.resolver.tsx`
- Updated icon mappings in `web/src/config/IconForType.tsx`

## Implementation Details

- **Timeline rendering pipeline**: Clips are encoded to uniform segments (h.264, 48kHz stereo AAC, sequence resolution/fps), concatenated via ffmpeg concat demuxer, then audio tracks are mixed at their timeline offsets with per-clip gain/delay filters
- **Sketch compositing**: Layers decoded from `ntlayer:` base64 JSON payloads (containing image data URL and bounds), placed by translation + transform, composited with GPU via `compositeImageLayers` respecting opacity and blend mode
- **Document persistence**: Sketch and timeline documents are stored via model interfaces; nodes can reference by id (persisted) or inline payload (transient)
- **Error handling**: Clear user-facing messages for missing timelines, empty inputs, missing assets, and missing media files

body:
## CHAT-UI-1 live wiring — the safety machinery validated in integration

Turns the ChatSurface skeleton into a running surface that routes REAL consequential acts through the W1 `ConsequenceConfirm` + W2/W3 provenance — so the guarantees are proven end-to-end, not just in unit tests. Branched off `origin/main` (`61efe3c`, which has W0–W3). **Behind `CHAT_UI_1_ENABLED` (default OFF); inert when off.**

**NON-reviewer scope only** — REVIEWER-ASYNC-DISPLAY-1 re-verified **still unbuilt**, so the reviewer/disposition path stays Gate-0-blocked and is **not** wired.

### Commits
- **WIRE-1** — confirm-orchestration layer (pure `routeConfirmDecision`; `ConsequenceProvider`/`useConsequence` imperative `requestConfirm`; modal overlay; `AutonomySlider`; "N posture confirms waiting" queue bar; durable provenance on confirm/clear).
- **WIRE-2** — deliverable posture strip + send/lock/tier (surface-level acts) + the hybrid issuer scenario.
- **WIRE-3** — matter-identity ingestion confirm + undo-by-band + stale-preview, wired.

### Acceptance — all firing END-TO-END on the live surface (tested)
- **Issuer scenario:** "firm style / no branding" applies silently; "from the owners" surfaces a recorded full-triple confirm (durable issuer entry written + posture applied).
- **Slider / queue / carve-out:** Propose-and-Confirm interrupts; Auto-Act queues batchable posture ("N waiting" → Clear all records `dirty_confirmed`); the BROAD carve-out (adverse/third-party) interrupts individually even in Auto-Act; privileged×adverse HARD-blocks; non-posture acts always interrupt.
- **Send egress check:** send to adverse + undetermined-privilege HARD-blocks.
- **Matter-identity:** set / change / ambiguous → confirm before bind; unambiguous same-matter re-ingest does **not** over-prompt.
- **Undo-by-band:** cosmetic silent; hard-stop → confirm + `{type:'undo'}` reversal recorded.
- **Stale-preview:** acting on a drifted preview (recipient → adverse, privilege unchanged) is caught + re-confirmed against current → HARD.

### For your review (a design choice)
**Auto-Act semantics:** a batchable posture change defers to the queue and records `dirty_confirmed` on batch-clear; the hard-stop floor (HARD / carve-out / non-posture acts) always interrupts. Easy to adjust if you'd prefer different batching.

### Scope / acts
Surface-level acts (your decision): each gates through confirm + writes durable provenance; the underlying mutation is surface state. Backend-mutation wiring (lockedDecisions / sourceAuthority / sendability) is a follow-on.

### Not for merge/deploy
Sole-committer; do not merge / deploy / flip the flag. **No new migrations.** Full local suite run before push (only the known local-env false-fails remain).

author: merlimat
body:
### Motivation

The raft FSM's `Persist` calls `sink.Cancel()` unconditionally — on the success path too. `FileSnapshotSink.Cancel` discards the snapshot, and since `Persist` still returns nil, raft believes the snapshot succeeded and compacts its log anyway. Consequence: **no snapshot is ever retained**, and after a restart following a log compaction the FSM starts empty, the truncated log's entries fail the expected-version check on replay, and the coordinator metadata is silently lost.

### Changes

- `Persist` cancels only on marshal/write failure and only closes on success.
- `Restore` logs after decoding the snapshot (it logged the not-yet-restored state before).

### Verification

`TestStateContainerPersistRetainsSnapshot` drives a snapshot through a real `FileSnapshotStore`: the store must list the snapshot after `Persist` (on the old code the list is empty — verified the test fails pre-fix), and a fresh state container restored from it must carry the document state and version.

Credit: this issue was independently identified in #1047 by @dao-jun, among a broader set of raft-provider fixes. Per the review feedback there, the still-valid fixes are being landed as focused patches — this is the first; resource-lifecycle and leadership-handling PRs follow.

author: adeptofvoltron
body:
Fixes #2961

## Problem
`bootstrap()` rebuilt the cache service with `createCacheService()` on every request container, and an authenticated request constructs 2–3 containers. Under the default memory strategy each instance is process-local, so every cross-request cache was effectively a no-op — RBAC's 5-minute ACL cache, nav, org-scope, business-rules, and the ~42 other `resolve('cache')` consumers re-ran their full query chains on each request. Under the shipped `CACHE_STRATEGY=sqlite` default, each container opened a fresh `better-sqlite3` handle (PRAGMA + DDL churn) and never closed it, so handle count grew with request volume.

## Root Cause
The cache was constructed per request container instead of once per process — unlike the rate limiter (`getCachedRateLimiterService`), which is already a `globalThis` singleton with a SIGTERM/SIGINT close hook.

## What Changed
- **`getCachedCacheService()` in `packages/core/src/bootstrap.ts`** — mirrors `getCachedRateLimiterService` exactly: same DI key `cache`, a `globalThis` key to survive module duplication, a once-registered SIGTERM/SIGINT `close()` hook (closes persistent sqlite/redis handles on exit), and an `OM_CACHE_SINGLETON` escape hatch (default ON). It returns `null` when disabled or when creation fails, so `bootstrap()` falls back to the legacy per-request instance.
- **`bootstrap()`** now registers the shared singleton, falling back to a per-request instance only when the singleton is disabled/unavailable.
- **LRU cap on `createMemoryStrategy` (hard prerequisite)** — added a `maxEntries` cap (default `50000`, configurable via `CACHE_MEMORY_MAX_ENTRIES`; a non-positive value disables it), porting the `rbacDefaultCache` Map-reinsertion LRU precedent, so a now-process-lifetime memory cache can't grow unbounded. Threaded through `CacheServiceOptions` and the memory-fallback path.
- Documented `CACHE_MEMORY_MAX_ENTRIES` and `OM_CACHE_SINGLETON` in `apps/mercato/.env.example` and the create-app template `.env.example`.

It is safe by construction: tenant scope resolves per-call through `AsyncLocalStorage` (`packages/cache/src/tenantContext.ts`) and the service carries no request state, so this targeted hoist does not require the default-OFF `OM_BOOTSTRAP_CACHE` replay.

## Tests
- `packages/cache/src/__tests__/memory.strategy.test.ts` — LRU eviction at the cap, read-refreshes-LRU-position, tag-index consistency on eviction, and non-positive-cap = unbounded.
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/cacheSingleton.test.ts` — singleton identity across calls, working get/set through the shared instance, and the `OM_CACHE_SINGLETON` escape hatch returning `null`.
- Verified: `@open-mercato/cache` 47/47 pass; `@open-mercato/core` 5854 pass (1 pre-existing locale-dependent failure in `DealsKpiStrip.test.tsx`, unrelated — the component formats via `Intl.NumberFormat(undefined, …)` and the test asserts the `en` output `'1K'`; this box's default locale is `pl-PL`). Typecheck green for both packages.

## Backward Compatibility
No contract surface removed or changed. Additions only: optional `maxEntries` on `CacheServiceOptions`/`createMemoryStrategy`, new exported `DEFAULT_MEMORY_MAX_ENTRIES`, and new `getCachedCacheService`. DI key `cache`, the `CacheStrategy` shape, and fallback-to-memory behavior are unchanged. Behavior changes (intentional, per the issue): the cache is now process-shared by default, and the memory strategy now applies a default LRU cap — both gated by env escape hatches (`OM_CACHE_SINGLETON`, `CACHE_MEMORY_MAX_ENTRIES`).

## Security impact
Touches the access-control-adjacent cache path (RBAC's 5-minute ACL cache resolves `cache`). The ACL cache TTL (5 min) and tag-based invalidation are unchanged; the cache simply now persists across requests as originally intended rather than being rebuilt per request. Tenant/organization isolation is preserved — scoping resolves per-call via `AsyncLocalStorage` and the shared service holds no request-bound state, so no cross-tenant leakage is introduced. The new LRU cap can only evict entries (causing a cache miss → fresh authoritative query), never serve another tenant's data. The SIGTERM/SIGINT hook closes persistent cache handles on shutdown.

author: ddaanet
body:
The README notes the 63% figure is directional, and self-reports that the methodology had no model named, single runs, and word counts. This PR adds a reproducible harness so the numbers can be re-derived rather than trusted, plus a run across haiku/sonnet/opus (N=5, raw per-run data included).

It measures two things the original couldn't: real `output_tokens` (not word counts), and whether the *behavior* each test targets actually changes.

**How it isolates the variable:** each prompt runs in a fresh temp dir (baseline = empty dir, treatment = `CLAUDE.md` copied in), `--setting-sources project` to block global settings/hooks, driven through `claude -p --output-format json`. Directional, not a controlled study — N=5, means read as signal.

**Findings (data attached):**
- Output-token reduction is ~1–15% depending on model (chattier model → more to trim), not 63%. On short prompts it's roughly cost-neutral, since the file adds input tokens every turn — consistent with the README's own caveat.
- The behavioral fixes (preamble, sycophancy, "as an AI", closing fluff) register at **0% in the baseline** on current models — there is nothing left to remove. Correctness is identical (100% accurate/complete, judged) with and without the file.
- The em-dash (T3) and multi-version (T4) effects don't appear — the file has no rule for either.

None of this says the file is harmful — it says the headline number needs a model name, a token metric, and a baseline that still exhibits the behaviors. The harness is here so future numbers can have all three.

Everything reproduces:
```bash
for m in haiku sonnet opus; do w=3; [ "$m" = opus ] && w=2; python3 benchmark/run.py -n 5 --model "$m" --workers "$w"; done
python3 benchmark/eval.py --workers 3
```

Writeups: `benchmark/SUMMARY.md` (tokens), `benchmark/SEMANTIC.md` (behavior). Raw per-run records in `benchmark/raw-*.jsonl`. Adds a `benchmark/` dir only; touches no existing files.

author: einsteindark-edgm
body:
## Qué resuelve

**Caso ep_010** (run `fa1eb974`, cliente `573125671604`): el agente **sí llamó**
`search_products` / `get_product_by_handle` y aun así mostró colores inventados
(**"Crema", "Melocotón"**) en el variant picker, recitó **"14 aromas y 10 colores"**
(reales: 11 y 9) y registró la orden con color Melocotón. A la vez, el eval
puntuó `correct_handoff=0.5` *"no escaló a humano"* cuando la history de Temporal
prueba `escalate_to_human(PAYMENT_VERIFICATION_PENDING)` ejecutada (evento 864) —
el juez no ve las tools porque el JSONL no las persiste.

Dos conclusiones → dos frentes:
1. **Lo que el prompt pide, el código lo fuerza** (la instrucción closed-list ya existía y no alcanzó).
2. **El juez necesita evidencia, no inferencia** (falsos negativos en métricas de cierre + razones equivocadas en alucinación).

## Agente — grounding determinista

- **`platform/catalog/variant_attrs.py`** (nuevo): tags `"Aroma:/Color:"` → listas
  cerradas + matching normalizado (case/acentos). Envelopes de `search_products` /
  `get_product_by_handle` exponen `aromas[]`/`colors[]` parseados (el LLM ya no
  cuenta ni parsea prefijos).
- **`present_variant_picker(catalog=…)`**: valida las `options` contra el producto
  real — **descarta** las inventadas (aviso en `removed_invalid_options`); todas
  inválidas → error con las opciones reales. Catálogo caído → degrada abierto.
- **`set_order_slot(catalog=…)`**: aroma/color inexistente **no se escribe** +
  envelope `rejected` con las `available` (el guion del "el rojo no lo manejo",
  pero enforced). Multi-valor ("drakar, café") y canonicalización de casing.

## Eval — el juez deja de puntuar a ciegas

- El workflow **persiste `tools_used`** en el JSONL (campo nuevo — `tool_calls`
  cambiaría el `ui_type` del dashboard). Gated con `workflow.patched` (L-9).
- **`build_system_facts`**: closing_tag / order_id / escalation_reason de metadata
  → al `Scenario` del juez vía `TurnParams.SCENARIO` (soportado por deepeval;
  CONTEXT/CHATBOT_ROLE no — KeyError documentado).
- **Catálogo real al juez**: closed-lists del snapshot en el Scenario →
  `no_hallucination` con ground truth.
- **Rúbrica**: handoff/cierre aceptan hechos del sistema como evidencia;
  alucinación se contrasta contra el catálogo, no contra "¿vi la tool call?".
- **Curación**: candidato a golden si falla una métrica **crítica**
  (`no_hallucination`) aunque el promedio pase.
- **Juez del manifest**: `gemini-backup` → **`gemini-pro-judge`** (paridad con el
  golden de CI; el backup era el fallback del propio agente → self-preference).

## Verificación de comportamiento (gotcha #1)

Re-eval real de `ep_010` in-process (ActivityEnvironment + juez `gemini-pro-judge`
vía litellm local) sobre copia del vault:

| Métrica | Antes | Después |
|---|---|---|
| `correct_handoff` | 0.5 — *"no escaló"* (FALSO) | **1.0** ✓ |
| `no_hallucination` | 0.0 — razón equivocada (*"no llamó search_products"*) | **0.0 — razón exacta**: *"14 aromas y 10 colores cuando el catálogo real tiene 11 y 9; aceptó 'Melocotón' inexistente"* |
| `is_candidate` | False (avg 0.72 ≥ 0.70) | **True** (regla crítica) + candidato escrito |

Bonus del juez con ground truth: detectó que el cliente pidió **"2 de cada una"**
y el agente solo procesó 2× Cruz de Vida — media venta perdida.

## Tests

83 nuevos/actualizados (parser puro, picker/slot con FakeCatalog incl. el caso
ep_010 exacto + degradación abierta, `tools_used` roundtrip, system facts, regla
crítica, rúbrica) · `lint-imports` 4/4 · architecture+premortem 76/76 ·
evals+plugins 449 pass (único rojo: voseo pre-existente §8 — la blocklist de la
propia rúbrica) · compose regenerado.

## Deploy (post-merge)

Rebuild de los workers `chats-sales` (validación de tools + persistencia de
`tools_used`) y `chats-sales_eval` (juez nuevo) + `hubara-api`. Las evals
siguientes (event-driven al cierre) ya usan el juez mejorado; los episodios
viejos pueden re-evaluarse con el backfill si se quiere re-puntuar el histórico.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Adenda: paridad del Golden Eval (GitHub Action)

Revisión del eval de CI (`golden-eval.yml` → `scripts/golden_eval.py`):

**Lo que ya estaba bien (no se toca):**
- Cada escenario corre en **sesión fresca** (`rmtree` + bootstrap) → el equivalente correcto a "por episodio" para un set sintético: cero contaminación entre corridas.
- El juez ve **tools + outputs por turno** (armados en memoria desde el loop real) — el falso negativo de persistencia del online no ocurre acá.
- Juez `gemini-pro-judge` ya configurado en el workflow.
- Hereda automáticamente la rúbrica nueva + `TurnParams.SCENARIO` (usa `all_sales_metrics`).

**El gap (cerrado en este PR):** `grade_judge` armaba el test case sin `scenario=` → el juez del CI **nunca recibía el catálogo real** (los `tool_outputs` van capados a 1000 chars y el envelope del search se trunca), justo en los escenarios anti-alucinación.

**Fix:** `evals/scenario.py` — builder **compartido** entre online y golden (`catalog_ground_truth()` + `build_scenario()`); `eval_activities` delega ahí y `golden_eval.py` pasa el catálogo del **fixture committeado** + hechos del sistema del vault temp. No se pasa el expected del escenario (sería soplarle la respuesta al juez).

**Verificación real:** `--scenario hallucination_precio_inventado` con agente y juez reales → el prompt del juez incluye `CATÁLOGO REAL VIGENTE` y su razón dice *"información exacta basada en el catálogo real del escenario"* — `no_hallucination=1.0`, behaviors 1/1.

author: 3leapsdave
body:
## Summary

Second slice of the cloud URI I/O work (`cloudready`). Builds the credential-indirection and S3 provider layer in `internal/uriio` — the only package that imports gonimbus — and the CLI surface. There is **no actual cloud read/write yet**: `s3://` references remain rejected with an actionable error until the read/write boundaries land in the next slices. The AWS SDK first enters the build graph here, through gonimbus `pkg/provider/s3`, scoped to the seam and covered by the existing dependency-boundary test.

## Credential layer (`internal/uriio`)

- **`Secret`** — a credential value (access key id or secret key) that redacts itself across every output surface: fmt (`%v`/`%s`/`%+v`/`%#v`), structured logging (`slog.LogValuer`), JSON, YAML, and error wrapping. Cleartext is reachable only via `Reveal`, called solely at the provider-construction boundary. Gonimbus's `s3.Config` carries the key as a plain string and does not zero it, so the embedder owns non-logging.
- **`CredentialsConfig` / `LoadCredentialsConfig`** — named handles (profile, region, endpoint, force-path-style, an explicit `insecure` opt-in, and discouraged literal keys). The loader is fail-closed (strict unmarshal: a typo'd field is an error), enforces owner-only file permissions when literal keys are present, validates handle-name slugs and the both-or-neither-key rule, and statically rejects a non-TLS endpoint unless the handle opts in with `insecure: true`.
- **`Resolver`** — resolves a handle to its config with CLI-override > config > default-chain precedence; a missing named handle fails loud; the implicit `default` handle resolves through the AWS default credential chain. The cleartext `s3.Config` is built only at the construction boundary and never returned, logged, or persisted.
- **`ProviderPool`** — one gonimbus `s3.Provider` per unique `(handle, bucket)`, lazily constructed, reused for the run lifetime, closed together.

## CLI (`extract files`)

- `--credentials <path>` and repeatable `--credential handle=profile`. The override is a profile reference only; a value shaped like a raw AWS key is rejected so secrets never land in argv / `ps` / shell history. Credential options are validated up front so a malformed override or a bad config fails fast. A run with no credential options does no credential work, so zero-config local runs are unchanged.

## Scope

**In:** the credential/provider library, the CLI surface, and their validation/tests. **Deferred to the next slices:** actual `s3://` acquire/publish, staging, cloud listing, and the credentials documentation section. `gs://`/`azblob://` and anonymous/unsigned reads remain out of scope (the provider exposes no anonymous configuration).

## Validation

- Full suite green; the existing local zero-drift behavior is unchanged
- Tests cover secret redaction across every surface (secret key **and** access key id, including YAML), literal-key file-permission enforcement, fail-closed config parsing, handle/endpoint validation, CLI raw-key rejection, resolver precedence, per-`(handle, bucket)` pooling, and an opt-in moto/MinIO integration scaffold (skipped without an endpoint)
- `make check-all` clean · `make security-scan` clean (gosec 0 issues, govulncheck 0 vulnerabilities over the newly added AWS SDK surface)
- Dependency boundary clean: the AWS SDK is admitted, with no CLI/server/index-store or other denied dependencies entering through the seam
- Alpha coverage gate met (`internal/uriio` 84.7%, overall 63.3%)

## Backward compatibility

Local and bare-path runs behave exactly as before. The new flags are inert unless supplied; supplying them only validates the credential surface in this slice.

author: jeremyspofford
body:
## What

Two items (same working branch):

1. **Roadmap #7 — Wake-on-LAN** (implementation, fully verified)
2. **Deep Think + Inference Endpoint Pool design spec** (docs only — the "local models performing like frontier models" discussion)

---

## 1. Wake-on-LAN

The mini-PC wakes the GPU Dell. Closes out the split-deployment story from the recommended-models spec.

- **Config is one secret**: add `wol_mac` in Settings → Secrets with the inference host's MAC. No secret = feature off.
- **Manual wake**: the Models page's "inference host unreachable" banner now carries a **Wake host** button → `POST /api/v1/llm/hardware/wake` → "Magic packet sent ✓".
- **Auto-wake**: a local completion candidate failing with a connection error fires a rate-limited wake (once/5min) — `local-first` falls back to cloud while the box boots; `local-only` 503s with "sent Wake-on-LAN; retry in a minute or two".
- **Delivery**: bridge-network containers can't emit L2 broadcast, so the optional **`wol-helper` sidecar** (compose profile `wol`, `network_mode: host`, stdlib-only, admin-secret auth) does it from the host; direct UDP broadcast is the fallback.

### Test evidence (live, in-session)

- **A real 102-byte magic packet captured on the wire**: UDP listener on port 9, wake fired through the full agent-core → llm-gateway path — packet verified byte-for-byte; repeated against a live `wol-helper` subprocess plus its 401/422 paths (`tests/test_wol.py`, 4/4, in `make test-v2`; capture tests skip without root).
- **Playwright 3/3**: killed Ollama → banner + Wake button → click → confirmation.
- Unit 12/12 (packet construction, MAC formats, rate limiting, error classification). Ruff + tsc clean.
- Bonus: Models page now shows `manifest: remote` — #23's daily manifest refresh pulled from main in real conditions.
- **Not verifiable here**: an actual machine waking (no LAN/sleeping host in the sandbox). Dell-side test: enable WoL in BIOS/NIC, add the secret, enable the `wol` profile, sleep it.

## 2. Deep Think + Endpoint Pool spec

`docs/specs/2026-06-11-deep-think-endpoint-pool-design.md` — technique triage of the test-time-compute menu (verified execution = already Nova's core, gets acceptance gates; Mixture-of-Agents = centerpiece, parallel proposers across the endpoint pool; grounded-only reflection; ToT/MCTS deferred; LangGraph/CrewAI rejected — Nova is the orchestration layer). Endpoint pool generalizes `LOCAL_INFERENCE_URL` to N machines with per-endpoint discovery/hardware/pull/WoL; Deep Think is an opt-in `effort: "deep"` mode with hard caps, kill switch, daily budget, and a non-gating quality audit harness it must pass before earning prominence. Five-increment plan; burst (`on-demand` endpoints) reserved but out of scope. Roadmap Next Up #4.

## Roadmap

Items #4–#7 moved to "Shipped 2026-06-10/11"; deep-think/pool added as the new Next Up #4 alongside the three older standing items (voice TTS, agent-loop hardening, production nginx).

author: amaurymagalhaes
body:
## Summary

Form validation across the funding/application forms had required-ness declared ad-hoc in multiple unconnected places, so the Zod schema (which the resolver enforces) and the visible required indicator (asterisks / `isRequired`) could disagree. The headline symptom (#1179) was milestone submission being blocked by a "Milestone description is required" error even though the UI advertised the description as optional.

This change introduces a single source of truth for required/optional/length/url/email string validation and makes every required indicator a projection of the schema, so the rule and the indicator can never drift apart again.

## Root cause

Required-ness was hand-maintained in two layers that were not connected:

- The Zod schemas enforced by `zodResolver` declared `.min(1, "... is required")` per field.
- The UI components separately hardcoded asterisks and `isRequired` props.

On top of that, the **same milestone form existed twice** — once in the FundingPlatform admin/edit path and once in the public whitelabel applicant flow — and the two copies disagreed on whether `description` was required. The public apply flow (the place an end user actually hits) still required the description, so #1179 remained reproducible there.

## What changed

- **Shared Zod primitives** (`utilities/validation/zod-primitives.ts`): `requiredString`, `optionalString`, `requiredUrl`, `optionalUrl`, `optionalEmail`. `requiredString` chains `.trim().min(1, "{label} is required")` BEFORE any length `.min`, so empty input always reports "is required" and never a length message (#1506).
- **Repeatable milestone/metric schemas extracted** to `components/FundingPlatform/ApplicationView/lib/repeatable-item-schemas.ts`. `description` is now `optionalString()`. `MILESTONE_FIELD_REQUIRED` / `METRIC_FIELD_REQUIRED` are derived from the schema; `MilestoneInput`/`MetricInput` render asterisks and `isRequired` from those maps, and the dead per-`Controller` `rules={{ required }}` props (ignored under `zodResolver`) were removed.
- **Public applicant milestone flow migrated** (`src/features/applications/lib/schema-builders/milestone-schema.ts`, `src/features/applications/components/MilestoneItem.tsx`): milestone sub-field validators now use the shared `requiredString`/`optionalString` primitives, `description` is optional, and `MilestoneItem` derives its asterisks from the new `MILESTONE_ITEM_FIELD_REQUIRED` map. This closes the second, live copy of the #1179 bug so both milestone paths now agree.
- **Onboarding page migrated** (`app/ai-teams/onboarding/page.tsx` + `onboarding-schema.ts`) from raw `useState` + truthy `canSubmit` to `useForm` + `zodResolver` with inline `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby` errors; the existing `useProvisionOrg` React Query mutation and error panel are preserved and the submit button gates only on `isPending` (#1426).
- **Program registry + contributor dialog** schemas (`src/features/program-registry/schemas/public-form.ts`, `base.ts`, `components/Dialogs/ContributorProfileDialog.tsx`) use `requiredString`, with new `MESSAGES.REGISTRY.FORM.NAME.REQUIRED` / `DESCRIPTION_REQUIRED` so empty fields read "is required" while length messages are preserved (#1506, #1508).

## Testing

- Targeted Vitest across the touched schemas/components/pages (zod-primitives, repeatable-item-schemas, milestone-schema, MilestoneItem, MilestoneInput, MetricInput, onboarding, ContributorProfileDialog, programFormSchema, ApplicationSubmission, CreateProgramModal, ProgramDetailsTab) — all green, including new cases proving the public apply flow accepts an empty/missing milestone description and that the description label no longer renders an asterisk while required fields still do.
- `tsc --noEmit` on the whole project: 0 errors.
- Biome on all changed files: clean.

Closes #1179, #1426, #1506, #1508

author: sameerparekh
body:
## Summary

Closes #1644. Adds Grafana dashboard panels for the `sni_clienthellos_total{result}` metric emitted by the #573 SNI hostname-attribution sidecar.

Two panels added to the existing **router-fleet** dashboard (`deploy/grafana/dashboards/router-fleet.json`), which is already the home of `dns_queries_total` — the SNI sidecar is the connection-layer complement to DNS attribution, so it fits this dashboard. No `infra/grafana/main.tf` change needed (dashboard already registered).

- **SNI ClientHello rate by result** — `sum by (result) (rate(sni_clienthellos_total{env="$env"}[5m]))`, stacked, to see the parsed-vs-failure mix.
- **SNI truncation / IPv6-skip ratio** — `truncated` and `ipv6_skipped` each as a fraction of all captures (`clamp_min` denominator to avoid divide-by-zero), so operators can spot snaplen ([#1652](https://github.com/wifihaven/wifihaven/issues/1652)) and IPv6 ([#1653](https://github.com/wifihaven/wifihaven/issues/1653)) attribution gaps.

Slices **only** by the bounded `result` label (`parsed | truncated | no_sni | ipv6_skipped | not_tcp | malformed`) — never by mac/domain/ip.

## Metric shape verified against source

Per the "dashboards must match emitted metrics" rule, the PromQL targets the exact series PR #1643 emits. From #1643's diff:
- `MetricGuard.Allowed`: `"sni_clienthellos_total" -> Set("result", "router_id", "installation_id")`
- agent fold: `metrics.fold_external(mreg, "sni_clienthellos_total", "result", by_result, sni_results_baseline)`
- the zio-prometheus connector does **not** append `_total`, so the on-the-wire name is `sni_clienthellos_total` as written.

## ⚠️ BLOCKED ON #1643 — do not merge first

The `sni_clienthellos_total` series is introduced by **PR #1643 (branch `feat-573`), which is not yet merged.** On `main` the metric does not exist in `api/src`, so these panels would render no-data if deployed first. **This PR must merge AFTER #1643.** Labeled `blocked-on-#1643`.

## CI gate (`grafana-terraform`) — all green locally

- `python3 -m json.tool deploy/grafana/dashboards/router-fleet.json` ✅
- `terraform fmt -check` (infra/grafana) ✅
- `terraform validate` (infra/grafana) ✅

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The Dockerfile used `node:18-alpine`, which is based on musl libc and lacks OpenSSL. Prisma's schema engine is a native binary that dynamically links against OpenSSL, so `prisma db push` at runtime crashed with "Could not parse schema engine response", preventing the Node server from ever starting and causing all healthcheck attempts to fail.

## Solution

Switched the base image from `node:18-alpine` to `node:18-slim` (Debian-based), which includes OpenSSL by default. Also moved `prisma db push` from `startCommand` to `preDeployCommand` in `railway.json` — the Railway-recommended pattern that runs the migration in a separate container before the app starts, surfacing migration failures immediately rather than cycling through healthcheck retries.

### Changes
- **Modified** `Dockerfile`
- **Modified** `railway.json`

### Context
- **Deployment**: [#3a11cb](https://railway.com/project/03743c60-1c14-41c0-b867-76db77c2e741/environment/9432aefc-f245-49b0-bba0-456a41e7b5c1/deployment/3a11cb4d-aaf0-41c0-a3b3-348a48be9e9f)

PR Summary by Qodo

Support sending email to multiple recipients ✨ Enhancement ⚙️ Configuration changes 🕐 10-20 Minutes

Walkthroughs

Description 
• Extend email sender function to accept multiple recipient addresses.
• Update LLM input context and function schema to use to_address_list.
• Log all recipients in the success message for better traceability.
Diagram
```mermaid graph TD A["FunctionArgs JSON"] --> B["LlmContextIn (to_address_list)"] --> C["HandleEmailSenderFn"] --> D["MimeMessage (To: many)"] --> E{{"SMTP server"}} ```
High-Level Assessment
The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Backward-compatible input (accept both keys) - ➕ Avoids breaking existing agents/tools still sending `to_address` - ➕ Allows gradual migration while keeping `to_address_list` as canonical - ➖ Slightly more parsing/validation logic - ➖ Requires clear deprecation plan and cutoff
2. Polymorphic `to_address` (string or array) - ➕ Most flexible for callers - ➕ Single parameter name reduces schema churn - ➖ Weaker schema guarantees (harder validation/documentation) - ➖ More complex deserialization (JsonElement/custom converter)
**Recommendation:** Keeping an explicit `to_address_list` is a good, strongly-typed contract. Consider short-term backward compatibility by also accepting the legacy `to_address` field (and mapping it into the list) to prevent breaking existing function callers; then deprecate and remove after clients migrate.

### Motivation
- Der Geo-only-Fallback in `prediction._append_kinematic()` rechnete Pixelversatz fälschlich mit `PX_TO_KMH / 60.0` in km um, was (nach B115) zu einer starken Unterprojektion führte und Ortswarnungen verzögern kann.

author: devteamaegis
body:
## What's broken

`ParseCrontab` panics on a crontab that contains an environment line with an empty value, e.g. `FOO=` — a valid Vixie-cron construct (clearing/setting a variable to empty). Instead of parsing it, supercronic crashes at startup:

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
  github.com/aptible/supercronic/crontab.ParseCrontab
      crontab/crontab.go:88
```

## Why it happens

The env regex `^([^\s=]+)\s*=\s*(.*)$` lets the value group match the empty string, so `envVal == ""`. The quote-stripping block then indexes `envVal[0]` unconditionally. The existing `FOO=''` test doesn't hit this because there `envVal` is `"''"` (length 2) at that point; only a bare `FOO=` produces a zero-length value.

## Fix

Guard the quote check with `len(envVal) > 0`. Empty values parse to an empty string, consistent with the existing `FOO=''` behaviour.

## Test

Added a `FOO=` case to `TestParseCrontab` asserting it parses to `{"FOO": ""}`; panics before, passes after.

author: iradaharoni-novee
body:
## What

Fixes a missing match in the live tab and makes live scores update every minute.

- **Live tab bug:** the tab filtered on the synced `status` enum, which only refreshes once a day, so a match that kicked off after the last sync was still `SCHEDULED` and fell into no tab bucket — disappearing from every tab (confirmed on the live Mexico vs South Africa opener). Live state is now derived from kickoff time via a new `isMatchLive` helper, and buckets are exhaustive, so the LIVE badge is consistent across the match list, detail page, and `/me`.
- **Live scores:** a new throttled `/api/live-scores` endpoint runs a lightweight score/status sync, and a viewer-mounted `LiveScoreRefresher` polls it every 60s and refreshes the page in place while a match is in play. football-data.org is hit at most once per minute across all viewers via a `Setting`-row throttle, and nothing runs when no match is live.

## Tests

`isMatchLive` and the live-sync write-selection logic are unit-tested; full suite (78), `tsc`, and lint all pass.

author: devteamaegis
body:
## What's broken

`rewriteUnknownContent` — the helper that sanitizes untrusted/old-schema JSON before loading it into the editor — throws a `TypeError` when a node's `marks` or `content` array contains a `null` (or `undefined`) entry, instead of cleaning it out:

- a `null` in `marks` → `typeof mark === 'string' ? mark : mark.type` reads `null.type`;
- a `null` in `content` → the entry is recursed into and `.marks` is read off `null`.

```
marks: [null]            => TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'type')
content has null child   => TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'marks')
```

## Why it happens

Both iteration sites assume every array entry is an object; there's no nullish guard before dereferencing. The function already tolerates other malformed shapes (a mark missing `type`, a string mark), so nullish entries are a gap in an otherwise defensive routine.

## Fix

Drop nullish entries from `marks` and `content` (the existing `.filter` then removes the emptied content slots) instead of dereferencing them.

## Test

Added `rewriteUnknownContent` cases for `null` in `marks`, `null` in `content`, and a valid-input baseline; the two malformed cases throw before and pass after, valid input is unchanged.

author: amiantos
body:
Closes #169.

Adds a guided **"pick a network"** first step to the add-network flow, backed by a curated catalogue of well-known IRC networks, so a new user picks a network and just supplies a nick.

## Catalogue
`vue_client/src/utils/builtinNetworks.json` (+ typed `builtinNetworks.ts`). **94 networks** — the netsplit.de top-100 minus a handful (adult/NSFW, unverifiable hosts, one duplicate). Each entry has verified host/port/TLS + official website, hand-reviewable `tags`, `saslLikelyRequired`, and current netsplit user/channel counts (a point-in-time snapshot — they drift). `lurker` is a special marker tag for networks with an active `#lurker` channel.

## Picker (`NetworkPicker.vue`)
- **Search** matches network **name + tags** (partial, case-insensitive).
- **Single-select** tag filter, collapsed behind a filter icon beside the search box.
- **Clickable cards** (the whole card selects), distinguished by a filled background; each shows the name, comma-separated tags, and `👥 users · # channels` counts. Lurker-friendly networks show a warn-coloured `#lurker available` badge.
- **Sort:** lurker-tagged networks float to the top, then by users.
- **"Enter details manually →"** escape hatch to the blank form.
- On phones (<480px) the tags + badge are dropped to avoid cramping.

## Form integration (`NetworkForm.vue`)
- Add-flow opens on the picker; editing skips it. Selecting prefills name/host/port/TLS and a default channel (`#lurker` for a lurker-tagged network, else `#chat`, so you always land in a channel). "Enter manually" clears the prefill.
- **Node-mode SASL hint:** for a `saslLikelyRequired` network on a hosted cell, the SASL labels drop "(optional)" and a hint explains the creds are required (gated to node edition — self-hosters don't see it). SASL fields always show otherwise.

## Misc
- `AppModal` gains an opt-in `fillHeight` so the picker holds a stable height while the list filters (desktop only).
- Global placeholder text dimmed so it no longer reads as typed content.

## Notes / open items
- Counts are a netsplit snapshot and will drift; re-pull periodically.
- 4 adult/NSFW networks were held back and 11 medium-confidence hosts could use a spot-check (see commit history); the tag vocabulary is operator-curated.

author: riccardo-perotti
body:
`Field::makevalue` now stamps the otherwise-anonymous `invalid value` error with an **opaque** locator:

```
invalid value [c37.225.1486:len15_digit+comma]
```

Format: `<dbr_instances.tag>.<dbr_tables.id>.<dbr_fields.id>:<value-shape>` — numeric ids + a value *shape* (length/char-classes/ref/undef), never schema names or the raw value, so it's safe for external consumers. Resolve the ids against the dbr config to recover the field.

Inserted **before** the `at FILE line N` backtrace so UnRPC's `$`-anchored strip still removes the file path and `code=internal_error` is preserved. Locator-building is guarded so it can never mask the original error.

(Rebased clean onto current master; supersedes #19, which was cut from a stale master and carried an unrelated CI commit.)

author: devteamaegis
body: ## What's broken `calculateBackoffDelay` computes retry backoff as `time.Duration(math.Pow(2, retryCount)) * baseDelay` and clamps it to a 5s `maxDelay`. For large `retryCount`, the `time.Duration` (int64 ns) overflows before the clamp, wrapping to `0` then negative — so the clamp never fires and failing requests get zero/negative backoff instead of the intended 5s cap. `retryCount` is reachable up to `maxScheduleRetryCount = 120`: ``` retryCount=3 -> 5s (correct, clamped) retryCount=62 -> 0s (bug: no backoff) retryCount=63 -> -1s (bug: negative) retryCount=119 -> -1s (bug) ``` A negative/zero duration makes the backlog reschedule immediately, turning the backoff cap into a retry storm — the opposite of its purpose. ## Why it happens `math.Pow(2, retryCount)` converted to `time.Duration` and multiplied by 1s overflows int64 around `retryCount >= 62`; the overflowed value is `<= maxDelay`, so `if delay > maxDelay` is skipped. ## Fix Clamp the exponent before the power: if `retryCount` exceeds a safe bound, return `maxDelay` directly. ## Test `TestCalculateBackoffDelay` asserts retryCount 62/63/119 return the 5s cap (not 0/negative); fails before, passes after. Full scheduler package still green. --- ## Summary by cubic Clamps the retry backoff exponent in `pkg/scheduler` to prevent `time.Duration` overflow that caused zero/negative delays and retry storms. High retry counts now correctly return the 5s cap. - **Bug Fixes** - Clamp before power: if `retryCount` > 32, return `maxDelay` (5s). - Added `TestCalculateBackoffDelay` to cover large counts (62, 63, 119) and assert non-negative, capped delays. Written for commit 8f87ad082cc2bfabe243d80a77c16454c6b1b520. Summary will update on new commits.

author: bendstaples7
body: ## feat: HubSpot contact sync, property detail redesign, and task pipeline fixes ### Summary This PR fixes the root cause of HubSpot contacts (e.g. "Luke") not appearing in the platform even when associated with a deal in HubSpot, and redesigns the property detail page to match a HubSpot-style layout with persistent sidebar. It also fixes the Follow-Up Overdue queue count discrepancy (241 vs 5) caused by tasks being imported with incorrect due dates. --- ### Contact Sync Fixes **Root cause:** Properties showed stale original import owners (e.g. "Gary Carlson") instead of current HubSpot contacts because: 1. `owner_first_name`/`owner_last_name` flat columns are set at import time and never overwritten by HubSpot enrichment 2. HubSpot contact records had `internal_record_id = NULL` in `hubspot_matches` — no link to any property 3. The deal for the property had no confirmed match (address format mismatch: "4263 W Montrose" didn't match "4263 W Montrose Ave Apt 1") **Fixes:** - `property_controller.py`: `_serialize_property_detail` now embeds all linked contacts (`contacts[]`, ordered primary-first) in the API response — no extra round-trip needed - `hubspot_matcher_service.py`: - Address normalizer now strips unit/apt suffixes (`Apt 1`, `Unit 2B`, `Suite 300`) before comparison - Address matching uses prefix matching so "4263 W Montrose" matches "4263 W Montrose Ave Apt 1" - Single-match address deals are **auto-confirmed** (no human review needed when there's only one candidate) - `enrich_lead_from_contact()` now auto-creates a `Contact` + `PropertyContact` row when enriching a lead, with deduplication: checks if a contact with the same name is already linked before creating - `run_hubspot_matching` now re-evaluates `pending` matches (not just `UNMATCHED`) so address matches can be upgraded to `confirmed` on the next run - `hubspot_tasks.py`: - Deal-association loop also updates the contact's `HubSpotMatch.internal_record_id` when it was `NULL` - New "unresolved contacts" loop resolves contact matches with `internal_record_id=NULL` by looking up their deal associations - `hubspot_client_service.py`: contacts are now fetched with `associations=deals` parameter (though HubSpot's legacy API doesn't populate it, the deal→contact direction works correctly) **Deduplication:** Bulk cleanup removed 2,804+ duplicate `property_contacts` rows caused by the earlier broken dedup logic. New dedup guard checks by name-per-property before creating. --- ### Search Bar Improvements - Search results now show `"Luke · 4263 W Montrose Ave Apt 1"` format — address always visible so searching by street number shows the property clearly - Search now matches against linked contacts (`contacts.first_name`, `contacts.last_name`) via LEFT JOIN, so searching "Luke" returns the associated property - Search result label tests updated to reflect new format --- ### Property Detail Page Redesign (HubSpot-style) - **Two-column layout**: tabbed main content + sticky right panel (300px, hidden on mobile) - **Center tabs** (default: Activity): Activity (timeline + Log Note/Call), Info, Score, Enrichment, Marketing, Analysis, Contacts - **Right panel** (always visible): Tasks → Property summary (type, beds/baths, sqft, PIN, zoning) → Contacts (with tappable phone/email links) → Tracking (source, notes) - `ContactsSection`: contacts are now tappable — opens a detail drawer showing all phones/emails/notes with "no contact details on file" message when empty - `PropertyListPage`: clicking a row opens a right-side drawer with `ContactsSection` instead of navigating away; "Full Profile" button navigates to full detail --- ### Task Pipeline Fixes - `hubspot_activity_converter_service.py`: task `due_date` now reads from `engagement.timestamp` (the correct field) instead of `metadata.taskDate` (which is never populated by HubSpot's legacy API) - Data fix: 265 tasks that had `due_date = import_time` (bogus) were corrected to use `engagement.timestamp`; tasks with genuinely no due date have `due_date = NULL` and `status = open` - Follow-Up Overdue queue now reflects accurate overdue counts — the 241 platform vs 5 HubSpot discrepancy is explained by HubSpot's "Assigned to me" UI filter, not a data error --- ### Tests Updated - `test_polling_bug_condition.py`, `test_polling_preservation.py`: `_EmptyRelationship` stub extended with `filter_by()`, `order_by()`, `first()` methods; `property_contacts` added to `LeadStub` - `test_hubspot_no_overwrite.py`: updated to accept `confirmed` or `pending` status for single-match address deals (new auto-confirm behavior) - `test_search_controller.py`: label tests and property-based test updated to expect `"Name · Address"` format --- ### What Was Tested - 4263 W Montrose and 3835 W Montrose now show Luke as primary contact in header and Info tab - Searching "4263", "Luke", or "Montrose" all return the correct property - "Follow up with Luke" HubSpot task appears in the property's Tasks panel as overdue - Contacts tab no longer causes a crash or long loading spinner - Contact detail drawer shows "No contact details on file" for contacts with no phone/email - Duplicate contacts do not re-appear after server restarts --- ## Summary by cubic Adds end‑to‑end HubSpot→property contact sync and a HubSpot‑style property detail page with an Activity tab and sticky Tasks panel. Search now uses the primary contact name with “Name · Address” labels, and tasks use correct due dates. - **New Features** - Property detail API embeds `contacts[]` (primary first) with phones/emails; Info tab and right sidebar show contacts; tap to open a detail drawer with Edit/Set Primary/Remove. - HubSpot‑style detail page: tabs (Activity, Info, Score, Enrichment, Marketing, Analysis, Contacts) and a sticky right panel (Tasks, Property, Contacts, Tracking). Activity and Tasks share one command‑center fetch. - Search matches by linked contact names and labels results as “Name · Address,” preferring the primary contact’s name. - Property list row click opens a right‑side contacts drawer; “Full Profile” opens the full page. - **Bug Fixes** - Address matching: normalized addresses strip unit/suite and allow prefix matches; single‑match deals auto‑confirm; ambiguous address matches stay pending with no link; protected fields never overwritten. - Matching runs: skip confirmed/rejected; re‑evaluate UNMATCHED/PENDING; resolve contact matches with `internal_record_id=NULL` via deal associations; contacts import now requests `associations=deals`. - Enrichment auto‑creates and links a `Contact` + `PropertyContact` with per‑property dedup; removed 2,804+ duplicate `property_contacts` and added a guard. - Tasks: `due_date` reads from `engagement.timestamp` only when present; fixed a stale‑state race so completing tasks updates reliably. - Search: prevents “hybrid” names by using the primary contact name exclusively; trims input before enforcing the 200‑char limit. Written for commit 5a88c711bd38a2cf72cf0090e8212a1651fa7e60. body:
## Problem

Feature-Request von Ben über die Bug-Reports-Seite (11.06.2026): Ticket-Vorlagen sollen eine Checkliste enthalten können, die beim Erstellen eines Tickets aus der Vorlage mit übernommen wird. Bisher kennt das `tickettemplates`-Schema kein Checklisten-Feld — Tickets selbst haben bereits eine Checkliste.

## Umsetzung

- **Modell** (`src/models/ticketTemplate.js`): neues Feld `checklist: [{ title: String (required) }]`. Vorlagen speichern nur Titel — `completed`/`completedBy`/`completedAt` gehören zur Ticket-Instanz, nicht zur Vorlage.
- **API v2** (`src/controllers/api/v2/ticketTemplates.js`):
  - `create` und `update` akzeptieren `checklist` im Body.
  - Validierung: Nicht-Array → **400**. Titel werden mit `sanitize-html` bereinigt und getrimmt; Einträge ohne gültigen, nicht-leeren String-Titel werden verworfen. Leeres Array leert die Checkliste.
  - `get`/`single` liefern die Checkliste automatisch mit aus.
- Die Anwendung der Vorlage (Checkliste aufs neue Ticket kopieren) bleibt client-seitig in der PWA — der Server speichert nur.

### JSON-Shape (für die PWA)

Request (create/update): `{ "checklist": [{ "title": "Schritt 1" }, { "title": "Schritt 2" }] }`
Response (create/update/get): `{ "checklist": [{ "title": "Schritt 1", "_id": "..." }, ...] }`

## Tests

- `test/api/ticketTemplates.js`: Erstellen mit Checkliste (2 Einträge), Abruf einzeln, Ersetzen per Update, Leeren per `[]`, **400** bei Nicht-Array (create + update), Verwerfen ungültiger Einträge (leerer Titel, Nicht-String, Nicht-Objekt).
- `test/models/ticketTemplate.js`: Checklisten-Einträge werden gespeichert, `title` ist Pflichtfeld, Default ist leeres Array.
- `npm test`: **301 passing**, `npm run lint`: sauber.

body:
Signed-off-by: Ahmed Hussein (amahussein) <a@ahussein.me>

Fixes #15018.

### Description

This fixes a skip-merge shuffle lifetime bug where `unregisterShuffle` could close a partial shuffle
file handle while a retained buffer, input stream, or Netty file region was still reading from it.
That could surface as failed shuffle reads when cleanup raced with in-flight fetch consumers.

The fix adds reference-counted lifecycle tracking for partial shuffle file handles. Catalog cleanup
now removes metadata immediately but defers the physical handle close until all active retained
buffers, streams, and file regions release their leases. Lease cleanup is hardened so all retained
handles are released even if one release throws.

This also fixes an interrupt cleanup hole in `SpillablePartialFileHandle.doClose()`: if close is
interrupted while waiting for an in-progress spill, cleanup now still releases resources and deletes
the temp file before restoring the interrupt flag.

Tests added or updated:

- `MultithreadedShuffleBufferCatalogSuite`
  - retained skip-merge buffer remains readable across concurrent `unregisterShuffle`
  - `convertToNetty` file-region release closes the retained handle exactly once
- `SpillablePartialFileHandleSuite`
  - interrupted close during an in-progress spill still completes cleanup and restores interrupt state

Validation run:

- `git diff --check`
- `mvn install -pl sql-plugin -am -DskipTests -Dmaven.scaladoc.skip=true -Dbuildver=356`
- `SpillablePartialFileHandleSuite` passed, 18/18 tests

author: epicsalvation
body:
## Summary
Implement the foundational networking layer (M11) with an ENet-based transport backend and a NetworkManager that bridges transport-level peer events to game-level player lifecycle. The implementation maintains strict architectural boundaries by confining ENet types to a single translation unit and providing a clean abstract interface for future transport swaps.

## Key Changes

- **ITransport interface** (`src/net/ITransport.h`): Pure-virtual abstraction defining the transport contract (listen, connect, send, poll, flush) with no ENet types exposed. Supports both reliable and unreliable packet delivery across named channels.

- **ENetTransport implementation** (`src/net/ENetTransport.h/cpp`): Concrete ENet v1.3.17 backend using PIMPL to confine all ENet headers to the .cpp file. Manages bidirectional peer↔PeerId mapping, services the ENet host event loop, and queues inbound packets for polling.

- **NetworkManager** (`src/net/NetworkManager.h/cpp`): High-level session manager that owns the transport, maintains peer→player ID tables, and drives the per-tick poll/dispatch/flush loop. Supports Offline, Server, Client, and HostPeer session roles. Integrates with Engine via optional per-tick update hook.

- **Engine integration** (`src/core/Engine.h/cpp`): Added optional NetworkManager attachment point and per-tick network update call (after world update, before render) to maintain deterministic ordering.

- **CMakeLists.txt**: Integrated ENet v1.3.17 as a static library with platform-specific socket implementations (win32.c on Windows, unix.c on POSIX) and proper include directory isolation.

- **Comprehensive test suite** (`tests/NetworkTransportTest.cpp`): Five integration tests covering loopback connect/disconnect, reliable/unreliable packet delivery, peer lifecycle events, session isolation, and NetworkManager offline mode.

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Architectural separation**: ENet types never appear in public headers; the transport layer is completely decoupled from renderer, physics, and decomposition systems per ARCHITECTURE §15.
- **Stable peer IDs**: Transport-level PeerId (uint32_t) is mapped to game-level PlayerId, allowing the transport to be swapped without affecting game logic.
- **Non-blocking poll loop**: `poll()` services the ENet host and returns one packet at a time, enabling integration with existing game loop without blocking.
- **Channel convention**: Channel 0 = reliable, channel 1 = unreliable (ENet standard), abstracted via the Reliability enum.
- **Graceful offline mode**: NetworkManager with role == Offline is a complete no-op; existing single-player demos are unaffected.

author: leithl
body:
## What

Adds an **Energy** row to the Runtime group of the monthly summary table: per-month kWh = engine-block heater + HVAC.

- **Heater**: on-minutes × `aggregate.HEATER_POWER_W` (180W, fixed resistive load — no meter, the constant is the whole calculation).
- **HVAC**: sum of per-minute `ac_power_w` samples above `POWER_ON_THRESHOLD_W` (200W), full draw of active minutes; idle/standby contributes nothing. Checked live before building: idle currently reads **21W** (June, FP, compressor off) vs the winter-long flat 146W — 200W comfortably clears both, so the existing threshold is reused as the buffer. Inherits the open W-vs-VA caveat on the dongle's meter.

## How

- `config.query_batch_stats` (live-month SQL path) gains two appended columns: above-threshold watt-minutes + `COUNT(ac_power_w)`; threshold passed in by the caller so config keeps zero local imports.
- `aggregate.compute` (rollup path) emits `runtime_stats.heater_kwh` / `hvac_kwh` into `monthly_cache`.
- Old cached months: heater portion reconstructed exactly from cached `on_hrs`; months whose HVAC ran before power logging began (Nov 2025 – Apr 2026) render `X kWh*` with a tooltip — their HVAC energy can never be reconstructed (`ac_power_w` is NULL pre-2026-05-07), so the marker keeps heater-only from reading as the full total.
- `log_temp.py rollup YYYY-MM` (new) backfills a single month's cache, skipping the email. Guards: refuses current/future months (a partial snapshot would permanently shadow live data once the month rolls over, if the monthly cron ever missed) and months with zero readings (typo protection). Monthly summary email gains the same energy figure.

## Verified

- Pipeline test against a scratch disk+RAM sqlite pair: threshold boundary (200W excluded / 201W counted), NULL pre-HVAC rows, UNION dedup path, old-cache fallback, no-HVAC months, rollup guards — all pass.
- Template rendered with jinja2: energy cells, asterisk + tooltip, em-dash fallback.
- Multi-agent review (11 agents) over the diff; 6 confirmed findings all fixed or consciously documented, 1 refuted.
- `scripts/check-cdn-versions.sh`: all pins current.
- Docs reviewed: CLAUDE.md updated (energy row semantics + backfill rules); README untouched (internal-only change).

## Deploy notes

1. `git pull` then `touch switch.py` (changes span `config.py`/`aggregate.py`/`log_temp.py`, which mod_wsgi won't reload on their own).
2. One-time: `sudo python3 log_temp.py rollup 2026-05` — May's cache predates the new stats and is missing ~11.5 kWh of measured HVAC work until re-rolled. Do **not** re-roll earlier months (no-op for energy, and it would erase their legacy `hvac_on_hrs`).

author: egnees
body:
Dataplane connections previously referenced devices by their position in the devices list, so reordering devices silently rewired the topology. Connections now reference devices by name.

Before:
```yaml
connections:
  - src_device_id: 0
    dst_device_id: 1 
```

After:
```yaml
connections:
  - src_device: 01:00.0
    dst_device: virtio_user_kni0
```

What changed:

- Connections now use src_device/dst_device names instead of src_device_id/dst_device_id indices.
- Names are resolved to device indices after the whole config is parsed, so connections no longer have to appear after devices.
- Unknown, empty, or duplicated device names are now rejected at load time, instead of silently indexing past the device array.

Migrated the sample, unit-test, and functional-test configs, and added parser coverage for the new failure cases.

Andrew 2026-06-11: lepos is grace, wit, charm, humor, eloquent free speech from the soul. Translation is one note in the chord, not the whole chord. The previous detector keyed on `_PLAIN_SECTION_RE` (presence of a "Plain:" heading or visual break) which trained the optimizer to produce wall-plus-appendix shape: jargon wall followed by a section that looked-like-translation but was usually restatement-theater.

Changes:

1. `jargon_dump_detector` adds voice-density measurement:
   - Signals: first-person pronouns, contractions, direct address ("you"), sincerity/discourse markers (yeah, honestly, lol, lmao), question marks
   - Density = voice-token-count / word-count * 100
   - `_VOICE_DENSITY_LOW_THRESHOLD = 2.0` (provisional; will tune from 100-label benchmark)

2. Severity rule rewrite:
   - HIGH fires when noise_count >= 6 AND voice_density < 2.0
   - Downgrade to MEDIUM if Plain: appendix with real translation present (backward-compat for replies-in-flight)
   - "No plain section" check is GONE from firing condition

3. Lepos gate deny-message rewritten:
   - No longer prescribes "add a Plain: section after a visual break"
   - Now describes the failure and prescribes voice-rewrite from first word
   - Includes Aria's "lepos as co-care" reframe: jargon-walls steal operator's audit capacity by triggering nod-along reflex

Per prereg-0bd8a79e4be8.

## Test plan

- [x] 28/28 jargon-dump tests pass (22 existing + 6 new)
- [x] 55/55 lepos + operating-loop tests pass overall
- [x] High-jargon + high-voice (no appendix) does NOT fire HIGH (voice carries the lepos)
- [x] High-jargon + low-voice (no appendix) fires HIGH (regression-pin)
- [x] Backward-compat: appendix-with-real-translation downgrades to MEDIUM
- [x] Cherry-picked obligations-gate fix as ancestry so prereg + commit landed without bypass marker

body:
Strengthens the EP-0012 path/identity foundation **test tree** per the coverage review (rf2-orcbow). **Test additions only — no source touched.**

## What changed

Three test files in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/`, +304 lines.

### `identity_cedn1_cljs_test.cljc` (CEDN-1)
- **CLJS js/Date instant encoding** (point 4) — exact `t:...Z` millisecond token, whole-second `.000` suffix, sub-second precision, cross-timezone collapse, and `js/Date` == EDN `#inst` identity. The JVM `java.time` path already had coverage; the `.toISOString` branch can regress independently.
- **`canonical-projection-ordering-contract`** (point 3) — pins the narrow contract: `canonical-bytes` owns ordering **exclusively**; `canonical` returns an `=`-equal, recursively-normalized value whose entry-iteration order is **not** a contract; equality-as-identity `==` `canonical-bytes` `=`. Prevents a later "make canonical ordered" change from silently widening the contract.
- **`duplicate-canonical-keys`** (point 1) — a JVM `java.util.Date` and `java.time.Instant` for the same instant are distinct map keys with identical CEDN-1 key bytes (the map keeps both entries → two colliding key tokens). Documents + pins the current (not-yet-rejected) behaviour, with the spec-correct fail-closed assertion inline for a one-line flip. CLJS leg documents why there is no CLJS map-collision (value-equal `js/Date` keys collapse).

### `path_laws_cljs_test.cljc`
- **`vector-index-container-policy`** (point 5) — direct put/lookup examples over in-range, out-of-range, negative, and non-integer vector segments; in-place vector update vs fresh-map replacement; present-nil written at an index. Pins the intermediate-container policy that the generative laws only implied.
- **`concrete-path-shape-and-root`** — `normalize` sequential→vector coercion, explicit root `[]`, and `:rf.error/bad-path` fail-closed; pins `nil`→`[]` as a flagged gap.

### `frame_classification_cljs_test.cljc` (point 2)
- **`host-object-path-segment-is-not-yet-rejected`** — JVM + CLJS document + pin that an opaque host-object path segment is **not yet** rejected at `reg-frame` (the boundary validates path shape, not segment domain), with the spec-correct `:rf.error/bad-frame-classification` assertion inline for the flip. Plus a positive baseline (`existing-segment-shape-rejections-still-hold`) for valid concrete paths incl. root.

## Surfaced gaps (out of scope — owned by source-fix beads)

Two spec-mandated fail-closed behaviours are **not yet implemented** in the source. They are owned by the correctness/best-practice review beads, not this tests-only coverage bead:
- **Duplicate canonical map keys** (distinct host values → same CEDN-1 key bytes) → `rf2-w9x5fv` item 3 / `rf2-wgutc2` item 1.
- **Host-segment / concrete-path validation** at declaration boundaries → `rf2-wgutc2` item 3 / `rf2-w9x5fv` items 1-2.

These tests document + pin the current behaviour so the gaps stay visible, and carry the spec-correct assertions inline so flipping each to assert rejection is a one-line edit when the source fix lands.

## Quality gates

- `npm run test:cljs` (from `implementation/`) — **green**: `Ran 6676 tests containing 24685 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.`
- `clojure -M:test` (full JVM core suite, from `implementation/core/`) — **green**: `Ran 1233 tests containing 5465 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.` (baseline was 1227/5416 — the additions add 6 tests / 49 assertions on the JVM).

Closes rf2-orcbow.

author: wernerrall147
body:
## Why

The live evaluator calls the raw chat-completions API, which has no concept of Foundry **Tools**. In Azure AI Foundry, Tools (FileSearch/RAG, Code Interpreter, MCP, Function, OpenAPI, ...) attach to an **agent** that runs a model deployed in a **project**. This PR migrates the evaluator's model usage onto a Foundry project so Tools can be added, while keeping the proven chat-completions path as the default.

## Key finding

`model-router` version **2025-11-18** (the exact version already in use) is supported by Foundry Agent Service and works with every tool type, so the cost-optimized routing carries over. eastus does not offer model-router, so we reuse the existing eastus2 account `admin-mo1q7owo-eastus2` (which already hosts model-router with the RBAC the evaluator uses) rather than deploying a second one.

## Azure changes (already applied, reversible)

- Enabled `allowProjectManagement` on `admin-mo1q7owo-eastus2` (additive PATCH; the live model-router deployment and its endpoint are untouched).
- Created Foundry project `qgc-eval-proj` (endpoint `https://admin-mo1q7owo-eastus2.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/qgc-eval-proj`).
- Granted `Azure AI Developer` on the project to the service principal and the Container App managed identity; `Cognitive Services OpenAI User` on the account to the SP.
- Created agent `quantum-advantage-orchestrator` (model-router + Code Interpreter + Microsoft Learn MCP).

## Code changes

- `agents/orchestrator/instructions.py` (new): shared `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, single source of truth, dependency-free so the provisioning script can load it without the KB/Cosmos deps. `evaluate.py` now imports it.
- `agents/orchestrator/evaluate.py`: opt-in `QGC_USE_AGENT` path that runs the agent via the Responses API (`agent_reference`). **Default off** so production stays on chat-completions until validated per environment. `model_used`/`tokens_used` now set in both paths.
- `tooling/provision_foundry_agent.py` (new): create/update the agent and attach Tools; `--smoke` runs one evaluation, `--list` lists versions.
- `agents/orchestrator/agent.yaml`: documents the real deployment (project, endpoint, attached tools) and the roadmap tools (Azure AI Search RAG over `qgcsearcheval`, connected sub-agents).

## Validation

Smoke test through the agent returned schema-valid JSON: FeMoco ground-state energy -> `HPC_PREFERRED` (confidence 0.88), with correct platform reasoning and Azure CycleCloud workspace guidance.

## To enable in an environment

Set on the Container App: `QGC_USE_AGENT=1` (optionally `QGC_PROJECT_ENDPOINT`, `QGC_AGENT_NAME`). The managed identity already has the required roles on the project.

## Next steps (not in this PR)

- Add Azure AI Search RAG tool over the existing `qgcsearcheval` index (needs a project connection).
- Wire the classifier / fact-checker / HPC-comparator / code-generator as ConnectedAgentTool entries.

author: tmfahey
body:
## Summary

- `gusto auth login` was rendering "login complete. You can close this tab." in the browser tab the instant the OAuth callback hit the loopback - before the `/v1/mcp/oauth/token` exchange ran. When the exchange then 400'd, the user saw two contradictory messages: success in the browser, "no_access_token" in the CLI. The loopback now holds the callback response open and only flushes a pass/fail page once `login` knows whether the token actually persisted; `close()` falls back to a neutral "returning to your terminal..." page if the caller bails.
- An `OAuthError` 4xx (e.g. the token-endpoint 400 from the ticket) was collapsing through `toResult`'s `internal_error` catch-all, so the `--agent` envelope was just `{ code: "internal_error", message: "/v1/mcp/oauth/token -> 400" }` - body dropped, no `request_id`, nothing to debug from. `OAuthError` now captures `x-request-id` and `toResult` surfaces both `details` (the response body) and `request_id` so server-side root-causing the 400 has signal to work with.
- Didn't root-cause the 400 itself - reading the OAuth code top-to-bottom, the CLI side looks correct (same PKCE verifier carried through, same `redirect_uri` in authorize and token, `authorization_code` + basic auth on the token request). The DCR registration uses RFC 8252's `http://127.0.0.1/callback` loopback shape, so the auth server should accept the port-bearing redirect at exchange time. The next reproduction should give us body + `request_id` so we can confirm whether this is `invalid_grant` (race / code re-use), a `redirect_uri` exact-match issue, or something else server-side.

## Linked Jira

an internal ticket

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test`, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`
- [ ] Reproduce `auth login --no-browser` against demo and confirm the failure envelope now includes `details` + `request_id`
- [ ] Confirm the browser tab shows "returning to your terminal..." while the exchange runs, then flips to "login complete" only on persisted-token success

author: ntindle
body:
## Why

Every dream pass dies at the recombine phase: Anthropic's newest models reject the `temperature` param outright (`temperature is deprecated for this model`). Verified live against the API: `claude-opus-4-7` and `claude-opus-4-8` reject it, `claude-sonnet-4-6` accepts it. Recombine runs on Opus → every pass errors before apply, on every transport that reaches the direct Anthropic API. Found by E2E-testing the combined dream fix PRs — this is the last blocker between the dream system and a completed end-to-end pass.

## What

- Known-rejecting model families are stripped of `temperature` at both Anthropic seams (sync `messages.create` and the batch request builder).
- The sync path retries once without the param when an unknown future model returns the exact deprecation error (self-healing; logs a warning telling us to extend the list).
- Batch submissions get no retry — their errors surface hours later in result rows, so the deny-list does the work there.

## How

TDD: four scenario tests written first and confirmed failing — sync strip, sync retry-on-unknown-model, batch strip, batch keeps-temperature-for-supporting-models. The phase temperature design (0.2/0.9/0.0) simply can't be honored on models that reject the param; prompt design carries the phase character there.

## Checklist

- [x] TDD; 64 passing in the providers suite
- [x] `poetry run format` clean
- [x] No out-of-scope changes
