author: effortlesssteven
body:
## What

Scratch reclamation currently lives only in `routed-rust.yml`'s inline **Prepare scratch** step, so it runs solely on PR traffic. An idle build runner whose `/mnt/ci-scratch` fills from prior runs never gets swept until the next PR happens to land on it (#1028). This adds a **scheduled** (every 30 min) + `workflow_dispatch` lane that runs the **same** cleanup on a timer.

## Why it's low-risk

- The run block is **copied verbatim** from the inline step that already runs successfully on the `em-ci-small` runners (`routed-rust.yml:130`).
- Age-gated (`-mmin +45` protects active builds), every destructive command is `|| true`, and it only touches `/mnt/ci-scratch/{cargo-home,target,tmp}` + the sccache dir.
- The disk guard is **advisory** (emits a `::warning::`, does not fail the scheduled lane — avoids perpetual-red noise).
- Idle runners — exactly the ones that miss PR-triggered cleanup — are the free ones a scheduled job lands on, so it's well-targeted.

## Verification

- `check-workflows` / `check-file-policy` / `check-executable-files` / `check-generated` green; budget registered in `policy/workflow_allowlist.txt`; YAML validated.
- The new workflow does **not** trigger on this PR (schedule/dispatch only), so structure is gate-validated here; **runtime is verifiable post-merge** via `gh workflow run scratch-gc.yml` (a manual dispatch on a real runner).

Addresses #1028. (#1032 droid-queue was investigated and is an infra/runner-availability issue, not a repo-side fix — the gate deliberately enforces `cancel-in-progress: false`; documented on the issue.)

author: nwoolmer
body:
## Summary

Generalizes the DeepSeek-V4-specific REAP keep-map loader into a model-agnostic **`hipfire-reap`** crate and wires it into 4 MoE arches — **deepseek4, qwen35, lfm2moe, minimax** — so any of them can be selectively **expert-pruned** (emulate a REAP checkpoint) by partial-loading the kept experts from an existing quant, **no re-quantization**. Default-off ⇒ byte-identical load.

This is **Sub-project 1** of a larger design (spec + plan included in the diff under `docs/superpowers/`). SP2–4 (mixed-quant bucketed dispatch, load-time quant overlay, offline bake) are scoped but not in this PR; their seams (`TensorSource.overlay`, `ReapPlan.quant_overrides`) are threaded but inert.

> **Stacking note:** this branch is stacked on the unmerged `nw_reap162b_keepmap` (commit `43ed446d`), so this PR also bundles that ds4 REAP foundation + the spec/plan docs. Review the `hipfire-reap` crate + the 4 arch wirings as the SP1 contribution.

## What's in it

- **`crates/hipfire-reap`** (new): `ReapPlan` (parse/validate `reap_plan.json` + legacy `keep_by_layer.json` alias), `gather_rows` (exact byte row-gather for row-independent quant), `TensorSource`/`ExpertPlan` loader API, `ReapArchHook`. 14 CPU unit tests.
- **4 arch wirings**: each applies the plan at its single public HFQ→config entry point (`HIPFIRE_REAP_PLAN=<dir>`), overrides routed-expert count to the kept count, loads/packs only kept experts via `src(slot)`, and gathers router (+ per-expert routing bias) rows to the kept set. REAP and EP-sharding are mutually exclusive (ds4/minimax guard).
- **Tooling**: generalized `scripts/reap/build_keepall_sidecar.py` (emits generic `reap_plan.json`), updated README.

## ⚠️ Verification status

- ✅ **CPU**: all 5 crates build clean; `cargo test -p hipfire-reap` 14/14.
- ⛔ **GPU-DEFERRED (owed)**: the keep-all **identity NLL gate** (keep-all reproduces each arch's no-plan baseline to ~10 decimals — the safety net for the lift) and the ds4 **K144 PPL/KLD smoke** were NOT run (GPU in use by separate cohere work during development). **These must pass before relying on this in production.**

## Follow-ups (recorded, not in this PR)

- Run the GPU identity gate on all 4 arches + ds4 K144 smoke + legacy-alias check.
- qwen35 EP post-load transform (`shard_all_moe_layers`) lacks the ds4/minimax REAP+EP mutual-exclusion guard (pre-existing footgun).
- qwen35 ParoQuant path (`paro_load_moe_ffn`) doesn't honor the keep-map (HFQ path only).
- `cohere2moe` gets the identical wiring once it merges to master.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test -p hipfire-reap` (CPU) — green
- [ ] keep-all `reap_plan.json` reproduces no-plan baseline NLL to 10 decimals on each of deepseek4/qwen35/lfm2moe/minimax (GPU)
- [ ] ds4 K144: full-256 PPL ≈7.56 vs pruned-144 ≈17.73 through the generic path (GPU)

author: mswilkison
body:
Stacked on #4005 (base: `extraction/frost-signer-mirror-2026-05-26`). Implements item 3 of the review feedback (duplicated, divergent protocol constants) — Rust half; pairs with the Go-side PR #4030 stacked on #3866.

## Problem

Flagged in #4026: the engine validated attempt contexts using `int64_be(MessageDigest[0..8])` with the 1-based wire attempt number (the legacy `signingAttemptSeed` convention), while the Go RFC-21 layer derives `fold(SHA256(KeyGroup ‖ SessionID ‖ MessageDigest))` with 0-based attempt numbers. At Phase-7 wiring, every Go-derived attempt context would fail the engine's strict-mode `validate_attempt_context` — a deterministic, network-wide liveness failure invisible to either side's property tests.

## What changed

- **`roast_attempt_shuffle_seed(key_group, session_id, message_digest_hex)`** implements the normative RFC-21 Annex A derivation (see #4030). The key-group handle — this engine's hex-encoded serialized group verifying key — feeds the hash as an opaque UTF-8 string, exactly matching keep-core's `attempt.DeriveAttemptSeed` + `foldAttemptSeed` composition, including the strict 32-byte digest requirement.
- **`validate_attempt_context` now takes the session's key group** (threaded from `dkg.key_group` at StartSignRound and the session's `DkgResult` at FinalizeSignRound) and composes the shuffle source with the **0-based** RFC-21 attempt number. The FFI wire encoding stays 1-based (`attempt_number >= 1` still enforced; `wire = AttemptNumber + 1`); the engine subtracts one before composition, per the annex.
- **`testdata/coordinator_seed_vectors.json`** — byte-identical copy of the canonical file generated from the Go implementation. `coordinator_seed_derivation_matches_cross_language_vectors` pins, for all ten vectors: the folded seed (including negative values, so an unsigned port cannot pass), the selected coordinator (including the n=100 production-shape set), the 0-/1-based wire mapping, and end-to-end strict-mode `validate_attempt_context` acceptance of a context built from the wire encoding. Either language drifting now fails its own unit suite.
- **`docs/roast-coordinator-seed-derivation.md`** mirrors the normative annex for signer-side readers, with the regen/copy procedure.
- The coordinator-mismatch test derives the provably-wrong coordinator instead of hardcoding member 1 (which, under the new seed, happened to become the correct selection — exactly the class of silent assumption these vectors exist to catch).

## Notes

- Mixed-version note: engines on the old derivation reject contexts produced under the new one (and vice versa) — strict-mode attempt contexts are not yet produced by the Go layer in any deployment, so this is pre-wiring cleanup with no live-fleet impact.
- The attempt-context vector suite (`roast-attempt-context-v1.json`) is unaffected: it pins fingerprint/attempt-id domains with the coordinator as an *input*.
- Port back to the tBTC monorepo signer alongside the next extraction sync.

## Tests

Full suite: 245 passed, 0 failed; clippy and rustfmt clean. New conformance test exercises all ten cross-language vectors.

- `internal/agent/turn_progression.go`: Strip image data from messages after model response to avoid token waste on subsequent turns

- `internal/provider/token_estimator.go`: Account for image tokens in `countMessage` using OpenAI vision token formula

author: andtii
body:
Closes #77. Decision and design discussed on the issue; this is about layering and extensibility, not bundle size.

**What's layered now:**
- **`show` is opt-in** (content, not platform identity): `app.directive('show', show)` per app — works on the client and during SSR — or `registerShowDirective()` globally for bare-`render()` apps. The tuple form `use:show={[show, value]}` needs no registration. Breaking; pre-v0.6.x window, no shims.
- **Model handling is UNCHANGED for apps** — it's platform identity, exactly the way `@sigx/lynx` registers its own processor via the same `setPlatformModelProcessor` hook (which is unchanged: it's an external API). The "add more" seam is the new `registerModelProcessor(fn)`: extension processors run before the platform processor, first returning `true` wins, identity-idempotent — packs can add intrinsic-element model behaviors (custom elements, widget libraries) without replacing the platform's.
- **`show` owns its server rendering**: `getSSRProps` moved into the directive definition (the hook is now part of `DirectiveDefinition` in runtime-core proper — directives are isomorphic). server-renderer's lazy patching (`builtin-ssr-directives.ts`) and its type-augmentation shim are deleted; `DirectiveDefinitionExtensions` remains as a seam.
- **Packaging — platform side effects are now bundler-proof**: the DOM model processor ships as its own dist entry (`@sigx/runtime-dom/platform`) named precisely in `sideEffects`; `sigx` is `sideEffects: false` and its entries import the platform subpath explicitly. Previously the registrations survived only by entry-statement retention (and pinning the whole entry to "fix" that costs ~7 KB by dragging every export into every bundle). Now unused `Portal`/`useHead`/`show` tree-shake out of app bundles while the platform side effects survive any bundler.

**Verification:**
- 1518/1518 tests (4 new registry tests: extension-before-platform ordering, first-true-wins, fall-through, idempotency); typecheck/lint clean; size budgets green.
- `verify:pack` now asserts BOTH directions on a real Vite production build from packed tarballs: dev/devtools strings absent AND the model processor present (the scratch app gained a model-bound input) — locking the side-effect chain.
- Hello-world prod bundle: `Portal`/`useHead`/`show` gone, model processor retained through both the direct and the sigx re-export chains; 31.8 KB min (vs 38.7 KB with the naive sideEffects pinning).
- Examples need no changes (model is automatic; none use `use:show`).

author: tbraun96
body:
Closes the KV-block use-after-evict behind the #110 "batch=4 brick" (RC3 from the mixed-batch swarm). Independent of PR #157 (RC1/RC2 mixed-batch scratch race); both are needed to lift the recipe's `max_batch_size: 2` cap.

## Root cause
The mid-prefill SSM-snapshot checkpoint (`save_checkpoint.rs`) inserted radix tree nodes with `matched_tokens=end_token` ⇒ `is_seq_owned=false` ⇒ node `ref_count=1` ⇒ **immediately evictable while the sequence is still mid-prefill** and its delta-uploaded device block-table still points at those physical blocks. Under block pressure (concurrency≥4 + deep multi-chunk prefills) the next chunk's `ensure_blocks → evict` force-zeroes and reallocates a live block → use-after-evict.

## Fix
Drop the tree-node `insert` entirely. The SSM snapshot is found via the independent `SsmSnapshotIndex` (`insert_intermediate_snapshot`, kept) — keyed by `hash_token_prefix`, gated by `token_count ≤ matched_tokens`, reads no tree nodes. The matched path a future warm hit needs is supplied by `cache_sequence`'s full-range leaf insert after the sequence finishes. **Zero refcount-accounting change → no leak**: the seq's blocks stay pinned by their alloc ref in `seq.block_table` and become radix-visible only at `cache_sequence`, when the seq is no longer in-flight.

## Why NOT the swarm's original FIX-2
The swarm proposed `return_evicted_block → dec_ref`. That would **leak** here: this codebase is not balanced-refcounted — `release()` only decrements the radix *node* ref_count, never `kv_cache.block_ref_counts`, which is freed solely by eviction's force-zero. `dec_ref` semantics would strand blocks at count 1 forever. The swarm read the tree pre-#156; this PR is re-grounded on the current tree.

## Scope
Sub-bugs (c) `partial_suffix` and (d) `cache_sequence` over-inc verified **not** real on the current tree (force-zero collapses transient over-counts; partial blocks are freed only with their parent node). Left as a separate refactor-toward-balanced-refcounting, not bundled.

## Verification
- Compiles clean (image `2af98e1a`).
- Regression unit test (`radix_tree/tests/snapshot.rs`): intermediate snapshot registered with no tree insert is still found after the finish-leaf insert supplies the path.
- `debug_assert` tripwire in `apply_evicted_blocks`: any force-evicted block must have kv `ref_count ≤ 1` (catches re-introduction of an evictable live block).
- System gate (running): concurrency-4 + deep multi-chunk prefills under forced block pressure, asserting no CUDA-700 + no decode corruption; no-regression warm-hit check (Marconi intermediate hit still fires).

@aceangel3k KV-cache lifecycle change — worth a look at the snapshot-index decoupling argument (does any non-snapshot consumer rely on the dropped checkpoint tree nodes?).

## What

Adds 14 tests over `10-protocol/did-etzhayyim/src/cid.ts` — the CIDv1 assembler/parser layer that sits directly above the multibase/multihash/cbor codecs (covered in #1674). `genesis.test.ts` only smoke-touched `createCidV1`/`cidv1ToString`; this pins the rest.

`cid.ts` builds `varint(version) || varint(codec) || multihash` and parses it back. The parsers (`cidv1FromString`/`cidv1FromBytes`) and the multi-byte codec varint path had no direct coverage, and there was no known-answer anchor — so a regression in version/codec framing or multihash slicing would pass silently. author: aaronwald
body:
## Problem

The `ssmd connector subscribed to zero markets` CRITICAL alert fires for `kalshi-crypto`. The 15-minute crypto connector sits at **0 markets subscribed for ~45 min/hour**, dropping all 15M ticker/trade capture for windows opening at :15/:30/:45.

### Root cause

Kalshi transitions a market `initialized`→`active` (open for trading) **time-based on `open_time`, with NO `market_lifecycle_v2` event.** The `activated` event only fires when a *paused* (deactivated) market is re-enabled — never for ordinary window-open. Confirmed against [Kalshi docs](https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/market_lifecycle) (*"There is no `activated` WebSocket event for this transition"*) and our own `market_lifecycle_events`, where the sequence for a 15M market is:

```
created → metadata_updated → determined → settled   (no 'activated')
```

The cache only promoted markets to `active` on the `activated` event (`lifecycle.rs` `discovery_target_status`), which never arrives for 15M. So only the **hourly** `ssmd-secmaster-crypto` REST sync activated the currently-open window; the connector (which subscribes on `status='active'` via CDC) had nothing to subscribe to for the other three 15-min windows each hour.

(`metadata_updated` lands at window-open for 15M only because Kalshi sets the final strike then — undocumented and fragile, so it is **not** used as the activation trigger.)

## Fix

New `reconcile` module (`MarketActivator`) runs a **10s periodic sweep** that replicates Kalshi's time-based transition:

```sql
UPDATE markets SET status='active', updated_at=NOW()
 WHERE status='initialized' AND open_time IS NOT NULL
   AND open_time <= NOW() AND NOW() < close_time
```

CDC captures the UPDATE → connector subscribes via its existing path. Keeps `markets.status` correct for **all** consumers (monitor UI, cache warmer), not just the connector.

- **Promote-only & idempotent** — once `active`, a row no longer matches `status='initialized'`; no repeated CDC churn. Terminal lifecycle events (`determined`/`settled`) still drive the connector to unsubscribe at close.
- **Scope is safe** — every `markets` row is Kalshi and `initialized` is Kalshi-only, so no feed filter is needed. `NOW() < close_time` excludes already-closed windows; NULL `open_time`/`close_time` are excluded (fail-safe).
- **Fail-loud** — DB error crashes the process (no limping; K8s restarts).
- pg pool `max_size` 4→5 for the new consumer; interval uses `MissedTickBehavior::Skip`.
- `lifecycle.rs`: comment-only clarification that `activated` = paused-market re-enable, not window-open.

## Tests

12 unit tests in `reconcile.rs`: `window_is_open` boundary cases (inclusive open / exclusive close, missing bounds, zero-length, inverted, i64 extremes) + SQL scope/mutation guards (must only promote `initialized` in an open window; must never demote or delete). Full crate suite: **26 passed**. `cargo clippy` clean on changed code.

## Test plan

- [ ] Deploy cache, watch `kalshi-crypto` `markets_subscribed` stay > 0 across the :15/:30/:45 rollovers (not just the :00 hourly sync)
- [ ] Confirm `Activated open-window markets (initialized->active)` log lines at each window open
- [ ] Confirm the zero-markets alert clears and stays clear for a full hour
- [ ] Verify monitor UI shows open 15M windows as `active` (not `initialized`)

## Follow-ups (filed, not blocking)

- DB-backed integration test via testcontainers (insert initialized+open / initialized+future / active+open, assert exactly 1 promoted)
- Consolidate `derive_event_ticker` (lifecycle.rs) vs `extract_event_ticker` (warmer.rs) — pre-existing divergence on 4-segment tickers

author: bambamboole
body:
## Summary

When dumping a missing dotted translation key, the dumper now prefers an **already-existing** nested file that matches a prefix of the key, instead of always writing to a flat top-level file.

Example: with `lang/en/entities/salesOrder.php` present, dumping `entities.salesOrder.status` writes `status` into that file rather than creating `lang/en/entities.php`.

Rules:
- **Never creates new nested files/directories** — a key only lands in a nested file if that file already exists.
- Falls back to the existing behavior (flat top-level file named after the first segment) when no matching nested file exists.
- Prefers the **deepest** existing nested file when several prefixes match.

This pairs with `bambamboole/laravel-i18next`, which reads nested translation files namespaced by their path (`entities.salesOrder.*`); now keys saved via its store route round-trip back into the right nested file.

## Tests

- New `tests/Feature/NestedFileDumpTest.php` covers: writing into an existing nested file (and *not* creating a flat one), the flat-file fallback, and preferring the deepest existing nested file.
- Existing unit/feature coverage updated for the new file-resolution path.

Full suite (18 tests) + PHPStan + Pint green locally.

author: samuelv8
body:
## Summary

Adding a context to a workspace's `kubernetes.allowed_contexts` is currently rejected if the workspace has any active clusters or managed jobs, forcing a full teardown first. In `sky/workspaces/core.py`, `_validate_workspace_config_changes` only special-cases `private`/`allowed_users`; every other change falls into the `else` branch and calls `check_no_active_resources_for_workspaces(...)`.

A pure addition strands nothing: every existing context stays in the list, so running clusters/jobs keep resolving to a still-allowed context. This is the exact primitive a multi-cluster rollout needs — grow the allowed contexts incrementally without disrupting active workloads.

- Add `additive_allowed_contexts` to `WorkspaceConfigComparison`, computed in `_compare_workspace_configs`.
- `_validate_workspace_config_changes` now skips the teardown guard for additive-only context changes while still running the user-access validation body.
- Covers both `update_workspace` and `update_config`, since both share `_validate_workspace_config_changes`.

### Semantics

- Additive (allowed without teardown): `list -> list` where old is a subset of new, and `list -> 'all'` (broadening). Same-set reorders are also additive since no context is dropped.
- Not additive (teardown still required): `'all' -> list`, absent/`None` on either side, removals, or any change to other kubernetes fields (`namespace`, `context_configs`, etc.) or any other cloud.

## Test plan

- `pytest tests/unit_tests/test_sky/workspaces/test_workspace_management.py` (32 passed).
- New unit tests cover:
  - The additive truth table on `_compare_workspace_configs` (append, removal, reorder, `list -> 'all'`, `'all' -> list`, absent on either side).
  - Additive contexts combined with a sibling kubernetes field or a non-k8s field -> not additive.
  - `_validate_workspace_config_changes`: additive change skips `check_no_active_resources_for_workspaces`; non-additive change still calls it.
  - Combined added-user + additive-context (no teardown, no user check); combined added-user + non-additive-context (teardown guard enforced).
- Manual verification: with a cluster running on `ctx-a` in a workspace configured `allowed_contexts: [ctx-a]`, updating to `[ctx-a, ctx-b]` now succeeds; changing to `[ctx-b]` (removal) is still rejected until resources are torn down.

author: majilaii
body:
## The bug
"Posting a review" returned a generic non-2xx on every attempt. Root cause: `fn_create_entry_with_tables` RETURNS TABLE makes `entry_id` a PL/pgSQL variable, and the `ON CONFLICT (entry_id, …)` targets in its two fan-out inserts are ambiguous against it → SQLSTATE 42702 at runtime. PL/pgSQL parses lazily: the bug shipped in the May migrations but slept because the deployed entry function (April-vintage) used the old direct-insert path — the 2026-06-10 drift sweep deployed current main, whose create path calls the RPC with `p_participant_ids=[author]` on every entry. First execution → total breakage of the core write verb.

## The fix
`#variable_conflict use_column` pragma (migration `20260611000200`, body otherwise byte-identical to `20260509000110`) — wire shape preserved. Plus: entry's catch-all now serializes the real error message/code instead of `"[object Object]"`, which is what made this undiagnosable from the client.

## Verification (live prod, scratch account, fully cleaned up after)
- Raw RPC with participants: 42702 before → row after
- Edge path, ghost-restaurant shape: 500 → **200**
- Edge path, persisted restaurant_id + photos + sub-ratings: **200**

author: rsasaki0109
body:
## Summary

S11 of the MADOCA-PPP parity series — closes the bias signal-identity hypothesis with executable evidence, and ships the explicit-identity machinery as a default-OFF preview.

### Hypothesis closed

Suspicion from #139's audit: native collapses Galileo/QZSS bias signal ids to band level, so a C1C observation might receive an L1X bias (different tracking mode) than the bridge applies. Traced per observation code against MADOCALIB `mcssr_sel_biascode` (bridge trace level 4):

| Obs | Bridge id/value | Native id/value | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| E C1C/L1C | C1X +0.92 m | band id 2 (L1X) +0.92 m | identical |
| E C5Q/L5Q | C5X +1.62 m | band id 22 (L5X) +1.62 m | identical |
| J L1L | C1X +0.98 m | id-2 collision resolves to L1X +0.98 m | identical |
| J C2L | C2X −1.92 m | id 8 −1.92 m | identical |
| G C2W | C2W +0.16 m | would pick L2X +0.38 m | **0.000000 m** (C2W not the selected L2 obs) |

In this stream the per-band values never collide, so band collapsing is value-equivalent. Result: enabled run is **bit-identical** to default on MIZU (1.820470 / 1.195830 both).

### What ships

`GNSS_PPP_MADOCA_BIAS_IDENTITY=1` (default OFF): raw observation-code bias keys for GPS/Galileo/QZSS with an explicit `mcssrSelBiascode`-style lookup, and the selected RINEX observation type preserved through PPP combined observations. Correctness infrastructure for streams that do carry colliding per-tracking-mode bias values.

### Deferred lead (next slice)

The bridge trace revealed a real selection difference outside this surface: **QZSS secondary signal** — bridge pairs J L1 with **C5Q→C5X (L5)**, native selects **C2L→C2X (L2)**. Different iono-free pair → different geometry per QZSS row.

## Verification

- Full env matrix **bit-exact** vs pre-change reference; enabled run bit-identical to default
- `run_tests`: 318 passed / 43 skipped
- `tests/test_cli_tools.py -k qzss_l6 / madoca / clas`: pass

author: bromeon
body:
Follow-up to #1535.


### Consistent trait APIs: `WithUserRpcs` <-> `WithUserSignals`

Calling RPCs from outside a class now works through an inherent `Gd::rpcs()` method, mirroring how `Gd::signals()` already works. Inside a class you keep using `self.rpcs()`. The access shape is more consistent with the signals way, and the call itself is unchanged:

```rs
my_node.rpcs().say_hello_to("world").call();      // broadcast
my_node.rpcs().say_hello_to("world").call_id(1);  // to a specific peer
```


### Fixed: some RPCs were never registered

If a class declared `#[rpc]` methods but had no on-ready fields and didn't override `ready()`, its RPCs were silently never registered with Godot, and calling them failed at runtime with an error like "Unable to get the RPC configuration for the function ...". This was easy to hit with a class that only contains RPCs. Such classes now register correctly, so the calls work as expected -- no changes needed on your side.

author: fujacob
body:
## Summary Adds a new opt-in **"Add Space After Accepting"** toggle (Settings → General → Behavior). When on, accepting a suggestion that finishes a word also types a trailing space so the user can keep typing without reaching for the space bar. This was a requested feature; it's off by default so existing WYSIWYG accept behavior is unchanged unless opted into. The space is only appended when the accept **exhausts** the suggestion (the final chunk) — a mid-suggestion word accept is already followed by the next chunk's own leading space, so a space there would double up. Exhaustion is predicted the same way `commitAcceptedChunk` decides it (`session.advancing(by:).isExhausted`). The space is suppressed when the inserted text ends in punctuation (`done.`, `(yes)`, `really?!`), whitespace, or a space-less script (CJK/Thai never separate words with spaces), reusing the existing `isAcceptanceWordCharacter` / `beginsSpacelessScriptWord` primitives. Session accounting still advances by the unchanged `acceptedChunk`, and the session tears down on exhaustion, so the extra space never disturbs consumed-suffix reconciliation. ## Validation ``` xcodebuild -project Cotabby.xcodeproj -scheme Cotabby -destination 'platform=macOS' build -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData # ** BUILD SUCCEEDED ** xcodebuild ... test -only-testing:CotabbyTests/SuggestionSessionReconcilerTests CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO # ** TEST SUCCEEDED ** 93 tests, 0 failures (includes 6 new tests for the pure helper) xcodebuild ... test -only-testing:CotabbyTests/SettingsIndexTests -only-testing:CotabbyTests/SuggestionCoordinatorAcceptanceTests CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO # ** TEST SUCCEEDED ** swiftlint lint --quiet # on all changed files, exit 0 ``` Pure rule lives in `SuggestionSessionReconciler.insertionChunkAppendingTrailingSpace(_:)` (Support/), covered by new unit tests for word/digit/punctuation/whitespace/CJK/empty cases. The coordinator gates it via a small `insertionTextApplyingAutoSpace(...)` helper (kept separate so `acceptSuggestion` stays under the cyclomatic-complexity limit). ## Linked issues ## Risk / rollout notes - New persisted setting: UserDefaults key `cotabbyAddSpaceAfterAccept`, **defaults to false**, so no behavior change for existing installs until opted in. Threaded through the full settings stack (data → store load/write-back/save → model `@Published`/setter/snapshot/Combine publisher → snapshot struct → UI toggle → search index). - The new Combine upstream is paired with the existing trailing-punctuation toggle inside the timing tuple's last slot to stay under Combine's four-input `CombineLatest` cap. - No project.yml/pbxproj changes (new test code is auto-discovered by folder).

Greptile Summary

This PR adds an opt-in "Add Space After Accepting" toggle in Settings → General → Behavior. When enabled, accepting the final chunk of a suggestion appends a trailing space, letting users continue typing without pressing Space. The setting defaults to `false` so no behavior change occurs for existing installs. - The pure suppression rule lives in `SuggestionSessionReconciler.insertionChunkAppendingTrailingSpace`, which skips the space for text ending in punctuation, whitespace, or a spaceless-script (CJK/Thai) glyph; 6 new unit tests cover every branch. - Exhaustion is predicted with `session.advancing(by: acceptedChunk.count).isExhausted` before `commitAcceptedChunk`, matching the same logic, so a mid-suggestion accept (where the next chunk already carries a leading space) never receives a doubled space. Session accounting still advances by the unmodified `acceptedChunk`, keeping consumed-suffix reconciliation intact.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge — the feature is off by default, exhaustion prediction uses the same advancing logic as the actual commit, and suppression guards (punctuation, whitespace, CJK) are fully unit-tested. The acceptance coordinator carefully predicts exhaustion before inserting so the space is never appended to a mid-suggestion chunk, and session accounting still advances by the unmodified acceptedChunk, keeping consumed-suffix reconciliation intact. The new setting is opt-in with a false default, so existing installs see no change. The pure helper function is isolated in SuggestionSessionReconciler with comprehensive unit tests, and the Combine publisher nesting to stay within the four-input cap follows the established codebase pattern. No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

author: schubydoo
body:
## What

First slice of **CL-4** (Stage B interactive hosted sessions), split from the
monolithic CL-4 because the full slice (engine + endpoints + WS + UI) is too
large for one clean review. **This PR is the engine, as a pure library** —
mirroring how CL-1 (#224) shipped `claustrum_client` before anything wired it.
**CL-4b** will add the `/api/instances/{id}/message` endpoint, the
`/ws/hosted/{id}` WebSocket, `state.json` persistence, `SessionRunner` channel
dispatch, and the input/live-view UI.

The "hosted" channel runs a **headless `claude` stream-json agent on the
claustrum daemon's pipes** (not a remote-control bridge). Adding stream-json
output is exactly what turns the cloud door off, so the channel is local-only by
construction — proven in the CL-3 probes (`scratch/hosted-protocol-empirical.md`).

## Changes

- **`config.py`** — `SessionChannel = Literal["remote-control", "hosted"]`, an
  axis orthogonal to `ResumeMode` (which stays remote-control-only, so the pty/
  standard branches are untouched).
- **`models.py`** — additive, nullable hosted fields on `RemoteControlInstance`
  (`channel`, `claustrum_process_id`, `agent_pid`, `agent_proc_start`,
  `claude_session_uuid`, `daemon_last_seq`, `hosted_log_path`). All defaulted →
  existing `state.json` rows load unchanged (additive-only schema).
- **`hosted.py`** (new) —
  - `build_hosted_argv` — the observed claude-ssh minimal-mimic flag set
    (`--output-format/--input-format stream-json --permission-prompt-tool stdio
    --include-partial-messages --replay-user-messages`); **no `--remote-control`**.
  - `HostedSession` — drives one process over `ClaustrumClient` and routes its
    stdout NDJSON:
    - **control plane:** MCP `initialize`/`mcp_message` auto-acked with an empty
      success so a session never wedges; **every other** `control_request` —
      notably tool-permission `can_use_tool` — is **parked, never auto-answered**
      (fail-closed). CL-5 builds approve/deny on `pending_requests`.
    - **data frames:** every string leaf redacted via `sanitize_line`
      (defense-in-depth — a session/env id or secret anywhere in tool output or
      assistant text is masked before it reaches a browser), appended to a
      bounded ring (monotonic `event_seq`, honest `gap` markers), and fanned out
      to subscribers; the init frame yields `claude_session_uuid`.
  - `send_message` (minimal stream-json user frame), `stop` (SIGINT → grace →
    SIGKILL), `subscribe(after_seq)` ring replay for browser reconnects.

## Tests

21 new cases driven against the in-process `fake_claustrum` daemon: spawn
contract, redaction + uuid capture, MCP-ack vs permission parking, send/exit/
stop (incl. SIGKILL escalation), ring replay, slow-subscriber overflow.

- `uv run pytest -n0` → **866 passed, 97.19%** (gate 96%); `hosted.py` 96%.
- `uv run ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean; `uv run pyright src/clauster` clean.
- The two `# pragma: no cover` lines are daemon-loss-mid-operation paths that
  need a live daemon to force — exercised by CL-4b integration.

## Not in scope (CL-4b+)
Endpoints, WebSocket, UI, `state.json` wiring, runner dispatch (CL-4b);
permission approve/deny semantics + UI (CL-5); `--resume` respawn (CL-7).

body:
## Summary

Adds a user-selectable **Liquid Glass** theme alongside the classic matrix terminal UI, switchable live from a one-line APPEARANCE row in the app info sheet (tap `bitchat/`). Selection persists via `@AppStorage`.

| | matrix | liquid glass |
|---|---|---|
| Fonts | monospace (unchanged) | system |
| Colors | green-on-black (unchanged) | system labels, blue accent, peer colors kept |
| Chrome | opaque bars + dividers (unchanged) | floating `.glassEffect()` panels over a gradient backdrop |
| Layout | classic stacked (unchanged) | message list scrolls *under* the floating chrome (safe-area insets) |

### Architecture (commit 1)

- `Theme.swift`: `AppTheme` enum + `ThemePalette` semantic tokens (`background`, `primary`, `secondary`, `accent`, `locationAccent`, `accentBlue`, `alertRed`, `divider`), environment key, and a `@ThemedPalette` property wrapper
- Removed `backgroundColor`/`textColor`/`secondaryTextColor` prop-drilling through the header → composer → sheets hierarchy; views resolve the palette from the environment
- Matrix output is pixel-identical by construction

### Liquid Glass (commit 2)

- Real `.glassEffect()` on iOS 26 / macOS 26, gated by `#if compiler(>=6.2)` + `#available`, with an `.ultraThinMaterial` + hairline-stroke fallback — builds on older toolchains and renders frosted panels on pre-26 OSes
- Gradient root backdrop (glass needs texture to refract; it collapses over flat black)
- Theme threaded through `ChatMessageFormatter`; the per-message format cache gains a `variant` key so themes never serve each other's cached AttributedStrings
- All sheets (location channels, people, private chat, fingerprint, verification, notes, app info) share the same backdrop and surface language via `themedSheetBackground()` / `themedSurface()`
- New appearance strings localized for all 29 catalog languages

### UX fixes that apply to both themes

- Header controls (notes, channel badge, people count) get full-bar-height tap targets; people count is now a real `Button` instead of a tap gesture on the cluster
- `CommandSuggestionsView` renders nothing when empty — previously a zero-height view collected VStack spacing and pushed the composer input ~6pt off-center

## Test plan

- `swift test --parallel`: 954 tests, 143 suites, green
- macOS app built and visually verified in both themes (dark + light), including live theme switching and the location channels sheet
- iOS verified on device (composer centering, glass chrome)
- "Reduce Transparency" falls back to opaque material automatically (system behavior)

## Summary

The complete Zeta mobile app (Expo SDK 56 / React Native) plus the backend pieces it needs, built plan-by-plan on one branch (single-PR strategy — merged once at the end).

### Foundation (Parts 1–8b)

**Part 1 — Mobile token auth (backend):** PKCE exchange + rotation, Bearer middleware tests, OpenAPI contract + lint wiring.
**Part 2 — Expo app skeleton:** SDK 56, expo-router, NativeWind + Zeta tokens, generated typed client, i18next, jest-expo + RNTL, Make/CI.
**Part 3 — Client auth:** SecureStore tokens, single-flight refresh middleware, Zustand auth store, PKCE login, auth gate, profile.
**Part 4 — Videos list + playback:** TanStack Query, Mux thumbnails + HLS via expo-video.
**Part 5 — Upload flow:** sequential direct-to-Mux uploads, persisted retryable queue, upload screen + FAB + progress cards.
**Part 6 — Reviews:** threaded timestamped comments, seek-on-tap, gated composer.
**Part 7 — Groups + invites:** permission-gated member lists, leave flow, QR-scan/manual invite joining.
**Part 8a — Coaching booking:** bookings tab (upcoming/past, cancel, recording links), guided booking flow with distinct 400/409 errors.
**Part 8b — Live calls (Agora) + dev client:** platform-split call engine (react-native-agora v4 native, stub for web/jest), call store with generation guard + single teardown, full-screen call UI with permission gates; EAS project + local WSL dev-build path. Expo Go stays sufficient for everything except live calls.
**Backend security fix:** `POST /assets/{id}/complete` enforces visibility (404) + ownership (403).

### Expert parity (WP1–WP8)

Availability editor (weekly rules, session types, block times), group administration (preferences, member removal), reports, notification center + push preferences, personal-data editing. Verified on-device with the granted WorkOS permissions (`groups:preferences:edit`, `groups:user-list:delete`). Deferred by decision: push registration part B, account deletion + Sign in with Apple.

### Native-adaptive redesign + UI-kit handoff

- Platform-adaptive `z-*` primitive library (bare/`.ios`/`.android` tiers); @expo/ui Compose where it helps, RN fallbacks where Compose breaks flex layout or first paint (documented in `.agents/reports/`).
- Full visual redesign from the UI-kit handoff (`mobile/handoffs/handoff_ui_kit/`): role-token theme (light **and dark**), Nunito font pipeline with native fallback guard, stepped booking flow with persistent `ZBookingBar`, aligned type scale.
- Handoff bundle replaced with the self-contained version (local fonts, `_ds_bundle.js`), verified by pixel-sampling against the app.

### Full app review + fix run (2026-07-02)

Review report: `.agents/reports/20260702102000_mobile_full_review_handoff_structure_ux.md`. All findings fixed, notably:

- **Auth UX:** logout now returns to the app (`MOBILE_LOGOUT_RETURN_TO` env, documented in `.env.example`); failed code exchange surfaces an error on the login screen instead of failing silently; profile language applies on login.
- **Android:** in-content headers for formSheets (react-native-screens ignores `headerShown`), hero CTA fill (NativeWind function-style props are dropped on device), scheme-aware status bar/tab chrome, toast offset above the tab bar, 2dp focus borders on inputs.
- **Data freshness:** `focusManager` wired to AppState, pull-to-refresh on home, error slots for background queries.
- **Locale correctness:** date formatting honors the app language, local-date keys fix a UTC off-by-one, DE formats verified on device.
- **A11y:** screen-reader users get an explicit cancel button where the swipe action is invisible to TalkBack.
- **Copy:** EN sentence-case pass across mobile + web JSONs (kept in sync by hand — `sync:i18n` is destructive).
- Plus structural cleanups (shared tab-chrome hook, dead plumbing removed) and the add-to-calendar, danger-outline button, and avatar/input geometry batch.

### Merge with main (`f2b4aa0`)

`origin/main` merged into the branch (audit trail, invite-code soft launch, feedback inbox, contact/inbound-email → Discord, landing v2, Strido web rename). 12 conflicted files resolved; key decisions:

- Web i18n JSONs merged key-level three-way (main's Strido branding wins, branch's booking copy stays; +103 main-only keys preserved).

author: rs545837
body:
Closes GIT-24.

**Problem.** When logged in, the first cloud-routed command (`impact`/`context`/`entities`/`log`) calls `ensure_repo`, which auto-registers an unknown repo by POSTing its clone URL to sem-cloud to index. This synced **private** repos with no explicit consent.

**Fix.** Registration of a not-yet-known repo now proceeds only when the unauthenticated GitHub API confirms the repo is public (`private: false`). Private, missing, non-GitHub, or unreachable repos fall back to local execution unless the user opts in with `SEM_SYNC_PRIVATE=1`. Already-registered repos resolve from cache and skip the check, so there is no added latency or behavior change for them.

**Design note (open to feedback):** the opt-in is an env var (`SEM_SYNC_PRIVATE=1`) to avoid new persistent state. Could instead be a config flag or a prompt during `sem login` if you prefer.

**Out of scope:** repos already registered as private are not retroactively unsynced; that needs a server-side change.

Tested: `github_owner_repo` parsing (https/ssh/.git/non-GitHub) via a unit test; GitHub API behavior confirmed (public 200 `private:false`, missing/private 404).

author: gerchowl
body:
## #69: reconnect after handoff — idle hang behind frozen frame + unusable shell

After a live-handoff reattach, a client that inherited a **held** host terminal (alt-screen + raw mode, a frozen frame from the previous leg's seamless switch) could:
1. sit in the #52 retry window with **no visible progress** behind the frozen frame (perceived hang), and
2. be left **unusable** if the user ctrl-c'd the "hung" client — the held-terminal exit path missed restore.

### Fix
- **Unconditional restore (outcome 2).** A `HeldRestoreGuard` covers the held-terminal window of a leg, armed when the leg holds the terminal itself (`SWITCH_HANDOFF_PENDING`) or inherited a hold from a previous leg (new `HERDR_TERMINAL_HELD` env, set by the launcher in `run_attach_legs`). Any abnormal exit — error return, ctrl-c/SIGTERM/SIGHUP, panic, or the `std::process::exit` paths that skip `Drop` — reclaims the host terminal (leave alt-screen, raw off, pop kitty flags, reset modifyOtherKeys). A clean handoff into the next leg disarms it so the no-blip switch (#63/#67) is preserved.
- **Visible progress (outcome 1).** The live-handoff retry status is painted as a cursor-parked bottom-row overlay **on the held screen** (`\x1b7\x1b[9999;1H…\x1b8`) with a live elapsed-seconds counter, so the wait reads as progress, not frozen silence. Plain in-leg reconnects keep the in-place stderr line.
- **Refusal not masked by a dying server.** `set_read_timeout(None)` after a Welcome is in hand can EINVAL when a mid-handoff server half-closes the socket right after the refusal; that failure used to surface as a bare `ConnectionFailed`, defeating the retry classification. It is now ignored so the refusal drives the retry.

### Tests
- New unit tests: hold-flag tracking, `HeldRestoreGuard` drop reclaims an inherited hold, a disarmed guard keeps the hold for the next leg, and the elapsed-seconds status counter.
- New e2e `killing_a_client_mid_held_handoff_restores_the_terminal`: a refusing stand-in server drives a real `herdr client` (with an inherited hold) into the retry window; asserts (a) visible held-screen progress overlay with the elapsed counter, (b) full terminal restore sequence on SIGINT. The stand-in holds refused connections open to mirror a real mid-handoff server.
- Green: `client_mode` (17), `live_handoff` (16), `peer_federation` (7), and the full `--bin herdr` unit suite (2075). #67 no-blip and #52 retry semantics preserved.

Built/tested entirely in the devShell (sccache); commit passed guardrails gates.

body:
Two commits, one theme: every tripbot instance gets its own per-name host and a matching \`EXTERNAL_URL\`.

**Commit 1 (the bug, caught walking the stage consent flow):** \`tripbot-youtube\` serves on \`tripbot-youtube.stage.whereisdana.today\` but its \`EXTERNAL_URL\` said \`tripbot.stage.whereisdana.today\`. Both OAuth flows build their redirect as \`EXTERNAL_URL + /auth/callback\`, so Google would bounce the consent callback to the **twitch** instance — which deliberately has no youtube creds (#701).

**Commit 2 (consistency, Dana's call):** drop the primary-platform special case entirely — \`tripbot-twitch\` moves to \`tripbot-twitch.<dns_base>\` in every env, symmetric with vlc/onscreens/obs and with EXTERNAL_URL. The \`primary\` concept disappears from the ingress path.

dist diff: the four \`*-tripbot-twitch\` units (host, external-dns hostname, TLS secret name, \`EXTERNAL_URL\`, config-hash) + \`stage-1-tripbot-youtube\` (EXTERNAL_URL). Argo rolls the tripbot pods once; external-dns republishes the records; cert-manager issues certs for the new hosts. Twitch tokens are unaffected (refresh doesn't touch the redirect URI) — only *future consent flows* need the new URLs registered.

## Console steps (before relying on any re-auth flow)

- **Twitch dev console** — the app(s) carrying tripbot callbacks: add
  \`https://tripbot-twitch.stage.whereisdana.today/auth/callback\` (dev app, replacing the old stage entry eventually) and the prod equivalent on prod's app.
- **GCP console** (tripbot-stage → Web OAuth client): add
  \`https://tripbot-youtube.stage.whereisdana.today/auth/callback\`.

Old URIs can stay registered during the transition; prune once the new hosts are confirmed working.

77/77 cdk8s tests pass.

author: httpassoca
body:
## What

Migrates the site's hand-rolled UI primitives to the [dssoca](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dssoca) design system (v0.8.2):

| Before (local) | After (dssoca) | Where |
|---|---|---|
| AppButton | `Button` (primary) | contact form |
| AppInput | `Input` | contact form |
| AppLink | `Link` | home, career, all 10 blog posts (`to=` → `href=`) |
| AppExtension | `Accordion` | notes page (lazy-load preserved via `onChange`, `multiple` open) |
| ThemeMenu + LanguageMenu | `Menu` ×2 | header (radio mode, self-dismissing) |
| MobileBottomNav | `BottomNav` | layout (3 runtime-registered glyphs + built-in `note`) |

Kept custom (no dssoca equivalent): AppTextarea, AppTitle, AppContent, AppLoader, AppError, AppImage, HeroIcon, AppSVG.

## How theming is preserved

`dssoca/theme.css` is **not** imported — it restyles global elements (`a`, headings, `code`, scrollbars) and only knows dark/light. Instead, `src/sass/dssoca.sass` bridges the site's `--app-color-*` variables to the `--ss-*` tokens dssoca components consume, so **all 5 themes (dark/light/coffee/dracula/tokyo-night) keep working**. Size/motion tokens use dssoca's `md` defaults; neutrals (`--ss-line`, `--ss-hover`) are derived from the theme text color via `color-mix()`; coffee gets an opaque `--ss-bg-elev` override for the menu panel.

## Intentional visual deltas (dssoca metrics adopted)

- Zero border-radius and dssoca padding/hover on swapped components (DS house style)
- Links render in the primary color with hover-revealed underline + external-link icon
- Menu triggers/panels and bottom nav adopt the dssoca square style; theme swatch dots and flag icons folded into labels
- Notes accordion loses per-note DOM `id` anchors

## Notes

- `yarn.lock` and `package-lock.json` coexist; only `package-lock.json` was updated. Local pnpm artifacts (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) were not committed.
- `color-mix()` requires 2023+ browsers.

## Verification

- `svelte-check`: 0 errors (clean baseline before and after)
- `vitest`: 15/15 passing
- `vite build`: ✓ (also exercises dssoca's TS dist components through svelte-preprocess)
- SSR smoke test on the production build: `ss-link`/`ss-btn`/`ss-input`/`ss-menu` render on `/`, `/career`, `/contact`; token bridge present in the emitted CSS

## Summary

Adds the mypy runner using the same reveal_type-injection harness as ty + pyright + pyrefly.

## Architectural note

mypy is annotation-driven by design — unhinted function returns surface as Any rather than being inferred from the body (\`--check-untyped-defs\` walks the body, but the inferred return type still flows out as Any). The score on TypeEvalPy (deliberately unhinted corpus) reflects that design choice; it'd score very differently on annotated code.

Expected scoring cluster: ~ty level (annotation-driven). Distinct from pyright/pyrefly (aggressive inference).

## What's in here

- \`Dockerfile\` — python:3.11-slim with mypy 1.13.0 pinned
- \`src/runner.py\` — reveal_type injection harness, mypy text output parsing, type flattener handling \`Literal[X]\`, trailing \`?\` (tentative), \`def () -> R\` -> callable
- \`runner_class.py\` — adds \`MypyRunner\` to the registry

## Smoke test

\`assignments/chained\` — 6/8 EXACT (same as ty). Function returns inferred via reveal_type in body; \`c = b()\` returns Any.

author: aquigorka
body:
Remediates the preemptive internal audit (`pm-theahaco/audits/preempt-soroban-2026-06-11/AUDIT-REPORT.md`) ahead of the RV engagement. One commit per finding for traceability.

## Findings → commits

| Audit ID | Severity | Commit | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| MOON-01 | Critical | `53bc4ee` + `8ad0f37` | Bind owner-signed `Create`/`ExtWithdraw` conditions to executed effects (subset `authorized ⊆ executed`); balance check retained. `8ad0f37` relaxes the initial exact-match to subset so the provider fee is permitted (see below). |
| MOON-02 | Medium | `07a4790` | Manage storage TTL — bump persistent UTXO meta / drawer bitmap / state and the contract instance so live state can't archive. |
| MOON-03 | Low | `c3dd832` | `handle_utxo_auth` empty-args context now `continue`s instead of `return Ok(())` (no whole-check short-circuit). |
| MOON-04 | Low | `04d6b95` | Document + lock (regression tests) the verifier wrappers' dependence on host panic-on-failure. |
| MOON-05 | Low | `c7e0256` | Reject non-positive deposit/withdraw amounts in-contract (`InvalidExternalAmount`). |
| MOON-06 | Low | `9a4d172` | Reentrancy guard around `transact` (`ReentrantCall`). |
| MOON-09 | Info | `866f331` | Emit `Upgraded { wasm_hash }` on upgrade (governance trail). |
| MOON-10 | Info | `9ea90cf` | Make the utxo-core events feature compile (dedup imports + `&BytesN` fix). |
| — | — | `5f5ea6a` | Version bump `0.2.0 → 0.2.1` (auto-tag). |

**Deferred (flagged in the audit):** MOON-07 (64 KiB drawer bitmap vs entry-size — needs protocol-limit confirmation), MOON-08 (`ExtIntegration` removal/impl — roadmap; the MOON-01 binding already makes it inert), MOON-09 constructor-auth alignment (changes deploy behavior — separate PM call), MOON-11 (dep patch-bumps + `# Panics` docs — not touching the audited dep stack pre-RV).

## MOON-01 — the Critical, with adversarial pre/post proof

The balance check alone (`total_available_balance == expected_outgoing`) guarantees value conservation but not *where* value goes. A provider could keep `op.spend` byte-identical (the owner's P256 sig still verifies over the unchanged conditions) and substitute `op.create`/`op.withdraw` to redirect funds while staying balanced → theft. The fix requires every owner-signed `Create`/`ExtWithdraw` to be executed exactly (same utxo/addr + amount); extra executed creates/withdraws are allowed (the provider fee) and bounded by the balance check to the residual the signers leave.

Adversarial test (`contracts/privacy-channel/src/test/moon01.rs`): a victim signs a spend authorizing an internal change-create, the bundle keeps `op.spend` byte-identical but redirects the output to an attacker, perfectly balanced.

- **PRE-FIX** (binding disabled): `transact` **ACCEPTED** — victim UTXO spent, attacker token balance `+500`, channel supply drained to `0`.
- **POST-FIX** (subset binding): same bundle **REJECTED** with `UnauthorizedOperation` — victim UTXO still `500`, attacker `0`, supply `500`.

Also covered: redirect-to-attacker-create rejects; a within-residual provider fee is accepted (the real e2e shape); taking more than the residual or adding any extra create to a residual-0 transfer reverts via `UnbalancedBundle`.

## Why subset, not exact-match
The real fee model has the provider executor add an **unsigned** `Create(opexUtxo, fee)` to collect the residual the depositor over-funds / spender under-claims (`provider-platform/.../executor.service.ts:81`); the client deposits `amount + fee` but signs a condition only for `amount`. Exact-match rejected that legitimate fee create (caught by the e2e). Subset keeps signed outputs inviolable while permitting the fee.

## Validation
- `cargo test --workspace`: **61 passed / 0 failed**. `cargo clippy --all-targets`: clean. `stellar contract build`: both wasms.
- **local-dev e2e against the fixed WASM: PASS** — full payment flow (deposit 10 XLM → send 5 Alice→Bob → withdraw 4) completes with the real provider fee model, while the adversarial redirect stays rejected.

## ⚠ Downstream (separate PM ops — NOT in this PR)
- The fixed WASM must be **redeployed + re-initialized** on testnet (then mainnet / D8).
- **Before that redeploy:** confirm **browser-wallet** and **provider-platform** bundle assembly attaches exact-mirror conditions for every executed user create/withdraw — otherwise the tightened contract will reject their bundles. (The local-dev reference client + executor already conform, verified by the e2e; the other consumers must be checked.)

author: sahil170595
body:
## Motivation

Closes the benchmark request in #27406: a compact, reproducible way to measure
*where the latency tail breaks down* as concurrency rises, across the workload
shapes that stress different serving boundaries — long decode (memory
bandwidth), long prefill (KV allocation + chunked prefill), repeated prefix
(RadixAttention reuse), and multi-turn agentic sessions with tool-call gaps
(cache retention under interleaving).

It is a thin driver over `sglang.bench_serving`: each (workload, phase,
concurrency, rep) cell is one bench_serving invocation; the driver aggregates
per-cell results into a boundary table (p50/p95 wall, p50/p95 TTFT, p95
multiplier vs N=1, aggregate decode tok/s, failure counts).

## What's included

- `benchmark/serving_boundary/` — driver, README with reference numbers, run.sh
- `agentic_session` workload preset: interleaved multi-turn sessions with
  per-session prefixes, per-turn tool-output suffixes, and client-side
  tool-call pauses between turns (short/long bimodal). A session holds its
  concurrency slot while paused, like a live agent mid-tool-call.
- Core support for the preset (all default-off, zero behavior change unset):
  - `generated-shared-prefix`: `--gsp-turn-gap-short-s` / `--gsp-turn-gap-long-s`
    / `--gsp-turn-gap-long-prob`. Gaps sample from an isolated RNG stream
    `(seed, 1)`, so enabling them leaves group assignment and the prompt pool
    byte-identical for the same seed (unit-tested).
  - `DatasetRow` / `RequestFuncInput`: optional `turn_gaps_s` field.
  - multi-turn wrapper: sleeps `turn_gaps_s[i]` before sending round i.
- CPU unit tests (`test/registered/unit/bench/test_gsp_turn_gaps.py`, 9 tests):
  gap shape/values, seed determinism, prob extremes, prompt-pool isolation,
  single-turn no-op, `from_args` validation.

## Reference numbers

Complete 108-cell run on main: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 1x A100-SXM4-80GB, 3 reps,
radix on + off, zero failed requests. Highlights (full tables in the README):

- `long_prefill_8k`: p95 wall multiplier **17.4x** at N=32 (TTFT p95 7.4s) —
  the prefill tail cliff.
- `repeated_prefix` at N=32: radix on vs off = 1080 vs 648 tok/s (+67%),
  TTFT p95 384ms vs 1157ms (3x).
- `long_decode` / `long_prefill_8k`: radix on/off identical — a built-in
  zero-overhead check for the radix cache on non-reusable traffic.

## Relation to other work

The `agentic_session` preset is intended as an evaluation vehicle for the
agentic KV-cache discussions in #27574 / #24656 / #21846 (cache retention
under session interleaving and tool gaps). Engine behavior is untouched —
this PR is benchmark + dataset client only.

## How to run

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --port 30000
python3 benchmark/serving_boundary/bench_boundary.py --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --port 30000
```

---

*Disclosure: developed with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5). All benchmark
numbers are from real GPU runs; raw data available.*

author: simonrevill
body:
## What

Lands the keystone `add` command's first **side effect** (RFC 0005 §4.1 step 2):
`add button` now actually installs the headless package via the project's
package manager. A new `--dry-run` reports the plan and stops.

## Changes (one red→green cycle per commit)

1. **`PackageManager` detection** — a new enum detects pnpm/yarn/bun/npm from the
   project lockfile (fixed precedence; npm the default) and builds the install
   command (`add` vs npm's `install`).
2. **`ProcessRunner` port** — a trait with an `OsProcessRunner` adapter (spawns
   the manager, maps a non-zero exit to an error) and an invocation-recording
   `InMemoryProcessRunner` fake. The adapter is unit-tested with harmless real
   commands (`true` / `false` / a missing program), so it reaches 100% without a
   live install.
3. **Install in `add`** — after reporting the plan, `add` ensures the resolved
   components' packages with one detected-manager invocation in the working
   directory. `--dry-run` reports and stops; an empty package set is a no-op; a
   failed manager is a new `CliError::Install` (exit code **10**).
4. **Checklist** — records the install, the new port/detector, and what remains.

```
$ primitiv add button                # detects pnpm → runs `pnpm add @primitiv-ui/react`
$ primitiv add button --dry-run      # plans, installs nothing
```

## Testing strategy (the side-effect seam)

The install execution is proven at the **command layer** with the recording fake
(asserting `pnpm add @primitiv-ui/react` in the right cwd, dry-run skips, empty
skips, failure → `CliError::Install`, cwd-read failure → `CliError::Io`). The
**`OsProcessRunner` adapter** is unit-tested directly with harmless commands. The
**e2e** uses `--dry-run`, so the real binary never shells out to a live package
manager in CI. `main.rs` (now constructing `OsProcessRunner`) stays covered by
the existing non-add e2e.

> **Known v1 wart (noted in the checklist):** a non-dry-run `add --json` install
> interleaves the package manager's own stdout with the JSON. Agents wanting pure
> JSON use `--dry-run`; routing the manager's output to stderr is a follow-up.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace` — green.
- `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --exclude harmoni-core --exclude harmoni-wasm
  --fail-under-lines 100 --fail-under-regions 100 --fail-under-functions 100` —
  **100%** lines, regions, and functions (new `add.rs`, `package_manager.rs`,
  `process.rs`, `error.rs`, `cli.rs`, `run.rs`, `main.rs` all at 100%).

## Build-phase progress (~77%)

| # | Build-phase item | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rust CI + test harness | ✅ Done |
| 2 | Token emitter (CSS / SCSS / Tailwind) | ✅ Done |
| 3 | `primitiv theme` (brand → paired light+dark) | ✅ Done |
| 4 | Mode scoping (`data-theme` / `data-density`) | ✅ Done |
| 5 | Styling contract + `contract.json` | ⬜ Not started |
| 6 | Default theme authoring (workbench) | ⬜ Not started |
| 7 | The CLI | 🟡 In progress — `init`/`tokens`/`theme`/`list` + `add` resolution, install plan (`--json`), and now **package install (process port + `--dry-run`)** landed; remaining: `add` style-copy + `primitiv.lock` (blocked on items 5/6), wiring, the `--styles-only`/`--no-styles`/`--format`/`--path`/`--force` flags, HTTPS registry; init detection; `list` installed column; Tailwind `dark:` remap |
| 8 | Distribution (`optionalDependencies` matrix) | ⬜ Not started |

Overall ≈77% (items 1–4 done; item 7's `add` now performs its first real effect — package install).

## Next

The remaining `add` effect — copying component styles — is **blocked** on items
5/6 (the registry has no per-component style files to serve yet). So the natural
next unblocked steps are **init detection** (the lockfile PM detector this PR adds
is now reusable) or starting **item 5 (`contract.json`)**. Happy to pick, or tell
me which.

body:
## Summary

Adds Kafka as a second pub/sub backend, as a sibling sub-package to RabbitMQ (`warren/pubsub/kafka/`), with a backend selector wired through the runtime and `rmq`/`kafka`/`gcs` split into optional dependency extras.

> **Draft until** the genai-utils compose dress rehearsal (Kafka + RMQ regression) and the DSH e2e are green — evidence links will be added here before review/merge, per the implementation plan.

## Semantic mapping (RMQ → Kafka)

| RMQ behavior | Kafka implementation |
|---|---|
| Fanout exchange `jobs` | One topic; every consumer group sees every message |
| Queue per worker type `jobs.<worker_type>` | Consumer group per worker type, default group id `<topic>.<worker_type>`, overridable |
| Competing consumers in a worker type | Partitions within the group |
| `message.ack()` after success | Commit offset after processing (manual commit, at-least-once) |
| `nack(requeue=True)` | Don't commit + `seek()` back to the message offset → re-polled |
| `reject(requeue=False)` (hard failure / malformed JSON) | Commit anyway (drop is intentional and terminal) |
| `prefetch_count: 1` | Sequential per-consumer processing loop |
| Declare exchange/queue on setup | Verify topic exists (`PubSubSetupError`); optional create-if-missing for local |
| Mongo-based retry + retry-worker republish | Unchanged — broker-independent |
| Worker self-selection by `data_type` | Unchanged — application code |

Failure semantics (soft/hard-failure envelopes, retry math) are copied from the RMQ consumer manager and verified byte-for-byte identical by envelope-parity unit tests; extraction of the shared core is an explicitly deferred follow-up.

## Breaking changes (0.1.1 → 0.2.0)

1. `pip install warren` no longer pulls `aio-pika`/`google-cloud-storage` — use `warren[rmq]` (and `[gcs]` where the GCS resolver is used).
2. `RuntimeInfra.rmq_connection_manager` → `RuntimeInfra.pubsub_connection_manager`.
3. `RetryConfig` canonical import is `warren.pubsub.common` (old path re-exported, no action needed).
4. Custom runners constructing RMQ classes directly should move to the `warren.runtime.backends` factories.

## Evidence

- [x] Unit suite: 70 passed; ruff clean
- [x] Local broker smoke (apache/kafka:4.0.0): round-trip, soft-failure envelope, hard-failure drop, no redelivery loop
- [x] Local bare-process fake pipeline, both backends: 4 docs / 18 chunks / 18 embeddings, job completed
- [x] Compose dress rehearsal (Kafka variant) — `E2E RESULT: PASS` (4/18/18 + injected retry + no-reset rerun + at-least-once worker-kill redelivery)
- [x] Compose dress rehearsal (RMQ regression) — `E2E RESULT: PASS` (same image, BACKEND unset)
- [ ] DSH e2e on platform-managed Kafka — `E2E RESULT: PASS`

## Overview
Many of the HED experiments have an unusually high background. This results in artificially low value of the weighted R-p factor (`Rwp`) for whole pattern fits for these datasets. In addition to this changes, the computation for the chi^2 factor is greatly simplified. A bug was also discovered where the sqrt of the values that should have been reported was getting calculated.

the difference vector that was used for the minimization problem now conforms to the values used in GSAS. There was a sqrt operation that was extra in hexrd before this PR.

body:
Converts 19 Swift security query `.qlref` tests from `.expected`-file-based testing to inline expectation tests by adding `// $ Alert`, `// $ Source`, and `// $ Sink` comments directly in the Swift source files.

## What changed

- **19 `.qlref` files** updated to add `postprocess: utils/test/InlineExpectationsTestQuery.ql` (compact single-line form)
- **35 Swift source files** annotated with inline expectation comments derived from existing `.expected` files:
  - `@kind problem` queries: `// $ Alert` at each result's end-line
  - `@kind path-problem` queries: `// $ Alert` at alert location, `// $ Source` at source (when on different line), `// $ Sink` at sink (when on different line from alert)
- No `.expected` files were modified

**Before/after example (`CWE-760/ConstantSalt`):**
```swift
// Before
let myConstantSalt1 = Data("abcdef123456")  // no annotation
let _ = myEncryptor.key(..., salt: myConstantSalt1, ...) // BAD

// After
let myConstantSalt1 = Data("abcdef123456") // $ Source
let _ = myEncryptor.key(..., salt: myConstantSalt1, ...) // $ Alert
```

Lines with pre-existing `// BAD, descriptive text` comments were restructured to `// $ Alert // BAD, descriptive text` so the `$` appears first in the comment content (required by the inline expectation parser).

## Skipped tests (12)

| Test | Reason |
|---|---|
| 4× `PrintAst.qlref` | AST dump queries |
| `library-tests/ast/Errors.qlref` | No `@kind` metadata |
| `AlertSuppression.qlref` | `@kind alert-suppression` |
| `Diagnostics/ExtractedFiles.qlref` | `@kind diagnostic` |
| `Diagnostics/SuccessfullyExtractedLines.qlref` | `@kind metric` |
| `CWE-757/InsecureTLS.qlref` | `file://` synthetic alert locations in `#select` (9 rows) |
| `CWE-321/HardcodedEncryptionKey.qlref` | `file://` synthetic alert location |
| `CWE-078/CommandInjection.qlref` | `file://` synthetic alert locations |
| `CWE-135/StringLengthConflation.qlref` | `file://` synthetic source locations (13 rows) |

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Follow these instructions for Swift.
**qlref conversion instructions**

Here’s the repeatable recipe for converting a CodeQL language’s `.qlref` tests to inline expectation tests.

**Overall Workflow**

1. `cd` into the language folder.

2. Run `grep -rL "InlineExpectationsTestQuery" --include="*.qlref"`.

3. Ignore generated `.actual` files, `.testproj` copies, and other generated artifacts.

4. For each `.qlref`, resolve the referenced query and read its metadata.

5. Classify each test before editing:

  - `convert now` for standard `@kind problem` and `@kind path-problem`

  - `skip` for anything else, with a short concrete reason

6. Inspect the existing `.expected` file before converting:

  - If it is empty and the query is a standard `problem` or `path-problem` query, usually convert by adding the postprocessor only. No source comments are needed.

  - If it is non-empty, add inline expectation comments to the source files at the expected result locations, then add the postprocessor to the `.qlref`.

7. Keep the existing `.expected` file. Do not edit generated expected files by hand, even when converting.

8. Edit only source files and `.qlref` files.

9. Maintain a skip list for tests not converted, with exact paths and short reasons.

10. Do not make a PR.

**`.qlref` Formatting**

For a single postprocessor, use the compact form:

```yaml

query: path/to/Query.ql

postprocess: utils/test/InlineExpectationsTestQuery.ql

```

If the `.qlref` already has other postprocessors, use list form:

```yaml

query: path/to/Query.ql

postprocess:

  - utils/test/PrettyPrintModels.ql

  - utils/test/InlineExpectationsTestQuery.ql

```

If the original `.qlref` was a plain single-line query reference, convert it to `query:` form only when adding `postprocess:`.

Always preserve existing postprocessors.

**Expectation Comments**

Use the language’s supported inline comment syntax from its inline expectation implementation. Typical tags are:

```text

$ Alert

$ Source

$ Sink

```

For example, in Java or Kotlin:

```java

sink(userInput); // $ Alert

```

For `problem` queries, add `Alert` at each expected result location.

For `path-problem` queries, add:

- `Alert` at the alert location.

- `Source` at the source location, unless the source is on the same line as the alert.

- `Sink` at the sink location when it is a distinct relevant location.

Multi-line result locations should be annotated on the end line.

If more than one result is expected on the same line for the same query, just use a single tag in the comment, for example:

```java

foo(bar); // $ Alert

```

Only add comments to real source files that belong to the test. Do not annotate generated copies, shared vendored fixtures, or shared stubs unless that is clearly the right ownership boundary for the test.

**Empty `.expected` Files**

If a `problem` or `path-problem` test already has an empty `.expected` file, the default conversion is:

1. Leave `.expected` untouched.

2. Add `postprocess: utils/test/InlineExpectationsTestQuery.ql` to the `.qlref`.

3. Add no source comments unless the test actually has expected results that are currently represented elsewhere.

This is common in zero-result tests.

**Query Ids**

Do not add `[query-id]` by default.

Only qualify tags when needed, usually when more than one inline expectation test in the same effective test folder or database can see the same source comments. Then use the query’s metadata id:

```java

response.write(x); // $ Alert[java/xss]

```

Apply this to `Alert`, `Source`, and `Sink` only for the comments that need disambiguation.

If you add query ids in a shared folder, validate the owner queries for those comments as well, not just the query you were editing.

**Good Skip Reasons**

Skip, or revert to non-inline, when conversion would make the test misleading, brittle, or noisy. Common reasons:

- The query is not `@kind problem` or `@kind path-problem`.

- The query is a telemetry, metrics, table, definitions, diagnostic, extractor-information, stub-generation, or tool-specific query.

- The test is an AST dump or similar structural output test, such as `PrintAst`.

- The selected result text is inside a string literal, raw string, heredoc, text block, XML literal, or multiline literal and adding a comment changes the selected text.

- The expected location is inside documentation syntax where adding a comment changes what the query reports, such as Javadoc tags.

- The `.expected` output is nonstandard enough that mechanical conversion is risky.

- Results are in shared stubs, generated copies, vendored files, or synthetic/test-project paths where inline comments would pollute shared fixtures.

- The alert, source, or sink locations are too dense or ambiguous to make the source understandable.

- The language’s inline expectation implementation does not support the source file or comment style needed.

- The query uses a special result kind or framework behavior, such as alert-...

</details>

author: amkfbant
body:
## SP-2: 自律 `course orchestrate`（drive-only bounded driver）

SP-1 の `course → phase → hitch` DB roadmap 層の上に、**link 済み hitch を phase tree 順に駆動して phase status を機械的に advance する drive-only の bounded driver**（CLI + MCP）を追加します。foundation の第3サブプロジェクト（SP-0 rename / SP-1 roadmap 層に続く）。**migration ゼロ**。

### モデル
```
course orchestrate <id>  ── 1 pass、冪等再開
  └ phase tree を pre-order walk（top-level subtree 単位で隔離）
       └ 各 phase: linked hitch を ConvergenceService で評価 → 決定論 dispatch
            └ drivable な hitch を HitchOrchestrator で駆動（stopAtCloseReady, PR なし）
```

### 設計（user 承認 4 方向 + Fable 設計レビュー 6 修正）
- **Drive-only**: auto-spawn しない（spawn は後続増分）。
- **phase status は CAS `pending → in_progress` のみ**。close / PR / spawn は書かない（§完了=operator）。`ready-to-close` は live convergence 由来の**派生**（stored しない＝findings を隠せない）。
- **1 pass / 冪等再開**、常に `stopAtCloseReady`（PR を開かない）。
- `needs_link` は leaf 限定・報告のみ・続行（container 誤爆なし）。escalation は **top-level subtree 隔離**して他 subtree 続行。hard stop は driver 例外 / budget / not-active のみ。
- drivability は `allowedByConvergence` 再利用（MCP per-hitch gate と一本化）。budget は course 単位（`maxDrivenHitches` 3/clamp10 × `maxStepsPerHitch` 20/clamp50）。
- **course-pass lease**（`domain_locks` 再利用 `course:<id>`、drive 毎に heartbeat、busy/not-active で fail-closed refuse）。

### 何が追加されたか
| Surface | 追加 |
|---|---|
| `src/roadmap/` | `orchestrate-dispatch.ts`（純関数）/ `ready-to-close.ts` / `course-orchestrator.ts`（run+plan/lease/budget/CAS/DI）/ `course-orchestrate-runtime.ts`（CLI/MCP 共通の publisher-less factory）/ `orchestrator-types.ts`。`phase-repository.ts` に `transitionStatus` CAS、`rollup.ts` に `PhaseRollup.readyToClose`。 |
| CLI | `harness course orchestrate <id> [--max-driven-hitches][--max-steps-per-hitch][--dry-run][--json]`。`--dry-run` は read-only `plan()`（本番と faithful）。exit 0=completed / 1=user-fixable / 2=driver例外。 |
| MCP | `harness.course.orchestrate`（guarded mutation・visibility gate が drive/audit 前・clamp・idempotency・confirmation 不要・PR なし）。 |
| docs | `roadmap.md` / `cli.md` / `mcp.md` / `future-features.md` / `CLAUDE.md`。 |

### 安全境界
- **状態遷移は harness のみ・決定論**（dispatch 入力は SQL 集計 + read-only convergence、LLM 出力は根拠にしない）。phase write は CAS で operator の宣言（blocked/closed）を上書きしない。
- **PR を開かない構造保証**: runtime に publisher 非配線 + `stopAtCloseReady` の二重。万一 closeAndPr 到達でも throw→escalated の fail-closed。
- **per-hitch gate を drive 直前に再チェック**（`assertHitchCanStartMutation`）— drift した hitch は driveせず決定論記録（MCP entry 意味論に一致）。
- **lease heartbeat** で並行 pass を全 pass 期間 fail-closed に refuse（偽 escalation 防止）。
- MCP visibility は registry + handler の二層、null/other-project は drive/audit 前に deny。policy 事後 git diff 検証・confirmation 迂回なしは不変。

### レビュー
全7サブタスクを **codex exec gpt-5.5 high 実装 + codex gpt-5.5 xhigh レビュー**（各タスク P0/P1 解消）。大 Phase 最終で **Fable-5 + codex xhigh が独立に同一 P1×2 を検出**（lease heartbeat 欠落 / per-drive gate 不在）→ 修正 → **codex xhigh 再レビューで P0/P1 ゼロ**。

### テスト
`npm run typecheck` clean、フルスイート緑（SP-2 で +約46テスト）。回帰テスト: CAS が operator 宣言を尊重 / subtree 隔離 / budget 枯渇 not_driven / 冪等再開 / lease busy・not-active refuse / **LeaseLostError fail-closed abort + lock leak なし** / per-hitch gate drift で driveしない / dry-run faithfulness / MCP visibility・clamp・idempotency / createdBy lineage。

### Out of scope（`future-features.md`）
auto-spawn（`needs_link` が接合点）/ course レベル PR 自動化 `--open-prs` / phase auto-close / hitch 並列 drive / `course_orchestration_runs` durable テーブル / phase 間依存エッジ。

author: jerome-benoit
body:
## Summary

Source-aware gateway access policy for the UI server. A common prologue runs before HTTP, MCP, and WebSocket request handling and evaluates the request against `uiServer.accessPolicy` once per request.

## Configuration

`uiServer.accessPolicy` (all fields optional):

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requireTlsForNonLoopback` | boolean | `true` | Reject non-loopback plaintext requests. |
| `trustedProxies` | string[] | `[]` | IPv4/IPv6 literals of immediate reverse proxies whose forwarded headers are honored. Hostnames and CIDR ranges are rejected at config load. |
| `allowLoopbackProxy` | boolean | `false` | Honor forwarded headers when the immediate peer is loopback AND listed in `trustedProxies` (e.g. `['127.0.0.1', '::1']`). |
| `allowedHosts` | string[] | `[]` | Host header allowlist. When the listen host is loopback, all loopback aliases (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) are added implicitly; when it is a single non-loopback address, the address itself is added. Wildcard listen hosts (`''`, `0.0.0.0`, `::`) add nothing implicit and require an explicit list. Entries are validated as host literals (no path, query, or fragment). |
| `allowedOrigins` | string[] | `[]` | Origin header allowlist as origin URLs (no path/query/fragment). Empty falls back to matching the request Origin's hostname against `allowedHosts`. |

`accessPolicy` is rejected at config load when nested under `uiServer.options`.

## Behavior

- Loopback request sources are allowed in plaintext.
- Non-loopback sources require TLS termination upstream by a reverse proxy listed in `trustedProxies` that forwards `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` (or RFC 7239 `Forwarded: proto=https`).
- Forwarded headers are honored only from `trustedProxies`; only single-hop chains are accepted. Multi-entry `Forwarded` and multi-value `X-Forwarded-*` are rejected.
- `Forwarded` and the matching `X-Forwarded-*` header for the same dimension cannot both be present.
- Empty forwarded values are treated as absent.
- RFC 7239 hidden-identity forms in `for=` (`unknown`, obfuscated identifiers `_<token>`) resolve to the trusted proxy's remote address.
- Decisions are memoized per request via a `WeakMap`.
- Denied requests are accounted against the rate limiter.
- HTTP/1.1 `requestTimeout` (30 s) and `headersTimeout` (5 s) bound slow-loris exposure. HTTP/2 streams self-protect.
- Denial responses carry `Connection: close` on HTTP/1.1; HTTP/2 omits the header (RFC 7540 forbids it).

## Denial reasons

`tls-required`, `proxy-tls-required`, `host-not-allowed`, `origin-not-allowed`, `forwarded-from-untrusted-peer`, `loopback-proxy-disabled`, `duplicate-gateway-headers`, `ambiguous-forwarded-{header,client,host,protocol,parameter}`, `invalid-forwarded-client`.

## Defaults that change observable behavior

- `requireTlsForNonLoopback: true` — plaintext non-loopback configurations are rejected unless TLS is terminated upstream by a proxy listed in `trustedProxies` forwarding `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, or the field is set to `false` (only safe on private/loopback bindings).
- Wildcard listen host (`''`, `0.0.0.0`, `::`) requires an explicit `allowedHosts`. The bundled `docker/config.json` sets `"allowedHosts": ["localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1"]`.
- `trustedProxies` accepts only IP literals.
- `uiServer.options` rejects an embedded `accessPolicy` key.
- MCP transport-level error responses (404 Not Found, 400 Bad Request, 405 Method Not Allowed, 500 Internal Server Error) now carry a `${status} ${reasonPhrase}` plaintext body and a `Content-Type: text/plain` header, matching the HTTP transport. Previously these responses were emitted with no body or Content-Type.

## Validation

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` — 0 fail, 6 skipped.

author: sinabarimd
body:
## What is Chief of Staff?

[Chief of Staff](https://github.com/sinabarimd/chief-of-staff) is an open-source reference implementation of a multi-agent personal operating system: eight Claude-based domain agents coordinated by an executive notification layer, plus a fully local voice frontend that runs on a single consumer GPU. The whole voice path is local, no cloud LLM call.

Key technical details that fit this list specifically:

- Voice stack lives in 12 GiB of VRAM: WhisperLive (TensorRT Whisper small.en FP16) + Llama 3.1 8B INT4 via vLLM + Kokoro TTS, all on one consumer card. ~155 MiB free at steady state.
- ~300 ms from end-of-utterance to first audible word; sentence-streaming pipeline so TTS starts before the LLM finishes.
- Includes both wake-word models (microWakeWord TFLite for ESP32-S3 satellites, openWakeWord ONNX for a Pi/ReSpeaker), published as-is.
- Loop-prevention primitives between the agents are modeled on routing protocols (causality chain, hop counter, idempotency keys, agent-of-record).
- Reproducible token-cost methodology is in the repo for measuring your own personal-fleet workloads.

Architecture writeup: https://drsinabari.com/articles/chief-of-staff-personal-operating-system.html
License: MIT
