body:
## What
Removes the broken `On head / Off head` readout from the macOS app, CLI `info`, and Android.

## Why
The indicator was built on a synthetic test fixture (`08,07 == 0x04`) that never matched hardware. Investigation — decompiling Bose Music v13.0.7 + live probes on the QC Ultra 2 — proved:
- The real wear function is **`StatusInEar`** (block `0x02` / func `0x09`, a GET; decode `payload[0]` bit0=left, bit1=right bud).
- It's an **earbuds** feature. The over-ear headphones answer **`FuncNotSupp`** (error `0x04`) to `02,09`.
- On-head is handled **on-device** (sensor → AVRCP pause), never published over BMAP.
- `08,07` isn't the wear function at all — its byte is noise (flips 0x03/0x04 off-head).

## Changes
- Strip the indicator + `08,07` read from CLI (`Parsers/main/Tests`), macOS (`BoseManager/ContentView`), Android (`Parsers/BoseProtocol/BoseViewModel/MainActivity` + test).
- Document the verified finding in CLAUDE.md so it isn't re-added.

## Verified
CLI builds + unit tests pass + live `info` no longer shows the row; macOS app builds + signs; Android compiles + JVM unit tests pass.

author: ginderjeremiah
body:
## Summary

Fixes #408 — when a challenge completed, the unlocked item was not immediately equippable; only a page refresh revealed it.

**Root cause.** Challenge rewards are unlocked as a side effect of handling `BattleCompletedEvent` (`BattleStatisticsEventHandler` → `player.UnlockItem/Mod/Skill`), decoupled from the socket command that triggered the battle. Two problems compounded:

1. **Delayed dispatch.** `DomainEventDispatcher.DispatchAsync(aggregate)` snapshotted the event list *before* running handlers, so the unlock events a handler raised on the player weren't dispatched in that cycle — they lingered on the connection-scoped player aggregate and only flushed (persisted) on the *next* `SavePlayer`.
2. **No client notification.** The `DefeatEnemy` response carries only exp, and the client doesn't evaluate challenges itself (the server is authoritative). So the only way the client learned of an unlock was re-fetching `/api/Player` on refresh. (The frontend even had unused `addUnlockedItem`/`addUnlockedMod` stubs — a server push was the intended-but-unfinished design.)

## How it's fixed (push + event-drain)

**Backend**
- **`DomainEventDispatcher`** now drains events raised *during* handling in the same cycle (loop-until-quiescent, with a safety bound). Reward unlocks now persist immediately and are available to notify — this also closes a latent bug where an unlock could be lost if the connection dropped before the next save.
- **`Player.CompleteChallenge`** consolidates the per-challenge reward orchestration in the domain (unlock item/mod/skill) and raises a single **`ChallengeCompletedEvent`** carrying the challenge id + any reward ids.
- **`ChallengeCompletedNotifier`** — an API-layer `IDomainEventHandler` (registered in `Startup` because it depends on the socket infra) — pushes a new **`ChallengeCompleted`** socket command via `SocketManagerService.EmitSocketCommand`. Riding the Redis backplane like `SocketReplaced`, it reaches the player on whichever instance holds their connection and covers **every** completion path (idle victory, won-abandon, even a loss that completes a counting challenge), not just the explicit-victory response. The command is server-initiated only (typed response, no `Parameters` property → codegen emits no client request type).

**Frontend**
- The engine's **`handleChallengeCompleted`** marks the challenge complete in the `playerChallenges` store (live zone-gating) and unlocks each reward into the live managers (`inventoryManager.addUnlockedItem`/`addUnlockedMod`, `playerManager.addUnlockedSkill`), so a newly-unlocked item/mod is equippable and a skill selectable immediately. The TS client types were regenerated via codegen.

## Test plan

- **Backend (917 tests, all green):**
  - `Player.CompleteChallenge` unit tests (unlocks every reward kind; raises the event; no-reward case still announces).
  - `DomainEventDispatcher` drain test (events raised mid-handling dispatch in the same cycle).
  - `BattleStatisticsEventHandler` integration test asserting `ChallengeCompletedEvent` with reward ids.
  - New `ChallengeCompletedSocketTests` end-to-end: defeating an enemy that completes an item-reward challenge pushes `ChallengeCompleted` to the live socket with the reward id.
- **Frontend (1519 unit tests + lint + svelte-check, all green):** `handleChallengeCompleted`, `playerManager.addUnlockedSkill`, and `playerChallenges.markCompleted`.

## Docs
- `docs/backend.md` — the dispatcher-drain semantic and the challenge-completion server-push.
- `docs/frontend-screens.md` — the challenge screen now reflects completion/unlocks live.

Closes #408

body:
## Summary

PR 3d of the SSH epic (`plans/ssh-remote-access.md`). Makes an `ssh` hop survive a browser refresh by scoping the server-authoritative `sessions` read to the verified `player_key` **alone** — dropping the `machine_id` payload field, the own-workstation gate, and the SQL `.eq(machine_id)` filter.

ssh session rows carry the **remote** host''s `machine_id` (the coordinate-derived suffix), so the old own-workstation scoping silently dropped them on rehydrate — a refresh during an ssh hop quietly fell back to the local box. `player_key` scoping IS the boundary (you can only ever read your own sessions, wherever they hopped), so the full su + ssh chain now rebuilds on boot.

## Scope note

Most of 3d''s original plan bullets had already shipped in 3c/#218 — the failure messages (`Permission denied`, `Connection refused`, `No route to host`), the collapse of unknown-user/bad-password to one 401, and `exit` + `endServerSession` are all live and tested. What remained was the `listSessions` re-scoping (resequenced here from 3b) plus ssh-chain rehydrate coverage. The ssh **auth.log line** moved to PR 3e, where the remote patch read path makes it observable; `source_ip` already ships on the session row from 3c.

## Behavior changes

- `listSessions` returns the player''s active sessions **across all machines** (su elevations + ssh hops), not just the own workstation.
- An `ssh` hop now rehydrates on refresh: you stay on the remote host''s prompt and FS.
- `exit` is durable — after exit + refresh you''re back on your own box (`endServerSession` already wired).

## Changes

- `core/sessions/listSessions.ts` — schema drops `machine_id`; own-workstation gate removed; query takes `{ player_key }` only.
- `api/sessions.ts` — SQL drops the `.eq(''machine_id'')` filter.
- `adapters/sessionsApi.ts` — `listServerSessions` sends no machine filter.
- Tests: rewritten `listSessions` contract (cross-machine rows; forged-key/tampered/500 kept), a new **cross-action envelope rejection** test (the action literal binds a signature to one intent — a gap opened by removing `machine_id` from the schema), an adapter wire-shape assertion (no `machine_id`, explicit `Content-Type`), and two ssh-chain `rehydrateSessionStack` tests landing in the remote home.

## Test evidence

- ✅ 1072/1072 unit/integration tests passing
- ✅ Lint + build clean
- ✅ Mutation (changed files): 122/125 killed, **97.6%**; the 3 survivors are documented `try/catch`-normalized equivalents in the adapter (optional-chaining / garbage-row mutants whose outcome collapses to the same `network_error` / `[]` fallback — matches the established type-narrowing-equivalent rule).

## TDD evidence

RED → GREEN → MUTATE → KILL: `9241d95` (feature + tests in one squash-targeted commit; cycle followed per session). Plan re-scope `13d2e6b`; version bump `aae1881`.

## Live verification (real UI, agent-browser)

Full loop: crack `VANDELAY-INDUSTRIES` → nmcli connect (online) → `ssh root@<host>` → masked password → `root@iphone-139:/root#` with the **remote** `/etc/passwd` → **refresh → still on the remote host**, remote tree still reads → `exit` → back to `alice@skylab` → **refresh again → stays on own box** (exit durable). Wrong password → `Permission denied (password).`, no session.

### Pre-existing gap surfaced (not in scope)

`generateHomeLan` can place an NPC host at the same IP the player is DHCP-assigned — on the test network the only sshd host (.139) collided with the player''s own address. author: ryanrdetzel
body:
## Summary
This PR improves the security posture of the containerized applications by running Node.js services as an unprivileged user and updates the nginx static site server to use the unprivileged nginx image with port 8080.

## Key Changes
- **Static site (nginx)**: 
  - Switched from `nginx:alpine` to `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:alpine` for improved security
  - Updated exposed port from 80 to 8080 (standard port for unprivileged nginx)
  - Updated deploymill.json configuration to reflect the new port

- **Node.js services** (mcp-node, node, worker-node):
  - Added `USER node` directive to run containers as the unprivileged `node` user instead of root
  - Applied consistently across all three Node.js-based services

## Implementation Details
These changes follow the principle of least privilege by ensuring containers run with minimal required permissions. The unprivileged nginx image and explicit user directives prevent potential security vulnerabilities from container escapes or compromised applications. The port change from 80 to 8080 is a requirement of the unprivileged nginx image, which cannot bind to ports below 1024.
